data.author: valyala
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者的内部观测平台如何从19 PiB增长到超过100 PB，处理近500万亿行数据，并成功应对了20倍事件量增长，同时CPU使用率减少到原来的10%以下。尽管OpenTelemetry（OTel）在初期有效，但随着数据规模和复杂性的增加，OTel成为瓶颈。为此，作者开发了自定义管道（SysEx），以更好地满足高性能需求，并引入了基于ClickHouse的HyperDX，提供更高效的观测体验。最终，作者转向ClickStack，这是一个围绕ClickHouse构建的端到端观测堆栈，旨在提升数据探索和根因分析的效率。文章总结了在大规模数据场景下，OTel的局限性和自定义解决方案的必要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： observability（可观察性）工具与技术，特别是在有状态用例中的应用和数据处理方法

不同观点：
• **AntonCTO** 关注如何有效追踪和诊断视频会议应用中的问题，质疑是否有比手动过滤日志和跟踪更好的方法。他提出了一个具体场景，并询问是否有更先进的工具和技术来处理这种情况。

• **b0a04gl** 认为大量存储日志数据是无效的，主张通过自动化修剪未被警报查看或长时间未查询的日志来优化存储。强调了注意力加权保留的必要性，并指出当前很多数据只是高级的数字垃圾场。

• **jurgenkesker** 指出讨论内容仅适用于从ClickHouse收集日志，对其他日志不相关。虽然喜欢ClickHouse，但认为其应用范围有限。

• **mrbluecoat** 强调了OpenTelemetry的优势，能够在服务故障状态下被动收集日志，而传统系统可能无法做到这一点，这对事故后的根本原因分析很有帮助。

• **Xcelerate** 关注数据压缩和采样问题，认为可以通过减少样本数量或改进压缩技术来优化存储。同时，质疑当前的压缩技术是否已达到极限，并提出可能存在更高效的研究方法。

• **iw7tdb2kqo9** 没有ClickHouse级别规模的经验，质疑为什么使用ClickHouse而不是将日志数据存储为JSON文件，并对在大规模数据下的查询能力表示疑问。

• **jappgar** 对“可观察性最大化”持批评态度，称之为一种富有的 cult（狂热群体）。

• **atemerev** 对比ClickHouse和Postgres，对Postgres在导入大数据量时的速度表示不满。

• **the_arun** 关注日志的保留时间，认为超过一定时间后可能只需要汇总数据，而不需要原始数据。

• **revskill** 认为行业标准多为半成品或正在开发中，导致生态系统分割。批评标准制定者采用试错方法，认为这是不合理的。

• **the_real_cher** 对ClickHouse和Dynamo的大规模数据处理技术感到好奇，询问是否主要依赖大型哈希表。

• **henning** 指出使用宽事件会增加存储成本，认为在讨论中常常忽略成本问题，只强调好处。

• **Thaxll** 认为如果服务宕机时无法获取日志，整个解决方案就没有用。

• **ofrzeta** 认为当前的日志数据创建是浪费的，主张减少数据生成量，认为很多工程成就实际上是无谓的。

• **tjungblut** 简要总结了ClickHouse的零拷贝技术，提到其对原始字节的操作而非JSON的编组和解组。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点包括：大规模日志数据的存储和管理方法，是否需要存储如此多的数据，以及当前压缩和优化技术的效率。
• 不同用户对ClickHouse的实用性和优势有不同看法，部分人认为其应用范围有限或过于复杂。
• 对OpenTelemetry等新工具在服务故障状态下的优势有一定共识，但也有人质疑其成本和必要性。
• 讨论中多次提到数据压缩和优化技术，反映出对当前技术极限的关注以及对更高效方法的期待。

Engineering
Scaling our Observability platform beyond 100 Petabytes by embracing wide events and replacing OTel
Rory Crispin
Jun 19, 2025
-
32
minutes read
TLDR
#
Observability at scale:
Our internal system grew from 19 PiB to 100 PB of uncompressed logs and from ~40 trillion to 500 trillion rows.
Efficiency breakthrough:
We absorbed a 20× surge in event volume using under 10% of the CPU previously needed.
OTel pitfalls:
The required parsing and marshalling of events in OpenTelemetry proved a bottleneck and didn’t scale - our custom pipeline addressed this.
Introducing HyperDX:
ClickHouse-native observability UI for seamless exploration, correlation, and root-cause analysis with Lucene-like syntax.
Introduction
#
About a year ago, we
shared the story of LogHouse
- our internal logging platform built to monitor ClickHouse Cloud. At the time, it managed what felt like a massive 19 PiB of data. More than just solving our observability challenges, LogHouse also saved us millions by replacing an increasingly unsustainable Datadog bill. The response to that post was overwhelming. It was clear our experience resonated with others facing similar struggles with traditional observability vendors and underscored just how critical effective data management is at scale.
A year later, LogHouse has grown beyond anything we anticipated and is now storing over 100 petabytes of uncompressed data across nearly 500 trillion rows. That kind of scale forced a series of architectural changes, new tools, and hard-earned lessons that we felt were worth sharing - not least that OpenTelemetry (OTel) isn’t always the panacea of Observability (though we still love it), and that sometimes custom pipelines are essential.
In our case, this shift enabled us to handle a 20x increase in event volume using less than 10% of the CPU for our most critical data source - a transformation with massive implications for cost and efficiency.
Other parts of our stack have also changed, not least due to the
ClickHouse acquisition of HyperDX
. Not only did this give us a first-party ClickHouse-native UI, but it also led to the
creation of ClickStack
- an opinionated, end-to-end observability stack built around ClickHouse. With HyperDX, we’ve started transitioning away from our Grafana-based custom UI, moving toward a more integrated experience for exploration, correlation, and root cause analysis.
As more teams adopt ClickHouse for observability and realize just how much they can store and query affordably, we hope these insights prove as useful as our first post. If you’re curious about this journey, when and where OTel is appropriate, and how we scaled a log pipeline to 100PB…read on.
Get started today
Interested in seeing how ClickHouse works on your data? Get started with ClickHouse Cloud in minutes and receive $300 in free credits.
Sign up
Beyond general purpose: evolving observability at scale
#
Over the past year, our approach to observability has undergone a significant transformation. We've continued to leverage OpenTelemetry to gather general-purpose logs, but as our systems have scaled, we began to reach its limits. While OTel remains a valuable part of our toolkit, it couldn't fully deliver the performance and precision we needed for our most demanding workloads. This prompted us to develop purpose-built tools tailored to our critical systems and rethink where generic solutions truly fit. Along the way, we've broadened the range of data we collect and revamped how we present insights to engineers.
A new frontier of scale
#
When we last wrote about LogHouse, we were proud to handle 19 PiB of uncompressed data across 37 trillion rows. Today, those numbers feel like a distant memory. LogHouse now stores over 100 petabytes of uncompressed data, representing nearly 500 trillion rows.
Here's a quick look at the breakdown:
System
Uncompressed Size
Stored rows
SysEx
93.6 PB
431 Trillion
OTel
14.5 PB
16.7 Trillion
These numbers also tell a story. In our original post, 100% of our telemetry flowed through OpenTelemetry, with every log line collected via the same general-purpose pipeline. But as the scale and complexity of our data grew, so did the need for specialization.
While our total volume has grown more than 5x, the breakdown reveals a deliberate shift in strategy: today, the vast majority of our data comes from “SysEx”, a new purpose-built exporter we developed to handle high-throughput, high-fidelity system logs from ClickHouse itself. This shift marks a turning point in how we think about observability pipelines - and brings us to our first key topic.
We hope the following helps comprehend the scale at which LogHouse operates.
OpenTelemetry's efficiency challenges at extreme scale
#
Initially, we used OpenTelemetry (OTel) for all log collection. It was a great starting point and an established industry standard which allowed us to quickly establish a baseline where every pod in our Kubernetes environment shipped logs to ClickHouse.

data.title: Show HN: Luna Rail – Treating night trains as a spatial optimization problem
data.author: ant6n
data.article_summary: Luna Rail正在开发新一代昼夜火车，旨在优化空间利用、提升舒适度并兼顾经济性，提供比航空更环保的出行选择。其核心技术包括“酒店舱”和“座位舱”，前者为单人私密舱，白天可作起居室或移动办公室，夜间转换为舒适大床；后者为白天大座椅，夜间可平躺。通过物理模型和用户测试不断优化设计，测试显示多数用户认为这两种舱体比高铁二等座甚至一等座更具吸引力。技术目标是最大化车厢容量，使夜火车更具竞争力，并推动票价降低和线路扩展。Luna Rail还提供统一设计的应用程序，管理预订、信息和舱内控制等全程服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：卧铺列车的发展与挑战

不同观点：
• Freak_NL 认为，卧铺列车的发展受阻主要是因为航空业享有大量补贴，如未对航空燃油征税，以及各国政府对机场扩张的支持，导致环境成本外部化。此外，政府对铁路基础设施投资不足，以及跨国铁路公司之间的合作困难也是重要原因。同时，现代卧铺列车车厢的缺乏也是一个问题，尽管在设计上仍有改进空间。
• gregorvand 对卧铺列车的概念和执行表示赞赏，并分享了一个关于火车旅行经济学的BBC播客，以供进一步了解。
• L_226 和 rmccue 关注潜在的合作与竞争，特别是与Nox公司的市场竞争，并比较了Nightjet的Mini Cabins与此新概念的优劣。
• econ 提出模块化设计的想法，建议通过模块交换来提高列车利用率，并讨论了不同场景下的应用可能性。
• eqvinox 关注卧铺列车车厢的生产能力短缺问题，特别是ÖBB无法满足需求的情况，并询问是否计划建立自己的制造能力。
• fyrn_ 对概念表示赞赏，但指出美国在火车旅行方面的落后，并提到一个小 typo 错误。
• raybb 建议与欧盟内倡导更多夜间火车的组织合作，并表示将在其关于城市化的新闻通讯中介绍该项目。
• VoidWhisperer 对如何进入和离开上铺座位表示困惑，需要更清晰的解释。
• nylonstrung 对概念表示强烈支持，并表示期待使用。
• solardev 质疑空间优化是否是火车旅行发展的关键障碍，并讨论了不同市场中的票价与乘客密度问题，以及在美国等国家面临的更大挑战。
• MrJohz 关注家庭或团体旅客的需求，建议设计更大的隔间以增加灵活性。
• bruce511 提出为情侣设计可组合式 pod 的建议，并建议增加通风以提高舒适度。
• torwag2 强调通风的重要性，并幽默地建议增加打鼾测试以避免冲突。

补充讨论：
• 卧铺列车在不同地区的市场需求与接受度，如欧洲与美国的对比。
• 基础设施投资与跨国合作对卧铺列车发展的影响。
• 不同设计方案在实际应用中的可行性与潜在问题，如模块化设计和组合式 pod。
• 通风等细节设计对乘客体验的重要性。

The Future Of Sustainable Travel
Luna Rail is developing a new generation of night & day trains
optimizing space usage, comfort and economics all at once, providing a sustainable alternative for airline passengers and the best possible travel experience.
JOIN US
INVEST
GET NEWS
Travel with Comfort, without CO2
Night trains offer a
sustainable alternative
to aviation, at a fraction of the emissions per passenger-km.
The problem of existing night trains is lack of
comfort
, lack of
privacy
, that the trains have low
capacity
and can only
run at night
. This limits their attractiveness and economics. Our technology will solve those problems and will bring night trains into the future.
The Hotel Pod
The Hotel Pods: affordable premium
The hotel pod offers a
private single cabin
for all passengers while, significantly increasing the capacity over conventional sleeper cars.
By day, a spacious sofa creates your personal
living room
or office on the move. At night, the seat smoothly converts into a large, comfortable
bed
.
There are also variants for two or three passengers.
The Seat Pod
The Seat Pods: full privacy with high capacity
The Seat Pod offers a large, private
seat
for daytime travel that converts into a full lie-flat
bed
for the night.
Our technology achieves a high capacity, comparable to a six-passenger couchette and approaching that of conventional day coaches. But we provide more
space
, direct aisle access, and true individual
privacy
for all.
Developed in the physical world
We believe that the
user
of a product and their experience should be the central for development. You can’t test
ergonomics
or
comfort
from a rendering alone. It must be
experienced
. That’s why our process has been accompanied by continuous
user-tests

full-sized mock ups
and
rapid iterations
based on the
feedback
we get.

Guided by a Goal
Our development process is guided by a long-term, patent-pending goal: a day-and-night rail vehicle that maximizes passenger capacity. We adapted the technology for the real-world constraints of existing conventional railcars.
The approach is intended to make night trains truly competitive. We want to unlock the potential for profitable operations, lower ticket prices, and a significant expansion of the night train network.
Explore
“our approach” page
.
In the Future
We have developed and tested our approach assuming a newly developed rail vehicle. We then worked “backwards” adapting the approach towards existing rail cars.
In the short and medium term, our technology involving cabins around a central corridor can significantly improve the efficiency of night trains. In the long term, our patented approach involving cabins on all sides of a central corridor will increase capacity by another 25%.

“In the Media” page
.

Manage the entire journey with the Luna Rail app.
This includes the booking process, travel information, ticket validation, controlling the cabin including unlocking doors, as well as ordering service. • fyrn_ 对概念表示赞赏，但指出美国在火车旅行方面的落后，并提到一个小 typo 错误。

data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: Claude Code宣布支持远程MCP服务器，用户可以将第三方工具和数据源集成到编码环境中，而无需管理本地服务器。通过连接MCP服务器，Claude Code能够访问如开发工具、项目管理系统和知识库等服务，并在其中执行操作。例如，与Sentry MCP服务器集成后，可以在终端中直接调试问题；与Linear MCP服务器集成后，可以获取项目和问题详情，减少切换界面的需要。远程MCP服务器由供应商维护，用户只需添加服务器URL，Claude Code支持原生OAuth以确保连接安全。该功能现已上线，用户可查看文档或MCP目录开始使用。

不同观点：
• [a_bonobo] 认为目前MCP功能主要集中在桌面应用上，询问是否有人构建像Shiny web应用那样通过后台MCP服务器回答用户问题的工具，并提到acquaint项目仍在开发中。
• [vessenes] 赞扬MCP规范发展迅速，但指出由于缺乏版本控制、文档不全和归档不当，更新频繁（每三个月一次）让人感到困难。他希望API能有一年的稳定期。
• [joshwarwick15] 提供了一个远程MCP服务器的列表链接，方便人们连接使用。
• [schappim] 支持远程MCP的开放和访问，介绍了自己使用的WitsyAi工具，以及正在开发的“Heroku for remote MCP tools”平台Ninja，并表示愿意帮助初学者在Raspberry Pi上进行MCP开发。
• [federicotdn] 希望能在iOS应用中配置MCP服务器，并希望在claude.ai中有更多配置选项，如添加自定义HTTP头。
• [anotherpaul] 试图理解MCP作为连接API和LLM的接口，但对具体应该运行或使用什么服务感到困惑，请求简单解释。
• [kiitos] 提到MCP远程服务使用实验性的mcp-remote npm包，并质疑其专业性，引用Kyle Kingsbury的演讲表达对实验性技术的担忧。

补充讨论：
• [rane] 询问此新功能与Claude Code中现有MCP支持的区别。
• [WhitneyLand] 质疑Anthropic/OpenAI为何不开放其移动应用以支持自定义MCP服务器。
• [efitz] 建议将MCP改为支持websockets，以增加其应用潜力。
• [iddan] 分享了自己使用Xander.bot的经验，该工具利用MCP连接Claude Code和Linear，并能从Linear中获取上下文信息。
• [CharlesW] 询问哪些MCP服务器是Claude Code在编码任务中的必备之选，并提到具体有用的工具如@kazuph/mcp-fetch。
• [Aeolun] 指出尝试添加Github时遇到普遍失败的问题。
• [nvahalik] 分享了使用Claude处理Linear票据的实际经验，虽然不完美，但节省了15分钟时间。

争议焦点：
• MCP规范的快速变化和文档不全导致的实施困难。
• 远程MCP服务使用实验性技术可能带来的风险。
• 对移动应用不支持自定义MCP服务器的质疑。
• 添加Github等服务时遇到的技术问题。

总结：讨论围绕MCP的技术实现、工具选择、应用场景及其实际效果展开，参与者分享了各自的实践经验，并提出了对技术更新和文档支持的期望与质疑。

Product
Remote MCP support in Claude Code
Jun 18, 2025
●
2 min
read
Today, we’re announcing support for remote MCP servers in Claude Code. Connect your favorite tools and data sources to personalize your coding experience without needing to manage local servers.
Using Claude Code as your primary development interface
Claude Code can access both tools and resources exposed by MCP servers, giving it the ability to pull context from your third-party services—such as dev tools, project management systems, and knowledge bases—and take actions within those services.
You can integrate Claude Code with any remote MCP server, and the growing ecosystem of servers means that new capabilities are constantly coming online.
For example, by integrating Claude Code with the Sentry MCP server, you can access errors and issues from Sentry. Then, you can debug using the context of those issues without leaving your terminal.
You can also integrate Claude Code with the Linear MCP server to work with the context of your active projects.
“Linear's MCP integration brings Linear projects and issues directly into Claude Code,” shares Tom Moor, Head of Engineering at Linear. “With structured, real-time context from Linear, Claude Code can pull in issue details and project status—engineers can now stay in flow when moving between planning, writing code, and managing issues. Fewer tabs, less copy-paste. Better software, faster.”
Seamless connections with minimal maintenance
Remote MCP servers offer a lower maintenance alternative to local servers: just add the vendor’s URL to Claude Code—no manual setup required. Vendors handle updates, scaling, and availability, so you can focus on building instead of managing server infrastructure.
Claude Code also features native OAuth support for remote MCP servers, ensuring secure connections to your existing accounts. Simply authenticate to your servers once, and Claude Code handles the rest—no API keys to manage or credentials to store.
Getting started
Remote MCP server support is available now in Claude Code. View the
documentation
to get started or explore our
MCP directory
with recommended servers.

data.title: Mbake – A Makefile formatter and linter, that only took 50 years
data.author: rainmans
data.article_summary: **mbake** 是一个用于格式化和检查 Makefile 的工具。它提供可配置的格式规则、CI/CD 集成、扩展插件架构、丰富的终端输出和语法验证等功能。主要功能包括规范缩进与间距、处理换行符、智能合并连续行、自动插入和增强 `.PHONY` 声明等。安装可通过 PyPI 或 VSCode 插件完成，使用简单的命令行接口进行格式化和验证操作。支持自定义配置文件，并提供多种选项用于控制格式化和验证行为，如备份文件、显示差异、验证语法等。此外，还支持版本管理和 shell 命令补全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Make工具及其使用、Python语言的优劣、以及特定技术实现细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• [pjmlp] 认为这种工具早在1990年代就已经存在，并提到在《C/C++ Users Journal》和《Dr. Dobbs》杂志上看到过相关广告。这表明该工具的概念并不新颖。
• [kiitos] 和 [1oooqooq] 反对将 .PHONY 目标合并，认为 .PHONY 声明应紧邻其目标，以保持代码的可读性和结构清晰。
• [rednafi] 对使用Python开发工具持支持态度，尽管承认Python在性能和依赖管理上存在问题。他强调Python的社区和生态优势，并预测未来会有更多工具用Python编写。
• [jtwaleson] 建议将该工具打包为 pre-commit.com 的钩子，以便在代码提交前进行自动化检查。
• [b0a04gl] 担心工具机械地重写Makefile会丢失人为语义，提出格式化工具是否应保留人类上下文的讨论。
• [jbverschoor] 认为Makefile被滥用作任务运行器，偏离了其原本用于文件依赖管理的核心功能，主张使用更合适的工具来处理任务运行。

补充讨论：
• [AdieuToLogic] 分享了一次在开源会议上看到有人将make用作SAT求解器的经历，尽管这与当前项目无关，但引发了对make工具多样化应用的思考。
• [s4i] 询问是否支持某种语法以忽略特定规则，认为需要一种“逃生舱”机制。
• [kseistrup] 提供了AUR软件包的链接，为用户提供了便捷的安装方式。
• [rurban] 提出该工具与旧的Makefile's linter和formatter（如checkmake）的区别，引导大家思考其创新点。
• [teo_zero] 希望工具支持POSIX语法，扩大了对工具兼容性的需求讨论。

争议焦点：
• 关于 .PHONY 目标是否应合并的争议，部分人认为合并会降低可读性，而工具的支持者可能认为合并能提高代码整洁度。
• 关于Python作为开发语言的选择，部分开发者如[rednafi]强调其生态优势，而如[jbverschoor]则可能隐含对Python性能和适用场景的质疑。

总体来看，讨论围绕工具的功能实现、技术细节、开发语言的选择以及特定实现方式的优劣展开，反映了开发者社区对工具实用性和设计理念的不同看法。

• [s4i] 询问是否支持某种语法以忽略特定规则，认为需要一种“逃生舱”机制。
• [kseistrup] 提供了AUR软件包的链接，为用户提供了便捷的安装方式。
• [rurban] 提出该工具与旧的Makefile's linter和formatter（如checkmake）的区别，引导大家思考其创新点。
• [teo_zero] 希望工具支持POSIX语法，扩大了对工具兼容性的需求讨论。

• 关于 .PHONY 目标是否应合并的争议，部分人认为合并会降低可读性，而工具的支持者可能认为合并能提高代码整洁度。
• 关于Python作为开发语言的选择，部分开发者如[rednafi]强调其生态优势，而如[jbverschoor]则可能隐含对Python性能和适用场景的质疑。

总体来看，讨论围绕工具的功能实现、技术细节、开发语言的选择以及特定实现方式的优劣展开，反映了开发者社区对工具实用性和设计理念的不同看法。

data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章报道了世界上最大的野生动物天桥——**沃利斯·安嫩伯格野生动物通道**的最新建设进展。该项目位于加州阿古拉山，横跨101号公路，旨在帮助包括美洲狮在内的野生动物安全穿越繁忙的公路，恢复栖息地的连通性。自2022年开工以来，桥梁的主体结构已接近完成，使用了2600万磅的混凝土。下一步将铺设6000立方码的“超级土壤”，并种植5000株本地植物，以创造适合野生动物的栖息地。该天桥预计明年完工，建成后将减少野生动物因交通事故死亡的风险，并改善区域生态健康。文章还提到，著名美洲狮P-22的经历突显了这一项目的重要性。

Three years after construction began, it’s time to dump dirt on the project. Specifically, 6,000 cubic yards of a “super” soil followed by the planting of 5,000 native flora. I’m talking about the world’s
largest wildlife crossing
, which has reached another construction milestone as the bridge nears completion.
This
prepared soil
is the beginning of the end of construction for the
Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing
, which broke ground on Earth Day in 2022. Located in Agoura Hills, California, the nearly one-acre overpass stretches over a 10-lane section of U.S. 101.
The physical bridge structure is essentially complete, having required 26 million pounds of concrete, Beth Pratt of the National Wildlife Federation (NWF) told
KCAL
. The NWF Regional Executive Director added, “We just put the soil on top, and then we start burying utility lines and extend it over the access road.”
Multiple layers of soil will be needed to create a wildlife habitat on the overpass, and the soil application alone will take several weeks. However, when the Annenberg Wildlife Crossing is done, the bridge will reconnect the bisected areas of the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area. With more than 150,000 acres, SMMNRA is the country’s largest urban national park. But the freeways have long isolated the local fauna, from butterflies and cottontails to bobcats and mountain lions.
According to the
project
, as far back as the 1980s, researchers identified the Liberty Canyon area as a choke point for wildlife. However, it wasn’t until the
National Park Service
began a decades-long study of the region’s mountain lion population that the 101 freeway was deemed “the most significant barrier to the ecological health of the region.”
More than 300,000 vehicles travel along U.S. 101 daily. That’s enough traffic to give a driver anxiety—try being a
local critter
having to dart across the road just to find dinner.
P-22
, arguably the most famous mountain lion in and outside of Hollywood, surprised everyone by crossing freeways on his own. He eventually became the poster cat for the “Save L.A. cougars” campaign. Unfortunately, he was euthanized in late 2022 after being found with severe injuries, likely due to a vehicle collision, and a myriad of other health issues.
Mountain lions are the main conservation focus of this
wildlife bridge
. The big cats are territorial, and being locked in by freeways limits their roaming range and biodiversity. Without the crossing to expand their habitat, SoCal cougars could be extinct within 50 years. They also continue to be killed by vehicles.
“In the Liberty Canyon area where we’re putting the crossing, within the last four years, we’ve had four mountain lions killed just in that general area,” Pratt said.
Not just providing access to more sources of food, shelter, and mates, but the bridge would also offer an escape route from wildfires and other disasters. The Annenberg Wildlife Crossing is expected to reach completion next year.

data.title: What is the most realistic submarine movie? (2019)
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： submarine电影的评价与推荐

不同观点：
• [fracus] 和 [ChrisMarshallNY] 认为《Office Space》虽然是喜剧，但准确描绘了潜艇工作中的繁文缛节和工程师的孤立状态。相比之下，[ChrisMarshallNY] 更喜欢《Das Boot》，并提到德国电影行业的表现出色。
• [rwmj] 认为观看《Das Boot》后还有人自愿参军是很勇敢的，暗示该电影真实呈现了潜艇生活的压力和恐惧。
• [johannes1234321] 推荐《Das Boot》的DVD版本，尤其是导演剪辑版，因为这些版本更好地展现了潜艇生活的单调和紧张感。
• [avoutos] 强调《Das Boot》的配乐通过合成器、机械声音和声纳ping声，增强了电影的封闭感和压迫感。
• [southernplaces7] 详细分析了《Das Boot》的制作细节，如演员的训练和场景的真实性，认为该电影是对潜艇生活的最真实描绘，并将其与太空旅行相比较。
• [nemosaltat] 认为高级军官的意见在此调查中占比过大，并提出《Down Periscope》更准确地捕捉了潜艇生活中的荒谬和无聊。
• [gcanyon] 表示虽然《Das Boot》是预料中的答案，但其他例外回答也值得关注。
• [zabzonk] 提到《Operation Petticoat》是一部有趣的潜艇喜剧电影。
• [jmcgough] 对《Down Periscope》被提及感到有趣，并表示自己首先想到的也是这部电影。
• [adt] 建议直接询问实际的潜艇船员，以获取更真实的电影评价。
• [Hilift] 推荐了《On the Beach (1959)》这部末日题材的潜艇电影。
• [anonymousiam] 认为《Das Boot》最真实，同时推荐了《Crimson Tide》和《The Hunt For Red October》作为更具戏剧性的选择。
• [DocTomoe] 提到了《The Fifth Missile (1986)》这部电影，认为其描绘潜艇成员因有毒油漆导致精神错乱的剧情值得关注。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：《Das Boot》是否为最真实和最具代表性的潜艇电影。虽然多数人认为其制作精良、真实感强，但也有人提出《Down Periscope》等喜剧电影更具荒谬性和趣味性。
• 不同观众对潜艇电影的偏好各异，一些人更喜欢严肃写实的作品，如《Das Boot》和《Crimson Tide》，而另一些人则偏爱喜剧或戏剧性强的作品，如《Down Periscope》和《Operation Petticoat》。
• 对配乐和电影制作细节的讨论，如《Das Boot》的配乐和《The Fifth Missile》的剧情，也成为部分观众评价电影的重要因素。

data.title: Show HN: I'm a doctor and built a responsive breathing app for anxiety and sleep
data.author: lukko
data.article_summary: Lungy是一款由医生开发的呼吸应用，通过识别和回应用户的呼吸来帮助他们感到更平静和放松。该应用已在40多个国家推广，拥有超过10万名用户，被誉为“最美的呼吸应用”。它提供独特的呼吸练习，无需网络连接，并支持个性化进度和反馈。免费版提供日常呼吸练习，而付费版Lungy Deluxe则提供全部练习、自定义和详细报告。最新版本集成了HealthKit，支持Apple Watch的健康指标。用户评价积极，认为其设计简洁美观，对睡眠和放松有帮助。隐私和数据安全也得到了保障。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一款呼吸健康应用的评论，涉及功能、技术实现、医学依据、订阅模式、翻译问题等方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• [abcd_f] 对订阅模式和灰色用户状态表示困惑，认为该应用没有服务器端费用，不应采用订阅模式。
• [spondylosaurus] 关心是否有Android版本，因为目前只能通过Apple App Store使用。
• [HumblyTossed] 质疑该应用相对于简单设置计时器和进行盒式呼吸的优点。
• [fao_] 提到其朋友曾与NHS合作开发类似应用，但因Google的技术变动而失败，对当前应用表示欣慰。
• [tetha] 认为应用可以帮助有哮喘发作风险的人，分享了自己帮助一名哮喘乘客的经历，并建议增加应对哮喘发作的功能。

补充讨论：
• [its-summertime] 质疑应用所基于的医学研究，并认为一般呼吸练习效果存疑。同时，对应用收集数据用于广告表示担忧。
• [admiralrohan] 质疑为何V2版本将应用与焦虑和压力关联，指出早期发布时未提及此点。
• [subharmonicon] 分享了自己使用激励式呼吸训练器的经历，认为让呼吸练习更具参与感是积极的。
• [ChrisCinelli] 提到了一款类似的应用，表明市场上已有类似产品。
• [bsaul] 指出应用的法语翻译质量极差，举例说明翻译错误可能导致误解。
• [hinkley] 将应用功能与过去的“生物反馈”概念进行比较，表达对现代技术应用方式的不满。
• [biglung420] 表示自己和朋友大量使用该应用，并请求增加憋气功能。
• [r0fl] 曾觉得应用有些花哨且运行不稳定，但仍赞赏其创意和用户体验。
• [amelius] 询问应用是否正在等待FDA批准，关注其医疗认证情况。

争议焦点：
• 订阅模式的合理性，特别是在没有明显服务器成本的情况下。
• 应用相对于简单呼吸练习的实际优势。
• 应用的数据使用和广告问题引发的隐私担忧。
• 法语翻译的质量问题，可能影响用户体验和理解。

这些观点展示了用户对应用的功能、技术实现、医学依据、订阅模式和翻译质量的多方面关注。

data.title: I was surprised by how simple an allocator is
data.author: gilgamesh3
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了编写内存分配器的基础知识，并以简单的分配器实现为例，特别提到了伙伴系统（Buddy System）。文章首先指出开发者希望在mimalloc中预分配内存的需求，并通过自行实现一个简单的内存分配器来解决该问题。作者解释了内存分配器的作用，包括内存的分配、重新分配和释放，并讨论了内存碎片化问题，包括内部和外部碎片化。伙伴系统作为一种简单可靠的分配技术被详细介绍，其通过递归地将内存块一分为二来满足分配请求。分配和释放内存的操作都相对直接，主要是分裂和合并内存块。最终，作者对其简单实现感到惊讶，并计划将其用于mimalloc的预分配内存功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：内存分配器的设计与使用在不同系统中的重要性及其实现难度

不同观点：
• [b0a04gl] 认为内存分配器的选择对系统性能至关重要，特别是在像Unity和嵌入式系统中，选择不当可能导致帧丢失或严重bug。不同的场景（如实时系统、基础设施）需要不同的分配策略，通用分配器无法满足所有需求。Rust中的分配抽象主要是为了处理内存生命周期和所有权问题，且如`Bumpalo`这样的分配器在特定场景下非常有用。
• [romesmoke] 指出，分配器的设计，尤其是策略和政策部分，非常复杂。尽管编写一个简单的分配器不难，但设计一个在各种情况下都能高效运行的分配器非常具有挑战性。特别是面对不确定的对象大小和生命周期时，分配器可能表现不佳。因此，通用解决方案在实践中往往不够理想。
• [wavemode] 对原文试图传达的观点（编写分配器不难）表示怀疑，认为虽然像mimalloc这样的分配器代码量不大，但这并不能充分证明编写一个好的分配器是容易的。
• [GuB-42] 认为编写一个基础的分配器不难，但编写一个好的分配器则需要丰富的实际系统知识和经验。
• [the__alchemist] 分享了在嵌入式Rust项目中不使用分配器而遭遇内存不足的问题，指出大多数流行的protobuf库和ESP都依赖分配器，而使用无分配器的方案（如Heapless）可能导致内存紧张。
• [jasonthorsness] 主张应用更多专用内存分配器，因为针对特定使用模式设计分配器可以简化内存管理，特别是在使用模式可预测的情况下。然而，在高层次语言中实现这一点非常困难。
• [AndyKelley] 提供了一个简短的线程安全分配器示例，展示了编写一个简单的分配器是可行的。
• [notepad0x90] 关注内存管理内核子系统的复杂性，特别是关于固定页面大小的使用，并提问是否存在不使用固定页面大小的简单内存管理方案。
• [userbinator] 赞同分配器可以很简单，并指出一个基础的first-fit分配器可以非常短小高效，利用空闲空间存储元数据也是一种简单有效的优化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是编写一个好的内存分配器是否困难。虽然基础分配器的实现不难，但设计一个能在各种实际场景中高效运行的分配器需要深厚的专业知识和经验。
• 另一个值得注意的点是专用分配器和通用分配器之间的对比，专用分配器在特定场景下表现更好，而通用分配器则难以应对所有情况。
• 讨论中还涉及了内存管理内核子系统的设计，特别是关于动态页面大小的可行性和复杂性。

44315968.article_content:
Table of Contents
Introduction
Memory allocators
Buddy system
Allocation
Deallocation
Introduction
Recently I was looking at an issue on
mimalloc
, a "
state-of-the-art
" memory allocator developed by Microsoft.
The issue
was quite simple, developers wanted a way to preallocate a piece of memory and use it as mimalloc's heap. Seeing that
mimalloc
does not offer this feature, I thought:
"
how hard can it be to write a memory allocator to manage a preallocated region?
".
The answer to this question is:
"
given enough time, even a monkey with a typewriter can write a memory allocator
".
The implementation is around 163 LoC and very straightforward.
Memory allocators
To write a memory allocator, we first need to understand what an allocator does. An allocator is "
a component of a programming language or runtime system that is responsible for managing the allocation and deallocation of memory during program execution
".
1
Roughly speaking, a custom allocator needs to provide a way for the developer to allocate, deallocate and reallocate memory from the operating system.
The C standard library provides
malloc/free/resize
(
C11 introduced
aligned_alloc
and C23 introduced
free_sized
and
free_aligned_sized
), then a custom allocator will need to provide the same (
or nearly
) the same interface for easy integration with already existing code.
Memory Fragmentation
One of the problems an allocator tries to solve is memory fragmentation. Memory fragmentation happens when the memory is split into small unused blocks throughout a memory chunk, making larger allocations harder because there is fewer contiguous memory available to allocate.
Since memory is allocated in chunks, sometimes the real size allocated by the allocator is bigger than the requested size, and the unused memory left is wasted. This is called
internal fragmentation
2
.
External fragmentation
"arises when free memory is separated into small blocks and is interspersed by allocated memory"
3
.
There are a lot of methods an allocator can use to minimize memory fragmentation. General purpose ones do it by creating different allocation buckets based on the allocation size. So if an allocation of 512 bytes is requested, the allocator will use a bucket for small allocations, preventing that 512 bytes are wasted in the memory when big allocations happen.
Buddy system
There are various allocation techniques, and one of the simplest and most reliable is the buddy allocation, which is the one I implemented. It is widely used in the industry, and it is the one used by the Linux kernel to handle page allocations (
albeit a modified version
).
The way it works is by dividing a contiguous memory chunk into two smaller chunks of memory, each a power of two (
hence the "buddy"
), until a small enough size is reached, and then returning this memory to the user.
Allocation
As an example, suppose the programmer requested a 16KB memory chunk, and the size of the whole memory block is 256KB. It will do:
Requested size is smaller than the chunk size, it will split the 256KB chunk into two 128KB chunk.
Requested size is smaller than the current chunk size, first 128KB chunk is split in two 64KB chunk.
Requested size is smaller than the current chunk size, first 64KB chunk is split in two 32KB chunks.
Requested size is smaller than the current chunk size, first 32KB chunk is split in two 16KB chunks.
Requested size is equals the chunk size. Return it to the user.
Here is the representation of this allocation:
And that is it, just split the memory until the requested size is
<=
than the current chunk size. The disadvantage of this technique is that it has internal fragmentation since the returned chunk can be smaller than the requested size and so the unused memory is wasted.
Deallocation
To deallocate the memory is straightforward, just mark the chunk received by the
free
function as unused and check if its buddy is also unused, if it is, just coalesce it into a bigger chunk.
Suppose the previous 16KB memory chunk allocated is being freed, it would be like this
4
:
Resize
The resize part is also simple to implement, and it stays as a exercise for the reader.
Conclusion
After spending some time reading and implementing an allocator, I was surprised by how simple an allocator is. Even general purpose allocators like
mimalloc
is only a few thousand lines of code and most of that code is (
probaly
) just dealing with multithread.
The code for my implementation can be found here:
tgmatos/imalloc
I would have loved to delve more into the internals of an allocator, the techniques general purpose allocators use and everything, but I have neither the time nor the proficiency (
yet
) to write an article about it. I will probably do it in the future, but for now my plan is to just implement a way for mimalloc to use preallocated memory.
1
Definition taken from
What’s a Memory Allocator anyway ?
2
Internal Memory Fragmentation (wikipedia)
3
External Memory Fragmentation (wikipedia)
4
Sinc

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基拉韦厄火山相关的实时视频、旅游体验、气候影响及地理特征

不同观点：
• **asix66** 提供了基拉韦厄火山的实时视频链接和美国地质调查局（USGS）的火山更新时间表，旨在提供有关火山活动的最新信息。
• **jasonthorsness** 推荐乘坐直升机游览基拉韦厄火山，强调即使火山未喷发，从空中观察冷却的熔岩流也具有价值，能够感受到熔岩流动的巨大规模。
• **jmward01** 指出火山的喷发活动具有规律性，并引用了Geology Hub对之前喷发事件的报道，暗示对火山活动有可预测性。
• **dluan** 关注火山喷发对空气质量的影响，特别是Oahu岛的VOG（火山烟雾）问题，表达了对风向变化的担忧。
• **1970-01-01** 对直播链接表示失望，认为没有值得看的内容，只有蒸汽。
• **dboreham** 以幽默的方式提到自己似乎能“终止”火山喷发，通过个人经历调侃了火山活动的不可预测性。
• **snvzz** 对火山喷发的时机提出疑问，提到“最近的轰炸”，暗示可能对火山喷发与人类活动之间的关系存在质疑。
• **Eduard** 寻求具体时间戳，以观看“超过1000英尺高的熔岩”，显示出对特定喷发场景的兴趣。
• **ganeshkrishnan** 详细描述了大岛的多样气候带和自然景观，分享了一次独特的公共汽车旅行体验，突显了大岛的自然和人文魅力。

补充讨论：
• 火山活动的实时观测与信息获取是讨论的核心，asix66和1970-01-01的观点形成对比，一个提供信息源，另一个则对信息内容不满。
• 旅游体验是另一个重要讨论点，jasonthorsness和ganeshkrishnan都分享了个人经历，但前者关注火山本身，后者强调大岛的整体自然和人文景观。
• dluan和jmward01提到了火山喷发对环境和气候的影响，前者担心空气质量，后者指出喷发规律性。

data.title: 2048 with only 64 bits of state
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 《Bitwise Challenge: 2048》是一个在终端运行的经典2048游戏实现。该项目将整个游戏板状态压缩到仅64位，允许通过一个数字分享游戏状态。若环境变量`$STATE`未设置，则游戏会生成一个随机种子，开始新的游戏；若设置了`$STATE`，则游戏状态和后续生成单元都是确定的。项目主要使用Shell语言编写，目前获得60个星标和1个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：2048游戏的64位状态实现及其技术细节

不同观点：
• [eurleif] 认为实现的亮点在于用不到200行的bash脚本完成，而不是64位状态的实现。他解释了用4位可以表示一个格子的12种可能状态（包括空格），从而总状态可以用64位表示。
• [rossant] 建议将其实现为一个C语言函数`int64 run_2048(int64 state, int input)`，将状态和输入（上下左右）作为参数，返回新的状态，认为这可以作为一个有趣的代码高尔夫练习。
• [lotyrin] 强调了将复杂状态空间映射到简单线性序列的技巧，并举例说明如何将有限字符集编码映射到数字序列中，认为这是很多人忽略的技巧。
• [bvanderveen] 赞赏了简洁的实现，但指出了一个bug：使用“角策略”时，有时左上角的格子会随机变小。
• [nneonneo] 分享了类似的技巧，其2048 AI允许格子达到32768，并使用每个半字节表示一个格子，从而将整个游戏板打包到一个寄存器中。
• [carra] 提到原版2048游戏在达到2048后仍可继续，而该实现为了实现64位状态去掉了这一选项，但仍认为这是一个聪明的实现。

补充讨论：
• [enriquto] 通过数学计算论证了在不超过2048的情况下，总状态数为11^16，约需要56位，因此64位是足够的，认为这是一个紧凑的实现。
• [Normal_gaussian] 和 [meta-level] 没有直接讨论技术细节，而是提到安装命令和自己的bash脚本，更多是表达对该实现的兴趣或对比自己的经验。
• [kinduff] 简单赞赏了代码行数和实现的聪明。
• [mark_undoio] 表达了对作者的赞赏和对其创造力的惊讶。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于实现中的潜在bug，[bvanderveen] 指出的“角策略”问题是否存在及如何修复。
• 另一个讨论点是64位状态实现的实际限制和原版游戏的差异。

data.title: We’ve had a Denisovan skull since the 1930s, only nobody knew
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 2021年研究发现，出土于中国哈尔滨的14.6万年前的头骨属于丹尼索瓦人。最初该头骨被认为属于新物种**Homo longi**（龙人），但蛋白质分析显示其与丹尼索瓦人的蛋白质序列相匹配，证实其实为丹尼索瓦人。这一发现为了解神秘的丹尼索瓦人相貌提供了重要线索。头骨在1930年代出土后被隐藏多年，直到2018年才交给科学家研究。尽管**Homo longi**的分类曾有争议，新证据表明其应归为丹尼索瓦人，解决了长久以来的谜题。丹尼索瓦人作为我们祖先的“幽灵谱系”，因缺乏完整化石而长期神秘莫测，哈尔滨头骨的发现让我们首次清晰看到了这一古人类的面貌。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于哈尔滨头骨和古人类演化的科学讨论及其相关争议

不同观点：
• AlotOfReading认为，这篇论文解决了关于多地区假说的长期争议，支持了西方科学界的共识，即现代中国人并非由本地的古人类单独演化而来。他还指出，这篇论文为丹尼索瓦人的广泛分布提供了证据，并为未来的研究开辟了新方向。

• hyruo提出了两个令人费解的事实：1. 现代中国人的基因中几乎没有丹尼索瓦人的DNA，而东南亚和太平洋原住民的丹尼索瓦人DNA占比超过5%；2. 现代中国人的尼安德特人DNA比当代欧洲人多20%。

补充讨论：
• pyman的评论似乎与主题无关，提到了在父亲阁楼发现的旧存储盘，带有"Tommy’s bookmarks"的标签，并联想到网站URL可能早已失效，但未直接讨论古人类或科学问题。

• adampwells提供了一个与"Dragon Man"头骨相关的科学文章链接，可能为讨论提供了进一步的阅读材料。

• poulpy123表达了对点击诱饵标题的不满，但没有深入讨论科学内容。

• ldjkfkdsjnv留下了一句评论"Dark truths are hidden in ancient dna"，暗示对古DNA研究可能揭示的未知真相的兴趣，但没有具体展开。

争议的焦点：主要集中在多地区假说与单一地区演化假说之间的对立，以及现代中国人基因中丹尼索瓦人和尼安德特人DNA比例异常的现象。这些争议激发了对古人类演化和迁移历史的进一步探讨。

A
146,000-year-old skull from Harbin, China,
belongs to a Denisovan, according to a recent study of proteins preserved inside the ancient bone. The paleoanthropologists who studied the Harbin skull in 2021 declared it a new (to us) species,
Homo longi
. But the Harbin skull still contains enough of its original proteins to tell a different story: A few of them matched specific proteins from Denisovan bones and teeth, as encoded in Denisovan DNA.
So
Homo longi
was a Denisovan all along, and thanks to the remarkably well-preserved skull, we finally know what the enigmatic Denisovans actually looked like.
Credit:
Ni et al. 2021
The Harbin skull (left) and the Dali skull (right).
Unmasking Dragon Man
Paleoanthropologist Qiang Ji, of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and colleagues tried to sequence ancient DNA from several samples of the Harbin skull’s bone and its one remaining tooth, but they had no luck. Proteins tend to be hardier molecules than DNA, though, and in samples from the skull’s temporal bone (the ones on the sides of the head, just behind the cheekbones), the researchers struck pay dirt.
They found fragments of a total of 95 proteins. Four of these had variations that were distinct to the Denisovan lineage, and the Harbin skull matched Denisovans on three of them. That’s enough to confidently say that the Harbin skull had belonged to a Denisovan. So for the past few years, we've had images of an almost uncannily well-preserved Denisovan skull—which is a pretty big deal, especially when you consider its complicated history.
While the world is now aware of it, until 2021, only one person had known what the skull looked like since its discovery in the 1930s. It was unearthed in Harbin, in northeast China, during the Japanese occupation of the area. Not wanting it to be seized by the occupying government, the person who found the skull immediately hid it, and he kept it hidden for most of the rest of his life.
He eventually turned it over to scientists in 2018,
who published
their analysis
in 2021
. That analysis placed the Harbin skull, along with a number of other fossils from China, in a distinct lineage within our genus,
Homo,
making them our species' closest fossil relatives. They called this alleged new species
Homo longi
, or "Dragon Man."
The decision to classify
Homo longi as
a new species was largely due to the skull's unique combination of features (which we'll discuss below). But it was a controversial decision, partly because paleoanthropologists don't entirely agree about whether we should even call
Neanderthals
a distinct species. If the line between Neanderthals and our species is that blurry, many in the field have questioned whether
Homo longi
could be considered a distinct species, when it's even closer to us than the Neanderthals.
Meanwhile, the 2021 paper also left room for debate on whether the skull might actually have belonged to a Denisovan rather than a distinct new species. Its authors acknowledge that one of the fossils they label as
Homo longi
had already been identified as a Denisovan based on its protein sequences. They also point out that the Harbin skull has rather large molars, which seem to be a common feature in Denisovans.
The paper's authors argued that their
Homo longi
should be a separate branch of the hominin lineage, more closely related to us than to Denisovans or Neanderthals. But if the Harbin skull looked so much like Denisovan fossils and so little like fossils from our species, the alleged relationship begins to look pretty dubious. In the end, the 2021 paper's authors dodged the issue by saying that "new genetic material will test the relationship of these populations to each other and to the Denisovans."
Which turned out to be exactly what happened.
A ghost lineage comes to life
Denisovans are the ghost in our family tree. For scientists, a “ghost lineage” is one that’s known mostly from genetic evidence, not fossils; like a ghost, it has a presence we can sense but no physical form we can touch. With the extremely well-preserved Harbin skull identified as a Denisovan, though, we’re finally able to look our “ghost” cousins in the face.
Paleogeneticists have recovered Denisovan DNA from tiny fragments of bone and teeth, and
even from the soil of a cave floor
. Genomics researchers have found segments of Denisovan DNA woven into the genomes of some modern humans, revealing just how close our two species once were. But the handful of Denisovan fossils paleoanthropologists have unearthed are mostly small fragments—a finger bone here, a tooth there, a jawbone someplace else—that don’t reveal much about how Denisovans lived or what they looked like.
We know they existed and that they were something slightly different from
Homo sapiens
or Neanderthals. We even know when and where they lived and a surprising amount about

data.title: Hawaii Highways
data.author: yakattak
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由Oscar Voss创建的非官方、非商业性网站，旨在为夏威夷的“道路学者”和游客提供有关夏威夷公路系统的信息。网站包括各岛屿的州际公路和州县公路的详细信息，如路线编号、名称、终点、里程等，并提供了一些历史资料和照片链接。网站还设有欧胡岛高速公路出口指南和一般信息页面，包括常见问题解答和旅游贴士。作者欢迎读者提供帮助以更新和改进网站内容，并提醒用户参考夏威夷交通部获取最新的路况信息。网站无广告，信息准确性不保证，建议在陌生地区行车前进行本地咨询。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：夏威夷的公路、网站设计及其相关体验

不同观点：
• [nrclark] 认为夏威夷作为一个群岛却拥有州际公路（interstates）具有一定的讽刺意味，同时指出夏威夷应获得与其他州相同的道路资金支持。他还提到对命名惯例或新兴特性的一些思考。

• [CobaltFire] 对夏威夷的公路表示怀旧，并指出网站的最后更新时间为2014年1月，可能对信息的时效性有所关注。

• [anArbitraryOne] 认为苹果公司可以从这个网站学到一些用户体验（UX）的教训。

• [protocolture] 认为该网站的设计是网页设计的巅峰之作。

• [dineol] 表达了对该设计的喜爱之情。

• [bob_theslob646] 对网站的创建表示钦佩，同时分享了在夏威夷大岛夜间驾驶的恐怖经历，强调了夜间驾驶的困难与危险性，特别是从Kona机场向南行驶的单车道、多弯道的路段。

补充讨论：
• [ghushn3] 通过观察网站联想到自闭症的诊断率上升问题，认为自闭症一直存在，只是过去被不同地标记和理解，并强调这是出于善意的看法。

44350978.article_content:
Hawaii Highways
An unofficial, non-commercial Internet guide to Hawaii's highways, for "roads scholars" and road users
Version 2.5, by
Oscar Voss
(based on
C.C. Slater
's original sites)
Limited updates since 2010
(See
What's new
for latest changes, including several updates since 2010, and planned major updates and other improvements)
Route lists
Aloha!
This site has lots of information on Hawaii's highway system, for "roads scholars" (a/k/a "roadgeeks"), and for tourists and others to plan their travels in the islands.
Click the dark green buttons on the left for lists of the Interstate, state, and some county highways on
the Big Island
(Hawaii island),
Maui
,
Lanai and Molokai
,
Kauai
, and
Oahu
. Go to those lists for detailed information on specific routes, including route numbers, names, termini, mileages, and sometimes historical or other information and/or links to photos and other material elsewhere on this site. Also on the left is a button for detailed guides to
Oahu Freeways
exits and interchanges, including interchange diagrams.
Click the dark blue buttons on the lower left for general information. The
site guide
discusses how this site is organized, supplementing the
site map
's quick overview of what's where on this site. The
FAQs
cover lots of Hawaii highway topics and trivia, including one page of "
Tips for Tourists
." See also my collection of
over 330 road photos covering all of Hawaii's major islands
, including in-depth coverage of some specific highways and topics, such as the
gorgeous Interstate H-3
, Maui's
curvaceous Hana Highway
, and
lava closures of highways on the Big Island
. There are also pages on
Hawaii road signs
,
Interstate route ends
, and
state and county route ends
. For the latest on state highway construction and traffic conditions, and other official information, check in also with
Hawaii DOT
.
The views expressed herein are not necessarily those of Hawaii's state or county transportation departments. However, they provided valuable
assistance (see
Credits and Sources
).
E komo mai!
(Come on in!)
Exit guides
General info
I want your kokua!
Any kokua (help) I can get from readers, to correct or update the information on this site, or to make it more informative or easier to use, would be greatly appreciated. I don't live in the islands, and don't get to visit as often as I'd like. While I try to keep up from afar with road-related news from the islands, those of you who live or travel there can help me keep this site up-to-date. Road photos, especially historical photos, to add to this site's road photos collection would also be welcome (see my "wish list" on the
overview page for the road photos collection
).
Please
e-mail me
with any corrections, updates, etc.
Mahalo nui loa!
(Thank you very much!)
See
my rant on why Hawaii should have a freeway (or at least a highway) named for the late Don Ho
.
© 1999-2010
Oscar Voss
. Material from original site © 1997-1999 C.C. Slater, used with his permission.
This site is non-profit, non-commercial, and has no advertising (if any ads pop up while viewing this site, they are coming from somewhere else).
Complete accuracy of the information on this site cannot be guaranteed. Also, this site provides only limited information on road hazards and other conditions, as explained in the
Site Guide
. For state highways, check in with
Hawaii DOT
for updates on road closures and other conditions. Also inquire locally before driving in unfamilar areas, especially on unpaved roads.
For more tropical road photos, see my
Puerto Rico road photos pages
.
My Hot Springs and Highways home page
(including roads sites for other states).

data.title: Klein Bottle Amazon Brand Hijacking (2021)
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Amazon上的品牌劫持问题及其影响

不同观点：
• CliffStoll指出，他在Amazon美国的品牌劫持问题已解决，但在Amazon加拿大仍未解决，导致他无法在加拿大销售Klein瓶。他请求帮助解决此问题。
• sytelus认为Amazon对假冒伪劣产品问题漠不关心，中国供应商通过专业手段参与其中。他还提到其他竞争对手如Walmart和B&N在解决此类问题方面也不尽如人意。
• ColinWright介绍CliffStoll的身份和成就，提到CliffStoll的TED演讲及其作品《The Cuckoo's Egg》，并分享与其相处的经历，表达对其的赞赏。
• alister补充CliffStoll的身份背景，强调其在计算机 espionage 领域的贡献，并讨论Hacker News如何处理名人身份被冒用的问题。
• BrenBarn主张拆分大型企业如Amazon，认为市场份额过大导致企业对客户需求不再敏感，主张通过反垄断法律来解决。
• ggm提到监管缺失问题，指出Amazon等大企业似乎不受监管，呼吁Sherman反托拉斯法应对此类情况。
• iaw鼓励大家购买CliffStoll的Klein瓶，称其为宝藏。
• fermigier将CliffStoll的Klein瓶与Jacques Carelman的“Catalogue d'objets introuvables”相比较，强调其艺术和设计价值。
• b00ty4breakfast认为消费者对不便的容忍和消费习惯使Amazon得以继续其不良行为，呼吁通过伤害其业务来促使改变。
• AnotherGoodName认为像StockX这样提供验证服务的网站将超越Amazon，因为消费者更愿意为信任和无麻烦的购物体验支付更多。
• godelski担心如果不是像CliffStoll这样有名的人遇到此类问题，普通卖家将更难解决。
• neuroelectron分享了自己提交问题解决票但因无日志记录而关闭的经历。
• burnt-resistor赞赏CliffStoll的努力和产品质量，将其与Etsy卖家相比较。
• ilamont引用Amazon员工在Seller Central论坛上的回复，指出Amazon解决品牌劫持问题的复杂流程，卖家需“耗尽”多种自助选项才能触发实际调查。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到Amazon在处理品牌劫持和其他问题上的不足，以及卖家在解决这些问题时面临的困难。
• 对Amazon市场主导地位及其客户信任的下降也有较多讨论，部分评论者认为这是Amazon逐渐失去竞争优势的原因。
• 评论中也涉及对监管和反垄断措施的需求，以解决大企业的不当行为。

争议焦点：
• Amazon在处理品牌劫持和假冒产品问题上的效率和态度成为争议的焦点，卖家和消费者对其解决方案和响应速度不满。

data.title: Cross-Account and Cross-Region Backups with AWS Backup (and Friends)
data.author: terussell85
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了在使用AWS Backup时遇到的一个问题：尽管AI可能声称AWS Backup支持跨账户和跨区域备份，但实际上AWS Backup并不支持同时进行跨账户和跨区域的备份。文章指出，AWS Backup可以支持跨账户复制和跨区域复制，但无法同时实现两者，特别是在处理RDS、Aurora、DocumentDB和Neptune等数据库服务时。

作者强调，为了满足数据保护和灾难恢复的需求，同时实现跨账户和跨区域备份是必要的。跨区域备份可以防止未经授权的访问，而跨账户备份则可以在区域性灾难（如火山爆发）时保护数据。

尽管AWS Backup支持集中式备份计划，但目前仍无法同时实现跨账户和跨区域的备份。作者建议了一种临时解决方案，即使用AWS Lambda脚本在完成第一次复制后触发第二次复制，并删除第一次复制。最终，作者期望AWS未来能支持同时进行跨账户和跨区域的备份，以简化实施过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS Backup的成本、功能、及其替代方案的比较

不同观点：
• [tgmatt] 认为AWS Backup非常昂贵，并建议使用AWS DataSync作为更便宜的替代方案，甚至可以通过S3复制来进一步降低成本。他指出，AWS Backup的成本远高于其他方案。
• [time0ut] 同意AWS Backup在某些方面不够成熟，特别是在应对勒索软件等用例时。他提到在现有技术栈中集成AWS Backup比较麻烦，并推荐了一家提供类似服务的公司Arpio，认为该公司服务在大多数情况下更值得使用。
• [sgarland] 对跨区域备份的必要性提出质疑，认为如果整个区域消失，那么国家可能正在遭受攻击，此时SaaS产品的生死并不重要。
• [nodesocket] 质疑AWS Backup的必要性，特别是在基础设施已经通过Terraform定义的情况下，认为RDS、EBS快照、ElastiCache、S3等服务本身已经具备备份配置选项。

补充讨论：
• 成本是主要争议点之一，[tgmatt]和[time0ut]都提到AWS Backup的成本问题，并提出了更便宜的替代方案。
• [time0ut] 提供了Arpio这家公司作为潜在解决方案，并基于实际工作经验对AWS Backup的不足进行了补充。
• [sgarland] 对跨区域备份的实用性提出根本性质疑，认为在极端情况下，备份的实际意义不大。
• [nodesocket] 从基础设施自动化角度出发，认为如果已经使用了Terraform等工具，AWS Backup的附加价值有限。

这些观点共同构成了对AWS Backup及其替代方案的多角度讨论，涵盖了成本、功能、实用性和替代方案等多个方面。

In today’s edition of “don’t trust LLMs”, we learn that despite what AI tells you, AWS Backup doesn’t support Cross-Account and Cross-Region backups. It supports Cross-Account copying and Cross-Region copying, but apparently
not together
.
As part of Masset’s Data Protection and Disaster Recovery policies, we determined that having backups separated by both region
and
OU account was a good idea. This follows fairly closely to AWS’s recommended best practice of using a separate, centralized account for an immutable history of backups and log. In the case of logging, this is a no-brainer. Most services require just a few simple tweaks to copy logs to a centralized location.
However, the story is a bit different for backups. AWS Backup’s lack of support for the combination of differing regions and account is unfortunate.  It’s a relatively new (in terms of AWS lifecycles) service offering, so I’m willing to give it a bit of leeway… But having to choose between region or account means we can only mitigate one risk at a time.
It all feels so simple; wit’s just a few lines of Terraform code. But the first time it runs you’ll get a failure notification in your #alerts Slack channel and you’ll see something akin this beautiful error hidden on the copy job for your backup.
It’s obviously not telling the
full
truth.
AWS clearly states in their documentation
that cross-region is allowed. Unfortunately, that little superscript #3 bears a lot of weight:
3. RDS, Aurora, DocumentDB, and Neptune do not support a single copy action that performs both cross-Region AND cross-account backup. You can choose one or the other. You can also use a AWS Lambda script to listen for the completion of your first copy, perform your second copy, then delete the first copy… See
Cross-Region copy considerations with specific resources
for further information.
Our risk profile demands both.
Cross-Region:
Being in a separate region doesn’t protect you if someone gets unauthorized access to your environment account. We want a WORM account for backups and logs.
Cross-Account:
Being in a separate account doesn’t protect if you’re running your application in
us-west-2
and the
Yellowstone Caldera decides to finally erupt
. Now you have data in a different account that also ceases to exist. To allow the few remaining remnants of society to pick up the pieces and restore your application to its full glory, moments before the eruption
1
, you also need your backups in a different region (preferably very far away from Wyoming).
So, what’s dev to do? Honestly, for the vast majority of organizations, having
any backup
is probably sufficient. So you might be best just to copy to a different account and call it good. Or copy it to a region in the same account. Either way, you’re probably fine according to whatever your Risk profile and matrix specifies. Talk to your compliance officer for more details.
But since ignoring the problem would make this article irrelevant, let’s continue forth as if we
really really
need this.
A Foreword on Centralized Backups Using AWS Backup
It’s important to point out that AWS Backup has expanded in recent years and
does support the idea of centralized Backup Plans managed through a delegated account in an organization
. In most cases, you should use that approach instead of defining the Backup Plan in each source account. Behind the scenes, the copy jobs all turn out to be the same, but the centralized model can lead to simpler setup if your organization is complex.
However, as of June 2025, the dual-copy (region+account) problem unfortunately still exists in either approach, distributed or centralized. If you use a centralized Backup Plan and account for your organization, source accounts still can’t copy RDS backups across region and account to the destination at the same time. This inevitably leads to defining copies of your Vault and Plan in your Backup account for each active region in your source accounts. Then you need to setup automated copies to ensure they reach another Vault in a different, isolate region. Not ideal by far.
It seems like the natural evolution of centralized plans is that AWS will eventually support cross-account and cross-region copies simultaneously. Once that’s possible, you’ll be able to define a backup plan once and have it applied universally across your entire organization. Until then, just expect there still to be a bit of nuance in implementation. In this example, we’re going to assume that both source and destination live in the same region as the principles are the same.
The First Copy
The first decision we need to make is to determine which copy do we want to do first. One can be automated with AWS Backup, the other needs to trigger based on an EventBridge event.

44333155.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了在使用AWS Backup时遇到的一个问题：尽管AI可能声称AWS Backup支持跨账户和跨区域备份，但实际上AWS Backup并不支持同时进行跨账户和跨区域的备份。文章指出，AWS Backup可以支持跨账户复制和跨区域复制，但无法同时实现两者，特别是在处理RDS、Aurora、DocumentDB和Neptune等数据库服务时。

作者强调，为了满足数据保护和灾难恢复的需求，同时实现跨账户和跨区域备份是必要的。跨区域备份可以防止未经授权的访问，而跨账户备份则可以在区域性灾难（如火山爆发）时保护数据。

尽管AWS Backup支持集中式备份计划，但目前仍无法同时实现跨账户和跨区域的备份。作者建议了一种临时解决方案，即使用AWS Lambda脚本在完成第一次复制后触发第二次复制，并删除第一次复制。最终，作者期望AWS未来能支持同时进行跨账户和跨区域的备份，以简化实施过程。

不同观点：

主要讨论点：Radio Garden网站及相关应用的功能、使用体验、技术问题以及其作为语言学习和文化探索工具的价值。

不同观点：
• **分享和推荐电台**：
  - [jen729w] 推荐日本Shonan Beach FM，并分享了自己如何通过语音助手在特定时间播放该电台，认为其背景音乐非常适合日常生活。
  - [Kozmik1] 推荐塞内加尔和几内亚比绍的电台，认为它们的音乐非常有趣，同时提到某个已消失的电台Gumbe。

• **文化探索和语言学习的工具**：
  - [BrandoElFollito] 利用Radio Garden收听不熟悉的语言，并结合Google街景和维基百科深入了解该地区文化，认为这种随机获取知识的方式非常美妙。
  - [Duanemclemore] 强调该平台对语言学习的帮助，尤其是不熟悉的语言广告也成为学习机会。

• **技术问题和功能建议**：
  - [rcarmo] 提供了其他类似网站的链接，如Radio Paradise和Radiooooo。
  - [scottmcdot] 请求添加隐藏电台的功能，以便更好地管理和试验不同电台，但未收到付费会员的回应。
  - [turbosepp] 介绍了自己开发的Radiobird，专注于标记和模块化收听体验。
  - [phrotoma] 惊讶于Radio Garden的定位准确性，未允许浏览器获取位置却能精确定位城市。
  - [pmontra] 认为该应用在使用uMatrix时较难操作，且大城市电台选择不一致，但决定通过白名单解决。

• **个人体验和评价**：
  - [geff82] 表达了对远距离收听电台的热衷，回忆童年自制天线收听远距离电波的经历，对Radio Garden表示喜爱。
  - [NoboruWataya] 遇到问题，基于英国的IP却收到“英国以外电台不可用”的提示。

补充讨论：
• **广告和沉浸体验的冲突**：
  - [Kozmik1] 提到被美国 localized ads 中断沉浸体验的问题，建议通过自定义位置信息解决。

• **其他类似资源**：
  - [dunno7456] 提到仍在运行的Shoutcast目录。
  - [redwood] 推荐tv.garden作为相关资源。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在技术实现和用户体验的细节上，如定位的准确性、电台选择的一致性以及广告对沉浸体验的影响。

data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 本文是Josh Jackson所著《The Enduring Wild: A Journey into California’s Public Lands》的节选，介绍了美国土地管理局（BLM）管理的2.45亿英亩公共土地的历史与现状。这些土地虽然为公众所有，但其历史涉及对原住民的掠夺和暴力。BLM土地曾被认为不适合开发或无利可图，导致其长期遭受过度放牧和资源开采的破坏。目前，这些公共土地面临预算削减和出售的风险。作者希望通过亲身探访，讲述这些“剩余土地”的故事，让公众更加了解和珍惜这些资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对土地历史所有权和殖民问题的不同看法

不同观点：
• [achillesheels] 认为，现代社会建立在系统性从原住民手中夺取的土地上，批评那些假装忽视通过征服和改良土地推动人类进步的说法。他强调殖民前的土地管理权属于原住民，并暗示当前的社会在忽视这一事实。

• [JKCalhoun] 则关注当前的政治背景，认为公众突然关注土地历史所有权问题与美国政府拟出售公共土地的时机有关。他质疑这种关注是否仅仅是巧合，暗示可能有政治动机在背后。

• [sQL_inject] 反对将原住民理想化为和平爱护自然的形象，指出像科曼奇族这样的原住民部落也曾通过暴力征服和掠夺扩展自己的势力范围。他引用《夏月帝国》一书，强调这些部落并没有私有财产的概念，他们的"管理"方式是通过暴力扩展领土，而非出于高尚的理念。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是原住民在殖民前对土地的管理方式以及他们是否和平。sQL_inject 通过具体历史例子指出某些部落的暴力行为，挑战普遍的和平原住民形象，而 achillesheels 则更关注殖民者对土地的系统性夺取。

• 另一个讨论点是当前社会是否在忽视土地历史的真相。achillesheels 认为存在这种忽视，而 JKCalhoun 则关注政治时机，质疑公众对土地历史所有权问题的突然关注是否与政治议程有关。

• 历史叙述的真实性也是一个潜在的讨论点。sQL_inject 强调历史叙述不应被简单化或理想化，需要考虑具体的历史事实和不同部落的多样性。

“There’s Gold in the Hills” is an adapted excerpt from the book
The Enduring Wild: A Journey into California’s Public Lands
by Josh Jackson, published by Heyday and on sale June 24, 2025.
The BLM—short for the Bureau of Land Management—was established in 1946, when the Department of the Interior merged the General Land Office with the Grazing Service. Today, the BLM is one of four federal agencies that manage public land across the United States, and it manages an astonishing 245 million acres across the western states and Alaska. I was dumbfounded by this number. Two hundred and forty-five million acres? How on earth had I never heard of these lands?
Even the idea of “public lands” wasn’t a concept I fully understood. But as I learned more about them, I came to see public lands as something miraculous. When you consider our national zeal for owning private property, it is astounding we have set aside 618 million acres of federal land for the public. These are areas of land and water that are
owned collectively by the citizens
and managed by the federal government. The concept is worth reiterating: These lands are our common ground, a gift of seismic proportions that belongs to all of us. No matter your color, creed, or class, and even if you’ve never signed your name to a deed, you are a landowner. We are all landowners. Coming to terms with this endowment was a revelation.
Buy this book on
Amazon
or
Booksho
p
Of course, there’s a deeper story behind how these lands became part of the federal domain, and it likely won’t surprise you to learn that it’s an undeniably ugly one. It didn’t take long for me to discover that these lands were systemically stolen from the hands of the Native Americans who had stewarded them for millennia before colonialism in different forms devastated their tribes. Through invasions, plagues, violence, coercion, bribery, war, and lopsided deals with the United States government, Indigenous groups and their ways of life were nearly obliterated. Behind every layer of history I peeled back was a heartbreaking story of loss.
The second distinction that sets BLM lands apart lies in how these leftover lands were perceived and treated. Once they were deemed unsuitable and/or unprofitable for homesteaders, developers, and other federal land agencies, their fate seemed inconsequential. As a result of this perceived inferiority, vast areas of those lands were then severely degraded through both overgrazing and unchecked extraction of coal, gas, oil, and various minerals. Our BLM lands, while managed by a federal agency, were not always protected by it.
BLM lands continue to face threats on all sides. A reconciliation bill currently in Congress proposes firing up to 20 percent of BLM staff and cutting $532 million from the agency’s budget by 2026—devastating blows to a workforce already stretched thin. Meanwhile, efforts to sell off our shared public lands are gaining ground. Some 540,000 acres across Nevada and Utah are on the chopping block, at risk of being handed over to the highest bidder.
Learning about such land-use imbalances and the fragility of these supposedly protected areas was a sobering wake-up call for me, and it intensified my desire to experience these lands firsthand. But despite my growing knowledge, I still struggled to find certain details about BLM land within California, including how curious visitors could access them and what we might find there. The lack of personal narratives made these lands feel distant and disconnected, as though they existed only in the dry facts of government websites. Stories have a way of breathing life into places, helping us connect on a deeper level, but in my BLM research, such accounts were either absent or merely footnotes in major narratives about the West. It was no wonder I hadn’t heard of these lands before.
If these so-called leftover lands had a story to tell, I wanted to play a small part in telling it. So, with camera in hand and notepad in pocket, I hit the road.
We were stuck.
Absolutely, white-knuckle, bare-bones stuck.
To say we were in the middle of nowhere would have been an understatement. The closest town to our west was a full day’s walk. To our east, the nearest outpost was in Nevada, a marathon and a half away. And thanks to smoke from the 2021 Tamarack Fire blowing in from the north and the August daytime heat in the mid-80s, a long walk in either direction would have been a dreaded affair.
To make matte

data.title: Dynamic YAML with Python computed properties for fusing API workflows and SQL
data.author: maxgrinev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个使用YAML和SQL创建完整API工作流的工具——Sequor。该工具允许用户利用数据库作为处理引擎，通过API拉取数据、使用SQL转换数据，并推送至任何目标平台。通过动态YAML实现快速灵活的开发，支持从简单数据同步到复杂跨应用自动化的扩展。其特点包括：使用YAML定义清晰的工作流结构，支持Jinja模板和Python表达式实现无限定制，内置数据库集成，无需自定义代码。文中还提供了Shopify到Snowflake再到Mailchimp的实际案例，展示了如何快速实现API到API的工作流，并支持多种集成模式和预制模板，帮助用户降低SaaS成本并减少工具扩散。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对YAML中使用双花括号语法以及相关技术选择的讨论，以及对工具目标和市场定位的疑问。

不同观点：
• mdaniel：认为默认使用Jinja2风格的双花括号（{{}}）在YAML中会导致很多问题，尤其是在处理引号和表达式嵌套时，会引发"leaning toothpick syndrome"（复杂转义问题）。他建议更改起止符号为${{}}以避免技术债务，并提供了具体的代码修改建议。
• vivzkestrel：对工具的目标受众、用户收益、竞争产品以及商业模式提出了几个基础问题，表现出对该工具定位和市场策略的关注。
• bz_bz_bz：质疑在主要示例中重新计算客户指标是否会浪费Snowflake资源，关注工具的实际性能和资源利用效率。
• maxgrinev：支持动态YAML的使用，认为其在API集成之外也有应用潜力，分享了他们使用Python和JavaScript原型的经验，并寻求对该方法的反馈。

补充讨论：
• seebeen：对将一种被认为设计不佳的语言（可能是指YAML或Jinja2）与不适合作为处理引擎的数据库结合使用的做法表示质疑，隐含对技术选择的批评。
• mdaniel进一步补充：通过编辑补充了更多技术细节，并提供了相关链接以支持其关于避免技术债务和减少未来变更的建议。

争议焦点：
• 使用双花括号语法在YAML中的合理性及其带来的复杂性问题。
• 工具在实际应用中的资源效率和性能表现。
• 技术选择和设计决策的适当性，包括YAML和数据库的结合使用。

data.title: Otus Lisp
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: Otus Lisp (Ol) 2.6版是一个功能性Lisp方言，实现了R7RS Scheme的扩展子集，包括一些SRFIs。它小巧（约64KB）、嵌入式、跨平台，并提供高层次接口以调用其他语言代码。Ol支持多种操作系统（如Linux、Windows、macOS、Android等）和硬件架构（x86、ARM、MIPS等），也可通过WebAssembly在浏览器中运行。它具有高效的垃圾回收机制和纯函数式语言特性，如延续、尾递归和协程。新功能包括支持传统数学符号的输入法（Infix Notation）。Ol在多个平台和浏览器上进行了测试，并提供MIT和GPLv3双重许可。用户可以在线试用Ol，无需下载安装。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Otus工具的特点及其与编程语言、平台支持相关的讨论。

不同观点：
• mark_l_watson认为Otus看起来是一个不错的工具，类似于Gambit Scheme，且其大部分用Scheme编写，内置的CFFI（C外部函数接口）看起来很好。他表示自己多年享受使用Gambit Scheme及基于Gambit的Scheme，并对Otus表示认可。

• graemep则关注Otus引用的一句被误改的Greenspun名言。他指出Otus版本的表述和原版（关于C或Fortran程序中包含Lisp方言的实现）有显著区别，暗示Otus在语言实现上可能存在不严谨或广告式的表达。

• dleslie指出Otus是R7RS（Scheme语言标准之一）的一个有自己特色的实现，并提供了一个链接，列出了Otus与R7RS标准的多处偏差。这表明Otus虽然遵循R7RS，但在具体实现上做了不少改动。

• fsmv对Otus支持的平台列表表示赞赏，但质疑为什么平台支持止步于486处理器，尤其在已经支持众多平台的情况下，认为至少应该能支持到386处理器，尽管32位可能是一个限制因素。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Otus对Lisp方言的实现是否严谨。graemep指出了引用中的不准确性，暗示可能存在误导。
• dleslie提供的链接展示了Otus与R7RS标准的具体差异，表明该工具在遵循标准的同时也有自己的独特设计选择。
• fsmv的评论引发了关于平台支持范围的讨论，特别是对老旧硬件的支持及其技术限制。

这些观点共同构成了对Otus工具的多角度评价，包括其语言实现、功能特点以及技术限制等方面。

data.title: Python can run Mojo now
data.author: cantdutchthis
data.article_summary: Chris Lattner宣布Python现在可以调用Mojo代码，这是一种简单的编译语言，能够为Python提供更快的函数。通过使用`uv`工具安装Mojo模块，开发者可以在`.mojo`文件中定义函数并从Python调用。示例展示了如何在Mojo中实现阶乘和质数计数函数，并与Python和NumPy的实现进行比较。结果显示，Mojo在某些计算任务上明显更快，例如质数计数函数比Python快约40倍。尽管目前Mojo仍处于早期阶段，存在一些粗糙之处，如大数计算时的溢出问题，但其潜力巨大，特别是在需要高性能函数的场景下。Mojo相较于Rust更易学，为Python开发者提供了强大的性能提升工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mojo编程语言的潜力和市场接受度，及其与Python、CUDA、其他编程语言（如Julia、Nim）的关系和对比。

不同观点：
• **Mojo的市场接受度不确定**：[pjmlp] 认为Mojo是否能被广泛接受仍待观察，尤其是在已经存在其他竞争者（如Julia）的情况下。提到Nvidia在Python中支持CUDA JIT DSLs，可能会影响Mojo在研究人员中的接受度。
• **Mojo的商业模式和发展方向**：[GeekyBear] 提到Chris Lattner在播客中讨论了Mojo的开源及其商业模式，包括如何盈利。
• **Mojo是否仍然是Python的超集**：[JonChesterfield] 对Mojo是否仍然是Python的超集表示疑问，并指出如果Mojo变成一种“pythonic语言”而非真正的Python超集，其价值会降低。
• **Mojo与C++的对比**：[bgwalter] 认为Mojo并不比C++容易，且Python无法直接运行Mojo代码，而是通过创建C扩展来实现。
• **编译时优化与动态生成代码的需求**：[anon-3988] 指出Mojo应该专注于编译时优化和动态生成代码，而不是仅仅作为Python的加速器。提到Numba的局限性，并认为强类型的Python可以带来更多优化机会。
• **Mojo在ML和大数据处理中的应用**：[Scene_Cast2] 关注Mojo在处理Python与编译代码之间调用开销和对象传递的效率问题，特别是在ML中的应用。
• **Mojo的资金和商业影响**：[mindwok] 对Mojo的潜力表示期待，但对其获得的大量风投资金表示担忧，担心这会影响其商业模式。

补充讨论：
• **Mojo的性能提升**：[b0a04gl] 提到Mojo在性能上的显著提升，例如在质数计数任务中表现优于纯Python，但仍存在类型限制问题。
• **Mojo与Cython的对比**：[benrutter] 和 [tgma] 都提到Mojo与Cython的对比，认为Mojo在性能和易用性上可能有优势，但并未完全说服所有人。
• **学习Mojo的障碍**：[adsharma] 认为要求人们学习新语言并迁移代码是一个很大的障碍，建议通过转译（transpile）的方式从Python迁移到Mojo。
• **其他语言的比较**：[Tiberium] 提到Nim作为另一种与Python集成的编译语言，可能也是一个选择。

争议焦点：
• **Mojo是否仍然是Python超集**：一些评论者认为Mojo已经偏离了其最初作为Python超集的定位，而另一些人则认为其与Python的紧密结合是一个重要优势。
• **Mojo与Cython及C++的易用性对比**：评论中对Mojo是否比C++或Cython更容易使用存在分歧。

44331316.article_content:
Python can run Mojo now
2025-06-17
Chris Lattner
mentioned
that Python can actually call Mojo code now. I love this idea (!) as I'm definitely in the market for a simple compiled language that can offer Python some really fast functions. So I gave it a quick spin
Setup
The setup is much simpler than I remember it, you can use
uv
for it now.
uv pip install modular --index-url https://dl.modular.com/public/nightly/python/simple/
After that you can declare a
.mojo
file that looks like this:
# mojo_module.mojo
from python import PythonObject
from python.bindings import PythonModuleBuilder
import math
from os import abort
@export
fn PyInit_mojo_module() -> PythonObject:
try:
var m = PythonModuleBuilder("mojo_module")
m.def_function[factorial]("factorial", docstring="Compute n!")
return m.finalize()
except e:
return abort[PythonObject](String("error creating Python Mojo module:", e))
fn factorial(py_obj: PythonObject) raises -> PythonObject:
# Raises an exception if `py_obj` is not convertible to a Mojo `Int`.
var n = Int(py_obj)
var result = 1
for i in range(1, n + 1):
result *= i
return result
And you can then load it from Python via:
# main.py
import max.mojo.importer
import os
import sys
import time
import math
sys.path.insert(0, "")
import mojo_module
start = time.time()
print(mojo_module.factorial(10))
end = time.time()
print(f"Time taken: {end - start} seconds for mojo")
start = time.time()
print(math.factorial(10))
end = time.time()
print(f"Time taken: {end - start} seconds for python")
This was the output:
3628800
Time taken: 3.0279159545898438e-05 seconds for mojo
3628800
Time taken: 5.0067901611328125e-06 seconds for python
This all works, but at the time of making this blogpost I was able to spot some rough edges. If I increase the factorial number to 100 then the output changes.
0
Time taken: 2.7894973754882812e-05 seconds for mojo
188267717688892609974376770249160085759540364871492425887598231508353156331613598866882932889495923133646405445930057740630161919341380597818883457558547055524326375565007131770880000000000000000000000000000000
Time taken: 9.298324584960938e-06 seconds for python
This is probably because of some overflow issues on the modular side. The docs mention that this whole stack is pretty early, and I guess this is a sign of that.
Another example
Given that the overflow is probably the issue here, I figured I'd run one extra example just to see if we could measure a speed increase. So I went with a naive prime number counting example. This is the mojo code:
from python import PythonObject
from python.bindings import PythonModuleBuilder
import math
from os import abort
@export
fn PyInit_mojo_module() -> PythonObject:
try:
var m = PythonModuleBuilder("mojo_module")
m.def_function[count_primes]("count_primes", docstring="Count primes up to n")
return m.finalize()
except e:
return abort[PythonObject](String("error creating Python Mojo module:", e))
fn count_primes(py_obj: PythonObject) raises -> PythonObject:
var n = Int(py_obj)
var count: Int = 0
for i in range(2, n + 1):
var is_prime: Bool = True
for j in range(2, i):
if i % j == 0:
is_prime = False
break
if is_prime:
count += 1
return count
This is the Python code, note that I also added a numpy implementation for comparison.
import numpy as np
import max.mojo.importer
import os
import sys
import time
import math
sys.path.insert(0, "")
import mojo_module
def count_primes(n):
count = 0
for i in range(2, n + 1):
is_prime = True
for j in range(2, i):
if i % j == 0:
is_prime = False
break
if is_prime:
count += 1
return count
def count_primes_numpy(n):
if n < 2:
return 0
candidates = np.arange(2, n + 1)
is_prime_mask = np.ones(len(candidates), dtype=bool)
# For each position in our candidates array
for idx, candidate in enumerate(candidates):
if candidate == 2:  # 2 is prime
continue
# Create divisors array [2, 3, ..., candidate-1]
divisors = np.arange(2, candidate)
# Vectorized divisibility check
has_divisor = np.any(candidate % divisors == 0)
if has_divisor:
is_prime_mask[idx] = False
return np.sum(is_prime_mask)
n = 20_000
start = time.time()
print(count_primes(n))
end = time.time()
print(f"Time taken: {end - start} seconds for python")
start = time.time()
print(count_primes_numpy(n))
end = time.time()
print(f"Time taken: {end - start} seconds for numpy")
start = time.time()
print(mojo_module.count_primes(n))
end = time.time()
print(f"Time taken: {end - start} seconds for mojo")
The results look promising!

Time taken: 0.44585609436035156 seconds for python
2262
Time taken: 0.25995898246765137 seconds for numpy
2262
Time taken: 0.011101961135864258 seconds for mojo
There are better algorithms for prime counting compared to what I am doing here, so take this with a truck of salt, but this is
very
exciting. Mojo is a lot easier to learn than Rust, but I seem to get the function speedup that I want (need).
At the time of writing the main downside is that the modular stack is still

44331316.article_summary: Chris Lattner宣布Python现在可以调用Mojo代码，这是一种简单的编译语言，能够为Python提供更快的函数。通过使用`uv`工具安装Mojo模块，开发者可以在`.mojo`文件中定义函数并从Python调用。示例展示了如何在Mojo中实现阶乘和质数计数函数，并与Python和NumPy的实现进行比较。结果显示，Mojo在某些计算任务上明显更快，例如质数计数函数比Python快约40倍。尽管目前Mojo仍处于早期阶段，存在一些粗糙之处，如大数计算时的溢出问题，但其潜力巨大，特别是在需要高性能函数的场景下。Mojo相较于Rust更易学，为Python开发者提供了强大的性能提升工具。

data.title: Adobe Project Indigo is a new photo app from former Pixel camera engineers
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: Adobe推出了一款名为Project Indigo的iPhone相机应用，由前Google团队开发，结合了计算摄影技术，旨在解决智能手机相机控制有限和过度处理的问题。该应用提供自然的效果，而非“零处理”，并包含手动控制和AI功能，如“去除反射”。Project Indigo通过轻微色调映射和组合多达32帧来提升图像质量，支持生成JPEG或RAW文件。该应用目前可免费下载，适用于iPhone 12 Pro及以上机型，Android版本将在未来推出。

44327554.article_content:
Read full article
ian carlos campbell
Contributing Reporter
Updated
Wed, Jun 18, 2025, 5:34 PM
·
2 min read
0
Adobe / Engadget
Adobe launched its own take on how smartphone cameras should work this week with
Project Indigo
, a new iPhone camera app from some of the team behind the Pixel camera. The project combines the
computational photography
techniques that engineers Marc Levoy and Florian Kainz popularized at Google, with pro controls and new AI-powered features.
In their
announcement
of the new app, Levoy and Kainz style Project Indigo as the better answer to typical smartphone camera complaints of limited controls and over-processing. Rather than using aggressive tone mapping and sharpening, Project Indigo is supposed to use "only mild tone mapping, boosting of color saturation, and sharpening." That's intentionally not the same as the
"zero-processing"
approach some third-party apps are taking. "Based on our conversations with photographers, what they really want is not zero-process but a more natural look — more like what an SLR might produce," Levoy and Kainz write.
Adobe
The new app also has fully manual controls, "and the highest image quality that computational photography can provide," whether you want a JPEG or a RAW file at the end. Project Indigo achieves that by dramatically under-exposing the shots it combines together, and relying on a larger number of shots to combine — up to 32 frames, according to Levoy and Kainz. The app also includes some of Adobe's more
experimental photo features
, like "Remove Reflections," which uses AI to eliminate reflections from photos.
ADVERTISEMENT
Advertisement
Levoy
left Google in 2020
, and
joined Adobe
a few months later to form a team with the express goal of building a "universal camera app". Based on
his LinkedIn
, Kainz joined Adobe that same year. At Google, Kainz and Levoy were often credited with popularizing the concept of computational photography, where camera apps rely more on software than hardware to produce quality smartphone photos. Google's success in that arena kicked off a camera arms race that's raised the bar everywhere, but also led to some pretty over-the-top photos. Project Indigo is a bit of a corrective, and also an interesting test whether a third-party app that might produce better photos is enough to beat the default.
Project Indigo is available to download for free now, and runs on either the iPhone 12 Pro and up, or the iPhone 14 and up. An Android version of the app is coming at some point in the future.

data.title: 2025 Alonzo Church Award: Paul Blain Levy for Call-by-Push-Value (CBPV)
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 2025年Alonzo Church奖授予Paul Blain Levy，以表彰他对效应λ演算的奠基性研究，特别是通过**Call-by-Push-Value（CBPV）**演算实现的功能性与命令式编程的结合。Levy在其2004年的著作和2006年的论文中详细阐述了CBPV，成功整合了20世纪末分化的λ演算研究路径，涵盖代数数据类型、操作语义、指称语义和方程理论等方面。CBPV成为研究计算与逻辑现象的统一框架，涉及效应、极化、项归约、类型同构和程序转换等问题。Levy的工作不仅具有重要科学贡献，还为几十年来逻辑和编程语言语义学研究提供了独特入口。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用CBPV（Call-by-Push-Value）的编程语言Forsp的理解和解释

不同观点：
• **HeliumHydride的观点**：提出Forsp是一种使用CBPV（Call-by-Push-Value）范式的编程语言，并提供了一个链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40633003），该链接可能包含有关Forsp语言的更多信息。这表明HeliumHydride对Forsp和CBPV有一定了解，并认为该链接资源对讨论有帮助。

• **ggm的观点**：对FP（函数式编程）和Lambda演算有一定了解的人请求将Forsp和CBPV的概念用更通俗易懂的语言解释。这表明ggm对当前技术性的讨论感到困惑，希望能有人将其翻译成更易理解的形式，暗示讨论中使用的术语过于专业化或复杂。

补充讨论：
• **技术术语的复杂性**：从ggm的评论中可以看出，CBPV和Forsp涉及的术语和概念可能对非专业人士或不熟悉函数式编程和Lambda演算的读者来说比较难以理解，因此需要简化解释。

• **潜在的学习资源**：HeliumHydride提供的链接可能包含有关Forsp和CBPV的进一步信息，可以作为学习这些概念的资源。然而，是否能通过该链接获取通俗易懂的解释仍需进一步验证。

• **争议焦点**：争议的焦点似乎在于如何更好地理解和解释Forsp和CBPV的概念。对于熟悉函数式编程和Lambda演算的人来说，这些概念可能比较直观，但对于不熟悉这些领域的读者来说，则需要更多的解释和简化。

44335583.article_content:
The 2025
Alonzo Church Award
for Outstanding Contributions to Logic and Computation is presented to
Paul Blain Levy
for his fundamental study of effectful λ-calculi through the Call-by-Push-Value calculus.
The awardee book and paper are:
Paul Blain Levy. Call-By-Push-Value: A Functional/Imperative Synthesis. Semantics Structures in Computation 2, Springer 2004, ISBN 1-4020-1730-8
Paul Blain Levy. Call-by-Push-Value: Decomposing call-by-value and call-by-name. High.-Order Symb. Comput. 19(4): 377-414 (2006)
The Contribution
Initiated by Alonzo Church, the research programme into the λ-calculus as an abstract model of computation has spurred volumes of fundamental research in logic and computation. By the end of the 20th century, the studies of the λ-calculus in its purely logical form and its applied effectful form bifurcated. In an outstanding contribution, Levy has reunited the many existing research streams into the study of one subsuming calculus: Call-by-Push-Value (CBPV). Levy developed and presented an extraordinarily large body of evidence spanning a cross-section of the semantic theory of the λ-calculus and its application to programming language modelling, including: algebraic datatypes, operational semantics, denotational semantics, and equational theories. To date, CBPV remains a unifying starting point in the study of computational and logical phenomena, including: effects, polarisation, term normalisation, type-isomorphisms, and program transformations. In addition to its scientific contribution, the nominated monograph is a unique access-point into the culmination of decades of logic and programming language semantics.

data.author: foxtacles
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了LEGO Island网页移植项目，该项目通过Emscripten技术让1997年经典PC游戏在现代浏览器中运行。项目基于原游戏的反编译和可移植版本，由众多贡献者花费大量时间完成，旨在让更多人体验这款经典游戏。项目仍在开发中，可能存在一些bug，支持多种语言和画质设置。此外，文章还提供了相关纪录片、游戏原声直播、wiki资源以及其他开发工具和材料的链接。需要注意的是，该项目是非官方的乐高粉丝项目，与乐高集团无隶属关系。

data.title: Kubuntu finally removes support for X11 in new installs
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: Kubuntu决定在即将发布的25.10版本中，对全新安装仅支持Wayland，放弃X11。这一变化反映了Linux开发者普遍认为Wayland是未来趋势，如Linux Mint正在改善Cinnamon对Wayland的支持。Kubuntu开发者希望提前做出改变，以避免在长期支持版26.04中引发更多问题。他们认为维护X11代码阻碍了安全性和新功能的进展，且同时支持两个显示服务器任务繁重。不过，用户仍可通过安装plasma-session-x11来恢复X11会话。并非所有Ubuntu分支都跟进，Xubuntu等预计仍将提供X11选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对从X11环境迁移到Wayland的强制性举措的态度

不同观点：
• [反对迁移观点] DaSHacka认为，从X11迁移到Wayland是“强制性”的，并批评Wayland为“半成品解决方案”。该评论者显然对现有X11环境感到满意，且认为向Wayland的迁移是不成熟和被迫的，表现出对现有工作环境被改变的不满。
   
• [支持迁移观点] 此观点未在评论中直接呈现，但可以从反对者的言论中推测出可能存在支持迁移的群体。这类用户可能认为Wayland是未来趋势，具备技术优势（如更好的性能、安全性或对现代图形硬件的支持），并希望社区能够更快地过渡到这一新环境。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Wayland是否已经成熟到足以替代X11。DaSHacka明确表示Wayland仍是一个“半成品”，暗示其功能或稳定性可能存在问题，而支持者可能认为这些问题是过渡期正常的，长期来看Wayland会更加优越。

• 另一个讨论点是用户选择的自由。反对者认为这种迁移并非用户自愿，而是被技术发展“逼迫”所致，反映出对技术决策过程中用户自主权受限的不满。

• 例子方面，DaSHacka提到“用户不愿意从现有的X11环境切换”，这表明在实际使用中，X11仍然能够满足大多数用户需求，而Wayland的必要性或优势尚未被所有用户认可。

44351347.article_content:
X11, the old window system whose days have long felt numbered, just saw another one of its major supporters head for the exit. Kubuntu has decided to follow its parent distro's lead, making its next release, version 25.10, a Wayland-only affair for fresh installs.
It seems many Linux developers see Wayland as the future. Just recently, Linux Mint
started working to improve support for the protocol in Cinnamon,
tackling lingering issues with keyboard layouts and input methods. You can
even see the progress in KDE's development
, where an upgrade to Wayland PiP is planned for KDE Plasma 6.5.
So what's the logic behind dropping a session that, for the most part, still works?
According to Kubuntu's Rik Mills
, the team wants to "rip off this sticking plaster" now, in an interim release, rather than piss off a lot of people by doing it in the next Long-Term Support version, 26.04. The developers feel that maintaining code for the aging X11 system holds back progress on security and new features that Wayland can enable more easily. Plus, supporting two separate display servers is a massive undertaking.
Of course, this change might have some people worried, but relax; all is not lost if you still need the old session. If you're running hardware that acts up, like some older NVIDIA cards, or who relies on an ancient application that doesn't play nicely with the XWayland compatibility layer, you can still get your familiar session back. Just enter the following command in your terminal:
sudo apt install plasma-session-x11
Once that command finishes, the X11 session will appear as an option on the login screen, so you can carry on as before.
As OMGUbuntu notes
, not everyone in the Ubuntu family is following its lead just yet. Other official flavors like Xubuntu, Ubuntu Budgie, and Ubuntu Cinnamon are expected to keep offering an X11 session on their default installs for this cycle.

data.title: Bluetooth Jammer
data.author: yeknoda
data.article_summary: ESP32-BlueJammer是一个基于ESP32和nRF24模块的干扰设备，能够干扰2.4GHz频段的通信，包括蓝牙、BLE、WiFi、遥控无人机等。它通过产生噪声和发送不必要的包来中断设备间的通信，适用于安全测试和受控干扰。设备有效范围超过30米，可使用更大天线或放大器增强信号。注意，干扰通信在许多地方是违法的，该项目仅用于教育目的。使用时需准备ESP32开发模块、两个nRF24L01+PA+LNA模块等硬件，并通过按键切换不同干扰模式，OLED显示当前通道，状态LED指示当前干扰类型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个潜在的干扰设备的用途、合法性及其应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• btreecat：认为该设备可能通过精确定位干扰实现有效作用，特别是在测试遥控控制链路的弹性时。他还分享了在油井平台使用LoRa技术提高连接稳定性的实际经验，并表示希望在实验室测试该设备以增强实际应用的信心。
• InTheBarn：质疑该项目的合法性，认为使用此类设备可能会导致用户面临法律问题，如罚款。
• mfkp：提出该设备可能在抵制通过蓝牙信标跟踪用户位置和购物习惯的场景中有用，但也提到简单的解决方案如不带手机和用现金支付。
• phplovesong：指出项目源代码缺失的问题。

ESP32-BlueJammer
The ESP32-BlueJammer (Bluetooth jammer, BLE jammer, WiFi jammer, RC jammer) disrupts various devices using an ESP32 and nRF24 modules, causing plenty of noise and sending unnecessary packets (DoS).
It interrupts:
The whole 2.4GHz broadband!
Everything that works on 2.4GHz is being interfered, like:
audio in speakers being transmitted over bluetooth, microphones on 2.4GHz, smartphone connections, WiFi, RC Drones (etc.), IoT devices, smart gadgets, wireless keyboard & mouse, just anything on 2.4GHz!
Ideal for controlled disruption and security testing. Based on 2,4GHz communication.
It has a big range (over 30Meters+ - may vary on your antenna and hardware setup!) on newest Bluetooth versions with casual 2.4GHz antennas, you can easily increase this aswell by taking some simple "bigger" router antennas.
An amplifier (2.4GHz) may be an good option too!
Remember that jamming is illegal and should not be used with malicious intent!

Don Anon Tech's online-shop
DIY-PCB:
"Blue ESP DIY PCB"
This PCB can fit an ESP32 DevKit and 2 RF-modules such as nRF24 or CC1101 etc., you can use it in combinations (1x nRF, 1x CC1101) to create several things.
Remember: It is not intended for illegal use, neither for my project!
For this one, all you need is listed below:
Required:

, any ESP32 should work as long as it has the needed pins, 38P required!)

Why do you need to get the nRF24's? -> the pinout can be used to connect either nRF24 or CC1101 modules for further experiments with an ESP32 chip.

= 79CH

How to use?
To disrupt various channels on the 2.4GHz band, do the following to enable your ESP32-BlueJammer:
Every mode starts right away after powering on the device! There is no additional button to start the attack!
It simply jams right away once powered!
Combo-Channel-Select_BT-BLE-WiFi-RC firmware:
use the "Boot" button on the ESP32 to switch between the channel modes on the Combo-Firmware!
the OLED will display your current operation channel
the status LED let's you know about the current state you're in:
1 blink = BT
2 blinks = BLE
3 blinks = WiFi

the serial output of your ESP32-BlueJammer will output the following lines when switching mode:
State 1: Bluetooth
State 2: Bluetooth Low Energy
State 3: WiFi
State 4: RC
all other firmware:

44350448.article_summary: ESP32-BlueJammer是一个基于ESP32和nRF24模块的干扰设备，能够干扰2.4GHz频段的通信，包括蓝牙、BLE、WiFi、遥控无人机等。它通过产生噪声和发送不必要的包来中断设备间的通信，适用于安全测试和受控干扰。设备有效范围超过30米，可使用更大天线或放大器增强信号。注意，干扰通信在许多地方是违法的，该项目仅用于教育目的。使用时需准备ESP32开发模块、两个nRF24L01+PA+LNA模块等硬件，并通过按键切换不同干扰模式，OLED显示当前通道，状态LED指示当前干扰类型。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对LeetSys平台的体验和功能反馈

不同观点：
• **隐私和服务条款问题**：
  ◦ [nelsonfigueroa] 提到平台没有提供服务条款和隐私政策链接，且必须通过Google登录。
  ◦ [captainzidgel] 也指出，虽然提到同意条款，但没有提供实际的条款链接。

• **技术问题**：
  ◦ [flare_blitz] 提到遇到“No response from Gemini”错误，且在首次使用时就被提示使用完免费面试机会，要求升级到高级版。
  ◦ [jedberg] 同样遇到了“no response from gemini”的问题，无法正常使用。

• **使用门槛**：
  ◦ [dsab] 表示由于没有Google账号，导致无法使用该平台。

• **营销和实际效果争议**：
  ◦ [nelsonfigueroa] 质疑平台宣传语中的“受工程师信任”是否属实，尤其是考虑到平台较新。
  ◦ [fermentation] 担心平台会促使招聘经理增加更多不合理的系统设计问题。

• **平台独特性**：
  ◦ [eranation] 质疑LeetSys与使用OpenAI API生成系统设计面试问题的区别，认为其缺乏独特性。

• **面试过程的争议**：
  ◦ [tayo42] 表达了对软件工程师面试过程的不满，认为这种面试越来越脱离实际工作需求，变成了一种遵循特定规则和使用特定术语的游戏。

• **平台质量质疑**：
  ◦ [low_tech_punk] 认为项目本身展示了AI系统设计可能出错的情况，暗示平台质量不高。
  ◦ [dartharva] 甚至打赌说该网站是AI生成的，质疑其质量。

补充讨论：
• [rbajp] 提供了替代方案，建议用户在遇到语音模式问题时可以切换到聊天模式。

争议焦点：
• 平台的技术问题和服务条款透明度是主要争议点。
• 面试过程是否合理和LeetSys的独特性也是讨论中的争议焦点。
