data.title: How to store Go pointers from assembly
data.author: pdziepak
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Go汇编中存储指针，同时确保与Go的垃圾回收器（GC）兼容。Go的GC通过写屏障技术实现并发垃圾收集，以避免长时间暂停。在汇编中操作指针时，需要手动通知GC以避免破坏其正确性。具体方法包括检查GC是否活跃，若活跃则调用GC写屏障函数记录指针存储，否则直接存储指针。这种方法有效减少了GC暂停时间，并防止潜在的调试故障。文章还提及了利用128位原子操作增强并发数据结构的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Go语言中使用汇编（assembly）的合理性和潜在风险]

不同观点：
• [rsc] 认为在汇编中进行如写屏障（write barriers）等操作是危险且不稳定的，因为这些细节可能会随着Go的版本更新而改变。他建议将指针操作和内存分配等任务放在Go代码中完成，仅在绝对必要的情况下（如性能优化需要特殊指令时）才使用汇编。

• [hsnice16] 并没有直接回应关于汇编的讨论，而是提到自己正在阅读一本关于Go的书，并且最近在推特上讨论了Go的垃圾回收（GC）问题，提供了相关推文的链接。这可能暗示他对Go的低层机制（如GC和汇编）有一定兴趣，但未明确表态是否支持或反对在汇编中进行操作。

• [jasonthorsness] 对Go汇编的存在表示疑惑，猜测其目的是为了在不使用CGO的情况下实现低层级操作。这表明他可能认为Go汇编的主要价值在于提供了一种不依赖CGO的低层级编程方式，尽管他也隐含了对这种设计选择的不确定性。

补充讨论：
• [rsc] 的评论中提到了Go汇编的潜在不稳定性，特别是手写写屏障的细节可能会随版本变化，这反映了对长期维护和兼容性的担忧。

• [jasonthorsness] 的猜测引出了一个技术设计上的讨论点：Go汇编是否主要是为了绕过CGO，以实现更高效或更灵活的低层级操作。这涉及对Go语言设计理念的理解和讨论。

• [hsnice16] 的推文链接可能包含了更多关于Go GC的具体讨论，但在此评论中未直接提供详细信息，只是表明其对相关话题有一定关注。

争议焦点：Go汇编的必要性和稳定性。具体表现为[rsc]对汇编中手动操作不稳定性的警告与[jasonthorsness]对其存在目的的疑惑之间的潜在争议。

How to store Go pointers from assembly
The standard Go toolchain comes with
an assembler
out of the box. Said assembler is highly idiosyncratic, using syntax inherited from Plan 9 and choosing its own names for platform-specific instructions and registers. But itâs great to have it readily available.
More mundanely, Go comes with a garbage collector. This post explains how to make these two components play nice, if we want to manipulate Go pointers from our assembly.
Preamble: Goâs GC write barriers
#
Goâs garbage collector strives to minimize long pauses, which calls for concurrent garbage collection: the garbage is picked up while your code is running. Even if youâre not a garbage collection expert you would have recognized this as a tricky problem. As the Go GC is marking reachable objects, new objects might become reachable due to code running alongside the GC.
A common technique deployed to address this problem consists of instrumenting all pointer stores to inform the GC that the destination is now being pointed to.
1
This instrumentation will augment all assignments with a bit of code informing the GC of the new reference. Or more concretely code like
x
=
y
will become more like
add_to_gc_queue
(
y
)
x
=
y
With âpointer storesâ we mean all assignments such as
x = y
where
y
contains pointers. For simplicity weâre just going to consider cases where
y
is a single pointer.
â©ï¸
Where
add_to_gc_queue(y)
makes it so that
y
will be picked up by the GC even if
x
had already been examined. The widget above is often called a âwrite barrierâ in the context of garbage collection.
2
As you can imagine this instrumentation has a cost, a cost that is particularly dear when it comes to the very common task of storing pointers in stack variables. So Go chooses to
not
instrument stores where the receiver of the store is on the stack. Instead until Go 1.8, the GC stopped the world before collection, taking care to re-scan stacks for goroutines which had run after the time they had been first examined. This ensured that no new stack references would â¦ go undetected.
Not to be confused with many other barriers used in various kinds of concurrent programming.
â©ï¸
This final stack rescanning procedure could often take uncomfortably long, and therefore Go switched to a broader write barrier, which roughly consists of adding both the old and the new reference to the GC queue:
add_to_gc_queue
(*
x
)
add_to_gc_queue
(
y
)
*
x
=
y
Above we have
x
to be a pointer to a pointer to highlight that the receiver of the pointer itself lives on the heap, rather than on the stack.
The details are fiddly
, but involving both the old and new pointer let the Go developers remove the final stack-scanning, decreasing the duration of stop-the-world pauses by two orders of magnitude.
The problem
#
When the Go compiler generates code, it automatically instruments all the relevant stores. However, fun awaits when we want to perform some pointer stores ourselves.
As a motivating example, consider a concurrent hash table storing key-value pairs together:
type
slot
struct
{
key
uint64
value
*
entry
}
We might want to leverage 128-bit atomic load/stores â which are not available directly in Go â by writing our get/put functions in assembly.
3
However we face a challenge: when writing to a
slot
from assembly, we need to inform Goâs GC of the store that just happened, or else pay the cost of rare and hard-to-debug faults, given that weâre breaking invariants central to the correctness of Goâs garbage collection.
In practice, the assembly for a store not happening on the stack
looks like this:
As a side remark, 128-bit atomics are underappreciated. They have the curious property of having become recently available on x86_64 CPUs going back more than 10 years, given that Intel and AMD
retroactively guaranteed aligned 128-bit loads and stores to be atomic on all AVX CPUs.
128-bit atomics are also available on all aarch64 CPUs supporting
FEAT_LRCPC
, introduced in ARM v8.4.
Given their usefulness (such as the example cited in this section), Iâd expect to see them gain wide adoption in concurrent data structures soon.
â©ï¸
// We're storing the pointer contained in BX into the memory
// pointed to by AX:
//
//     *AX = BX
//
// First, check if GC is currently active, i.e. if we need to
// even bother informing the GC of our store.
CMPL    runtime.writeBarrier(SB), $0
// If it is _not_ active, just jump to the store
// directly.
JEQ     doStore
// Otherwise, ask the GC to give us space for two pointers
// in the store buffer, the data structure recording stores
// happening while GC is taking place. `gcWriteBarrier2`
// returns where to store the pointers in R11.
CALL    runtime.gcWriteBarrier2(SB)
// Move the new pointer into the first location.
MOVQ    BX, (R11)
// Move the previous pointer *AX in the second location.
MOVQ    (AX), CX
MOVQ    CX, 8(R11)
doStore:
// *AX = BX
MOVQ    BX, (AX)

data.title: Backyard Coffee and Jazz in Kyoto
data.author: wyclif
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本城市中的商业和街头文化，尤其是小型酒吧、咖啡馆的进入门槛、运营模式及其文化意义，同时涉及城市规划、审美观念和法规管理等方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• **低门槛与商业繁荣**：nomilk认为日本城市中的商业运营门槛较低，允许市场在没有繁重许可和监管的情况下运作，这带来了积极的效果，比如允许独特和利基市场生存甚至繁荣。他以墨尔本的小酒吧场景与悉尼的对比为例，说明宽松的许可制度如何促进商业多样性。

• **文化体验与语言障碍**：dataviz1000分享了在小型爵士居酒屋的个人经历，强调了这些场所的独特文化氛围，如不接受小费但鼓励请酒保喝酒的习俗。他还提到在日本不会说日语可能面临的进入障碍，尽管他自己通过选择特定类型的酒吧避免了这个问题。

• **对"老旧"与"美学"的不同看法**：
   - **欣赏老旧与自然美**：anon-3988和lubujackson认为日本文化中对老旧事物和自然生长的包容是一种美学，强调了“让自然顺其自然”带来的深度和年龄感。
   - **对整洁美的不同理解**：anon-3988进一步指出，有些人更喜欢修剪整齐的草坪，而他们认为自然生长带来的不完美也是一种美，这反映了不同文化对美学的理解差异。

• **法规与商业可能性**：MarkusWandel和timr讨论了在日本即使在 marginal spaces（边缘空间）也能合法经营小型商业的可能性，这在其他国家如美国是很难实现的。timr还解释了日本租赁权和土地使用权的特殊性，使得这些小型商业能够存在。

• **都市探险与隐蔽商业**：boogieknite和frereubu分享了在京都发现的无标记酒吧和餐厅的经验，这些场所隐蔽且充满神秘感，反映了日本城市中独特的商业形态。frereubu还将这种体验与Netflix剧集《深夜食堂》联系起来，强调了这些小场所的社会和文化意义。

补充讨论：
• **音乐与文化氛围**：Dracophoenix和shermantanktop提到“爵士喫茶”（jazz kissa）作为一种独特的音乐欣赏空间，其设计目的是让顾客在安静的氛围中欣赏音乐。shermantanktop还指出，在日本城市中经典爵士乐的普及程度很高，可以在许多餐厅和咖啡店中听到。

• **审美与文化深度**：SSJPython和fitsumbelay总结了日本文化的“简约之美”和“wabi-sabi”美学，认为这种美学使得日本文化在面对经济问题和社会变化时仍能保持其独特的魅力和深度。

争议焦点：
• **对老旧和自然生长的审美分歧**：一些人欣赏日本文化中对自然生长和老旧事物的包容，认为这是一种美，而另一些人可能更喜欢整洁和人工修剪的美。这种审美差异反映了不同文化背景下的理解和偏好。

data.title: Rocknix is an immutable Linux distribution for handheld gaming devices
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: ROCKNIX是一个专注于复古游戏模拟的手持游戏设备的不可变Linux发行版。其特点包括跨设备本地和远程网络游戏、触屏支持、性能与电池寿命精细控制、音乐视频播放、蓝牙和HDMI输出支持、设备与云同步、以及VPN支持。社区通过Discord进行讨论，软件基于GNU GPLv2等开源许可证发布，品牌则采用Creative Commons非商业共享许可。该项目感谢开源社区的贡献与支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕ROCKNIX操作系统的评价、问题及对比其他类似系统（如JELOS、Bazzite、SteamOS）的讨论。

不同观点：
• freeqaz认为ROCKNIX似乎是JELOS的分支，因为其名称和JELOS相似，并询问是否有信息说明两者的区别。他也提到JELOS可能已经停止更新，所以看到ROCKNIX出现觉得很酷。
• MyPasswordSucks分享了使用ROCKNIX的实际体验，指出多个问题，包括系统从睡眠中恢复的成功率低、文件系统完整性检查时间过长且无法跳过，以及重启后数据丢失等问题。他还提到开发团队计划通过移除睡眠功能来解决睡眠问题。
• udia提到Bazzite也是Linux游戏生态系统的一个替代选项，并提供了Bazzite支持手持设备的链接。
• kadoban猜测ROCKNIX的名字是否受到Rockbox的启发，并指出两者在目的上有相似之处。
• c9fc42ad表示期待在Retroid Pocket 5上使用ROCKNIX，并提到目前在RG35XX-H上使用knulli.org的体验很好。
• haunter希望ROCKNIX支持Nintendo Switch，并提到虽然可以在Switch上使用Ubuntu或Fedora进行调整，但更希望有一个开箱即用的解决方案。
• ninetyninenine询问推荐的设备来运行ROCKNIX，表示自己有Steam Deck但想要更小、更省电的设备来运行所有复古模拟器。
• DevKoala质疑使用ROCKNIX相对于Bazzite或SteamOS加EmuDeck是否有真正的优势，并提到自己即将安装Bazzite。
• BizarroLand提到ROCKNIX可以在便宜的R36s设备上运行，并询问是否有人在此类设备上安装过，以及其性能与ArkOS的比较。

补充讨论：
• 关于ROCKNIX和JELOS关系的讨论，freeqaz认为ROCKNIX可能是JELOS的分支，但没有明确说明。
• MyPasswordSucks的实际使用体验揭示了ROCKNIX目前存在的一些技术问题，特别是与系统稳定性相关的争议。
• 多个用户（udia、c9fc42ad、haunter、ninetyninenine、DevKoala）对比了其他系统（如Bazzite、SteamOS、EmuDeck等），讨论了不同系统在设备支持和使用体验上的优劣。
• BizarroLand对ROCKNIX在廉价设备上的性能表现感兴趣，并与其他系统（如ArkOS）进行对比。

Welcome to the ROCKNIX Wiki
¶
Just Enough Linux Operating System (ROCKNIX) is an immutable Linux distribution for handheld gaming devices focused on retro gaming emulation.  It is developed by a small community of enthusiasts and our goal is to produce an operating system that has the features and capabilities we need and to have fun as we develop it.
Features
¶
Integrated cross-device local and remote network play.
In-game touch support on supported devices.
Fine grain control for battery life or performance.
Includes support for playing Music and Video.
Bluetooth audio and controller support.
Support for HDMI audio and video out, and USB audio.
Device to device and device to cloud sync with Syncthing and rclone.
VPN support with Wireguard, Tailscale, and ZeroTier.
Includes built-in support for scraping and retroachievements.

data.title: RaptorCast: Designing a Messaging Layer
data.author: wwolffrec
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了RaptorCast，一种用于Proof of Stake区块链的消息传递层解决方案，旨在解决区块提案在网络中快速、安全、可靠传播的挑战。主要关注三个方面：性能（快速传播）、安全性（验证区块来源和完整性）和鲁棒性（在存在数据包丢失和少数拜占庭节点的情况下重建区块）。

为了优化传输，选择UDP而非TCP以提高速度，并通过前向纠错（FEC）方案解决UDP的丢包问题，选用R10编码方案来处理缺失数据，同时通过符号级认证确保数据完整性。文章还讨论了数据传输协议和编码系统的选择过程，最终设计旨在平衡速度、可靠性和安全性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕网络协议和设计对性能影响的讨论

不同观点：
• [klabb3] 认为在大多数环境下，使用基于UDP的协议会比TCP更早遇到性能问题，尤其是在不同硬件和操作系统环境中。他指出，UDP在处理包交换、乱序消息和重传逻辑时更难优化，因此除非是像实时多人游戏这样对延迟敏感且能容忍一定数据丢失的场景，否则TCP更适合高吞吐量的需求。他还提到即使使用QUIC协议，情况也不会有显著改善，并表示对实际测试结果感兴趣。

• [yangl1996] 指出原文未提及相关文献中提出的"two-level broadcast"概念，并提供了一篇学术论文的链接。这暗示原文的设计可能并非全新，且有学术研究基础。此评论强调了在讨论技术设计时应参考已有文献。

• [wwolffrec] 提到Monad项目中使用了RaptorCast来实现快速可靠的块提案广播，满足高性能需求。他分享了Category Labs在设计高效消息协议时的经验，并提供了进一步阅读的链接。这表明在实际应用中，已有解决方案能够有效应对高性能网络需求。

补充讨论：
• [klabb3] 强调了在不同平台和硬件环境下，协议性能的差异，尤其是对UDP和TCP在实际应用中的表现提出了个人见解，并期待看到实际的测试结果和应用场景分析。

• [yangl1996] 提出了对原文内容未引用相关学术文献的质疑，表明在技术讨论中，参考已有研究的重要性。

• [wwolffrec] 通过实际项目经验，提供了一个具体的案例，展示了如何解决高性能网络中的消息广播问题，为讨论提供了实践依据。

争议焦点：主要集中在UDP与TCP在不同应用场景下的性能表现，以及在设计高性能网络协议时是否充分参考了已有研究和实践经验。

RaptorCast: Designing a Messaging Layer
â
In
Proof of Stake blockchains
, a pre-determined leader typically proposes a block of transactions at each round. The propagation of this block to all validators is one of the most challenging and time-consuming steps in the consensus protocol. In this blog post, we examine RaptorCast, a solution designed to address the following considerations:
Performance - a block proposal needs to be sent
quickly
to the rest of the network
Security - each recipient of the block (or its pieces) needs to be able to verify that it originated from the correct leader and arrived untampered
Robustness - honest validators need guarantees that in the presence of packet loss and a Byzantine minority they can reconstruct the block proposal
â
Background
â
How does a leader get their block proposal to other validators?
There are many strategies to tackle this challenge. The leader can naively send the proposal block to each validator
one by one
. However, this method does not scale. For instance, with 1,000 validators and a block size of 2MB, the leader would need to upload approximately
2GB of data
. Assuming zero network latency and a bandwidth of 1 Gbps, this would still take around
16 seconds
, which is clearly impractical for a performant blockchain.
In our system, we need to make a few key decisions to ensure compatibility with blockchain constraints while optimizing for speed and reliability. Specifically, we need to choose:
A
Data Transmission Protocol
â
An
Encoding System
â
A
Broadcast Strategy
Below, we describe each of these design parameters and explain our choices.
Data Transmission Protocol
When selecting a data transmission protocol for our system, we are primarily considering two options:
TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)
and
UDP (User Datagram Protocol)
. Each protocol offers unique advantages and trade-offs, and our decision should align with our performance, reliability, and security requirements.
TCP
is a connection-oriented protocol that ensures reliable data delivery. It provides features such as error checking, retransmission of lost packets, and data sequencing. This makes TCP highly suitable for environments where data integrity and reliability are criticalâespecially in scenarios involving potential packet loss or network instability. However, this reliability comes at a cost: increased latency when packets are reordered or lost, which can reduce performance in real-time or high-throughput applications.
On the other hand,
UDP
is a connectionless protocol that emphasizes speed and efficiency. It transmits data without the overhead of establishing a connection, making it ideal for applications that demand low latency and can tolerate occasional packet loss. However, we need to adjust our design to compensate for packet loss over UDP and ensure that the target number of encoding symbols is received by validators despite potential losses.
That said, UDP does not inherently provide mechanisms for authentication or packet delivery guarantees, which are
two major concerns
in our context. However, if we can address these limitations at other layers then UDP becomes a compelling choice.
So in our Proposal Block Propagation design we choose UDP over TCP to take advantage of its speed, and we try to address the packet loss and data integrity and message authentication issues with our design and encoding systems.
QUIC is another transport layer protocol that incorporates secure sessions and flow control strategies (similar to TCP) with efficiency gains. Relative to UDP, QUIC introduces additional overhead of handshakes and encryption that outweigh the benefit of better reliability guarantees.
Encoding System
Since we are choosing
UDP instead of TCP
, integrating an encoding system to handle packet loss becomes essential. By selecting UDP, we inherently accept the possibility of packet loss, so we must compensate for it efficiently. The most effective way to do this is by incorporating a
robust forward error correction (FEC) scheme
. For example, if we anticipate a
10% packet loss
, we can simply send
10% extra encoded packets
. This way, the receiver can successfully decode the source data as long as they receive a sufficient number of packetsâregardless of which specific packets arrive.
There are several well-known encoding schemes, including
LT codes
,
R10
,
RaptorQ
, and
Reed-Solomon
. Each offers distinct advantages: some, like Reed-Solomon (Reed & Solomon, 1960), are robust against
corrupted data
, while others, such as R10 and RaptorQ, are designed to handle
missing data
effectively.
For our system, we have chosen
R10
, an implementation of Raptor codes (Shokrollahi, 2006), due to its performance and scalability. However, R10 does
not inherently protect against symbol corruption
(i.e., modified data). To address this, we will incorporate
symbol-level authentication
to ensure data integrity and detect any tampering during tran

data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了全球清洁饮用水的获取问题。尽管近60亿人能够在家中方便地获得安全饮用水，但仍有20亿人无法获得，这是文章的核心数字。对于这20亿人而言，他们的水源可能需要长距离获取，且无法保证完全无污染。文章通过一个来自布隆迪的家庭实例，展示了这些人每天花费大量时间取水，且面临水源不洁导致的健康风险。取水不仅耗费时间，还影响了他们从事其他提高收入的活动或孩子的教育。全球约156万人像这个家庭一样依赖地表水生活，承受着类似的困境。文章呼吁关注这一问题，并强调了改善水源对贫困家庭的重要性。

44355985.article_content:
Home
Clean Water & Sanitation
Clean Water
In the time it would take me to write the next sentence, I could get up, walk to the kitchen, and pour myself a glass of clean water. I’ve never had to worry about whether that water would make me sick.
Almost six billion other people in the world share this reality. They have safe drinking water in their homes, ready whenever needed.
That still leaves two billion people without. That’s the most important number in this article:
two billion people who don’t have safe water to drink
.
But these large numbers can seem abstract. It’s not clear what this means in practice. If people don’t have safe water, what
are
they drinking? What does it mean for their daily lives?
Here, I want to answer these questions and bring a more human perspective that sometimes gets lost when we’re talking about millions or billions of people.
Before we get into some of the personal stories and accounts, it’s important to understand how levels of drinking water services are defined and how many people fall on each “rung” of the ladder. I’ve summarized this in the diagram below based on data from the WHO and UNICEF.
1
Download image
For someone to have “safe drinking water”, their water source needs to meet three criteria: it needs to be free from contamination, located at home, and available whenever needed. Again, this is the reality for almost six billion people.
What are the other two billion drinking? If you’d asked me in the past, I might have guessed that most people without safe drinking water were collecting water from streams or lakes. The world was binary: you either had safe piped water or were collecting it from a river. But that’s not the reality: people collecting surface water are in the minority. Only around 156 million people get their water this way. That’s
1.4% of the global population
.
The vast majority of the two billion — around three-quarters of them —
do
have access to a piped water source or protected well that is
probably
safe to drink. But it’s either not located in their home, is not always available, or there’s no guarantee it’s completely contamination-free. That usually means they must travel to get there; whether that round-trip takes less or more than 30 minutes determines whether they fall into the “basic source” or “limited source” category. This is summarized in the diagram below.
Download image
The reality for people without access to safe drinking water
We’ll now look at the realities for families in each of the categories above. To do this, I’ve relied heavily on the
Dollar Street project
, built by Anna Rosling Rönnlund at Gapminder.
2
It lets us see the realities of daily life for more than 250 families across 50 countries — from the very poorest to some of the richest.
Although families on different rungs of the “drinking water ladder” can have very different experiences, the costs of not having safe drinking water are the same. There are two main ones (which I’ll expand on later).
The first is the most obvious. Drinking contaminated water can
spread disease, make us sick, and in many cases, can be fatal
.
The second thing we think about less is
the time it takes to collect this water
. For many families, it can be tens of hours every week. That’s extremely far from my reality, where walking to the kitchen tap takes seconds.
Surface water from rivers, lakes, ponds, and canals
That’s 7% of people without safe drinking water
Meet J and D, and their six children. The couple
lives in
Burundi, and they earn around $41 per month each, which means they live in
extreme poverty
.
3
They farm on their own land, which provides most of their food. They built their three-bedroom house themselves.
They do not have safe drinking water. Instead, D and her children spend 14 hours a week — two hours a day — fetching water from a small stream nearby.
Download image
Source: Johan Eriksson for Dollar Street 2015
In the video, you can see them using a small plastic jerry can to collect the water from the river. In the next photo, one of the children is drinking from it.
There’s no guarantee that the stream water is safe to drink. It could contain chemicals, fertilizers, or pesticides washing off from farms upstream; bacteria from animal waste; or viruses and parasites from biological sources. Everyone in the family is at risk of developing diarrheal or bacterial diseases, which can be particularly damaging for people living in poverty because they are often
already malnourished
or have limited access to healthcare and medicines.
The time spent collecting the water is also a problem. Those 14 hours a week could be spent on work to increase the family’s income. For the children, it could mean the opportunity to go to school, read, play, or improve their skills in other areas. D and her kids spend another 21 hours a week collecting firewood. That’s almost a full-time job spent collecting water and wood.

data.title: Gov. Greg Abbott vetoes THC ban
data.author: DocFeind
data.article_summary: 2023年2月9日，德州州长Greg Abbott否决了一项有争议的州内THC产品禁令，并随后召集特别立法会议，要求议员严格监管这类物质。这项否决发生在最后一刻，使德州大麻产业暂时存活，同时也与副州长Dan Patrick产生矛盾，因为Patrick将THC禁令视为其优先事项之一。Abbott指出，参议院第3号法案（SB 3）面临合宪性挑战，且与联邦法律冲突，因此否决该法案。他呼吁采取类似酒精的监管方式，包括禁止向未成年人销售和推广THC产品，要求生产过程中的检测，允许地方政府禁止销售THC产品，并为执法提供额外资金。Patrick对此表示强烈反对，称Abbott的否决会让执法部门和受高浓度产品伤害的家庭感到被抛弃。Abbott的举动得到了部分退伍军人和农民的支持，他们依赖大麻产品缓解慢性疼痛并避免使用阿片类药物。

Gov.
Greg Abbott
on Sunday vetoed a contentious state ban on THC products and shortly after called a special legislative session asking lawmakers to instead strictly regulate the substance.
The late-night action just minutes before the veto deadline keeps the Texas hemp industry alive for now,
while spiking a top priority of Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick.
Senate Bill 3 would have banned consumable hemp products that contained any THC, including delta-8 and delta-9.
Abbott, who had remained quiet about the issue throughout the legislative session, rejected the measure
amid immense political pressure
from both sides of the aisle, including from conservatives activists typically supportive of Patrick’s priorities.
Soon after midnight, Abbott called lawmakers back to the Capitol for a special session beginning July 21 with consumable hemp regulation at the top of the agenda.
“Texas must enact a regulatory framework that protects public safety, aligns with federal law, has a fully funded enforcement structure and can take effect without delay,” Abbott said.
In a
statement explaining his veto
, Abbott argued that SB 3 would not have survived “valid constitutional challenges,” and that the bill’s total ban “puts federal and state law on a collision course,” noting that the 2018 federal Farm Bill legalized hemp products.
“Allowing Senate Bill 3 to become law — knowing that it faces a lengthy battle that will render it dead on arrival in court — would hinder rather than help us solve the public safety issues this bill seeks to contain,” Abbott said. “The current market is dangerously under-regulated, and children are paying the price. If Senate Bill 3 is swiftly enjoined by a court, our children will be no safer than if no law was passed, and the problems will only grow.”

Abbott urged lawmakers to consider an approach similar to the way alcohol is regulated, recommending potential rules including barring the sale and marketing of THC products to minors, requiring testing throughout the production and manufacturing process, allowing local governments to prohibit stores selling THC products and providing law enforcement with additional funding to enforce the restrictions.
Abbott’s veto
— and his push for a regulatory approach — puts him directly at odds with Patrick, the powerful head of the Senate, who had called the THC ban among his “top five” bills during his 17 years in the Legislature and threatened in February to force a special session if he did not get his way.
Patrick excoriated the veto
on social media Sunday
, saying Abbott’s “late-night veto” would leave law enforcement and families whose loved ones have been harmed by high-potency products “feeling abandoned.”
“Throughout the legislative session, @GregAbbott_TX remained totally silent on Senate Bill 3, the bill that would have banned dangerous THC products in Texas,” Patrick said. “I feel especially bad for those who testified and poured their hearts out on their tragic losses.”
Supporters of SB 3 argued that a full prohibition was necessary to protect young people from consuming products with high concentrations of THC. Patrick, in a May news conference renewing his criticism of the industry, called THC-infused products — such as gummies, beverages and vapes — a “poison in our public.”
The measure became one of Patrick’s most visible priorities this session, as he visited several cannabis stores and
filmed amateur-style investigative videos
of what he described as dangerous practices.
Abbott’s veto comes six years after the Legislature inadvertently opened the door to a surge in hemp-based products when lawmakers, meaning to boost Texas agriculture, authorized the sale of consumable hemp.
Though that 2019 law does not allow products to contain more than trace amounts of delta-9 THC, it did not establish that same threshold for other hemp derivatives. Critics say the hemp industry exploited that loophole to usher in more than 8,000 retailers selling THC-laced edibles, drinks, vapes and flower buds across Texas.
Since then, the state hemp industry has exploded, accounting for roughly 50,000 jobs and generating $8 billion in tax revenue annually,
according to one estimate
.
The hemp industry, in addition to
some military veterans
and farmers
, had pushed for stronger regulations over a ban. Veterans and other Texans managing chronic pain and other conditions
described how consumable hemp products
have helped them cope and allow them to avoid opioids.

主要讨论点：关于一款新闻摘要应用的功能、可用性及自动化需求

不同观点：
• ukuina：介绍了自己开发的免费应用HackYourNews，能够总结新闻及其评论，使用了Gemini Flash技术，强调了其跨网站的摘要功能。
• greybox：对本地运行的应用表示赞赏，但指出目前移动应用市场缺乏跨应用的AI自动化功能，并举例说明了自己在法国旅行时遇到的麻烦，即需要手动在不同应用间切换来处理图像文本和翻译。
• sunnybeetroot：质疑该应用为何不向所有地区开放。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了RedMonk编程语言排名的最新情况，由亚马逊云服务（AWS）赞助。排名通过分析GitHub和Stack Overflow的数据，追踪语言的使用和讨论趋势。文章解释了如何解读排名图表，包括如何观察语言的排名变化以及新进和退出前20名的语言。RedMonk指出，这些排名并非精确的流行度测量，而是对趋势的汇总，且现有语言因累积优势而更具竞争力。文章还提到数据来源的局限性，鼓励使用其他数据源进行分析，并回应了对CSS是否为编程语言的常见质疑。

• [ksec] 对PHP排名第4表示惊讶和质疑，隐含着对PHP的高排名感到不解，可能认为PHP不值得如此高的排名。

44355234.article_content:
This iteration of the RedMonk programming Language Rankings is brought to you by Amazon Web Services. AWS manages a variety of
developer communities
where you can join and learn more about building modern applications in your preferred language.
As part of RedMonk’s
analysis about language rankings
, here’s a visualization that tracks the movement of the top 20 languages over the history of the rankings.
More commentary about notable movement among languages can be found in the
primary analysis
, and further
notes about our data sources are available here
.
Interpreting the Chart
You can track a specific language’s ranking over time by following the horizontal progression of the language’s rank over time. You can review the Top 20 languages of any given iteration by running through the respective data points vertically from top to bottom.
Any time points are clustered, that means there was a tie and multiple languages share the rank.
If a language was previously on the chart but is no longer visible, it means the language is no longer in the RedMonk Top 20. (While they are no longer included in this specific visualization, rest assured they are still active and vibrant communities.)
Languages that break into the RedMonk Top 20 are seen as new entrants to the chart. (Just like the languages that drop off the top 20, these didn’t ascend from nowhere. They were previously rising in the ranks before becoming top 20 languages.)
Common Questions About the Rankings
Why do you create these rankings?
: These rankings attempt to correlate trends between language usage and discussion around a language. We don’t proclaim our rankings to be precise, statistically-valid measurements of popularity; instead we see them as an attempt to aggregate trends across two major developer communities.
How do you create these rankings?
: Please see the
full analysis
for a complete description of the process, but at a high level we measure traction as seen via GitHub pull requests and Stack Overflow discussion.
Why GitHub and Stack Overflow? That’s going to over-represent/under-represent certain communities.
: Agreed, these measures are imperfect. More specifically:
As previously discussed
, we are seriously reviewing the ongoing quality of these data sources in an era of AI code assistants. The volume of data available via Stack Overflow in particular is a concern.
We don’t claim these rankings are representative of broader use (i.e. we do not claim that language usage as seen on public GitHub repos is equivalent to total language usage)
Communities often connect in forums outside Stack Overflow. Unfortunately, we cannot run a separate query process for a hundred different languages across a variety of forums that range in openness of data availability.
We use GitHub and Stack Overflow first because of their historic import and second because of their public exposure of the data. We encourage interested parties to perform their own analyses using other sources.
Don’t incumbent languages have an inherent advantage here?
Indeed they do, as the metrics from GitHub and Stack Overflow are accretive. While rates of growth will be fastest for new projects with a smaller base, from a cumulative perspective new language entrants are behind from the day they are released. Displacing the most popular languages is a significant and uphill battle.
Has your process been consistent over time?
We’ve tried our best to keep things as consistent as possible, but we had to adapt to changes in data availability from GitHub in
January 2014
and again in
January 2017
. You’ll notice there is higher than typical change in those periods; the linked posts above may be helpful for those trying to sort out change due to process and change due to adoption trends.
CSS is not a language.
This is inevitably raised every iteration of this analysis. There is probably someone who wants to debate this with you in the comments somewhere on Bluesky, Reddit, Hacker News, etc. While we mostly stay out of the debate on this particular topic these days, we welcome this grand tradition.

   - **southernplaces7**：认为对核能的批评过于片面，核能技术尚未充分发展，且在一些领域（如军用反应堆、RTG）已展现出巨大潜力。不应因当前发展状态而全盘否定。
   - **coldpie**：强调核能作为无碳能源的重要性，尽管成本高昂，但通过投资可以降低成本。重建核能 expertise 是必要的，尽管需要为过去的错误买单。
   - **ecshafer**：希望在Oswego建设新反应堆，利用安大略湖的冷水资源，认为该地有足够空间。
   - **1970-01-01**：指出AI发展推动了核能，即使AI热潮过去，核电站仍能提供长期清洁能源。

• **质疑核能项目**：
   - **Workaccount2**：认为核能项目耗费巨大且成功几率低，建议投资于太阳能、风能和电池，五年内即可获得2GW的能源，成本更低。
   - **PaulHoule**：指出过去几代的核能设计存在问题，如EPR和AP1000，供应链依赖中国，建议考虑俄罗斯的VVER技术。对GE的BWRX300设计持怀疑态度。
   - **disambiguation**：引用Shoreham核电站的失败案例，指出由于公众安全担忧和三哩岛事故，该项目最终关闭，成为失败能源政策的象征。

   - **crmd**：质疑纽约电力管理局的高电价，指出其客户仅为政府机构，怀疑其管理效率。
   - **amanaplanacanal**：认为应通过竞标选择能源项目，而非由州长决定，质疑决策过程的合理性。

data.title: Minimal Boolean Formulas (2011)
data.author: mcyc
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了计算最小布尔函数公式所需的最少AND或OR操作符数量的问题。作者Russ Cox及其合作者Alex Healy在2010年确定了五个变量布尔函数所需的最小操作符数量为28。文章详细描述了计算过程，包括暴力算法和优化算法，并提到曾险些被Knuth的《The Art of Computer Programming》第四卷抢先。

对于两个变量，最难的函数是异或（XOR），需要3个操作符。对于三个变量，异或需要9个操作符；四个变量则需要15个。作者在2001年通过改编Floyd-Warshall最短路径算法，编写程序计算出这些结果。程序通过迭代更新，直到找到固定点，即不能再缩小公式大小为止。

文中还提到使用二进制真值表来表示函数，这不仅使函数编号密集，而且允许使用位操作来实现AND和OR操作，从而提高了计算效率。每个计算回合的时间复杂度为O(2^(2^(n+1)))，该程序在2001年成功计算出1到4个变量布尔函数的最小操作符数量。

• AaronFriel 认为 Karnaugh 地图（Karnaugh maps）作为一种直观工具，可以帮助人们找到这些简化方法，但未被提及。
• dooglius 提出是否可以直接使用晶体管或标准单元实现此方法，并认为这对ASIC，特别是从FPGA查找表映射的结构化ASIC非常有用。

research!rsc
Thoughts and links about programming,
by
Russ Cox
RSS
Minimal Boolean Formulas
Posted on Wednesday, May 18, 2011.
28
.
That's the minimum number of AND or OR operators
you need in order to write any Boolean function of five variables.
Alex Healy
and I computed that in April 2010.  Until then,
I believe no one had ever known that little fact.
This post describes how we computed it
and how we almost got scooped by
Knuth's Volume 4A
which considers the problem for AND, OR, and XOR.
A Naive Brute Force Approach
Any Boolean function of two variables
can be written with at most 3 AND or OR operators: the parity function
on two variables X XOR Y is (X AND Y') OR (X' AND Y), where X' denotes
“not X.”  We can shorten the notation by writing AND and OR
like multiplication and addition: X XOR Y = X*Y' + X'*Y.
For three variables, parity is also a hardest function, requiring 9 operators:
X XOR Y XOR Z = (X*Z'+X'*Z+Y')*(X*Z+X'*Z'+Y).
For four variables, parity is still a hardest function, requiring 15 operators:
W XOR X XOR Y XOR Z = (X*Z'+X'*Z+W'*Y+W*Y')*(X*Z+X'*Z'+W*Y+W'*Y').
The sequence so far prompts a few questions.  Is parity always a hardest function?
Does the minimum number of operators alternate between 2
n
−1 and 2
n
+1?
I computed these results in January 2001 after hearing
the problem from Neil Sloane, who suggested it as a variant
of a similar problem first studied by Claude Shannon.
The program I wrote to compute a(4) computes the minimum number of
operators for every Boolean function of n variables
in order to find the largest minimum over all functions.
There are 2
4
= 16 settings of four variables, and each function
can pick its own value for each setting, so there are 2
16
different
functions.  To make matters worse, you build new functions
by taking pairs of old functions and joining them with AND or OR.
2
16
different functions means 2
16
·2
16
= 2
32
pairs of functions.
The program I wrote was a mangling of the Floyd-Warshall
all-pairs shortest paths algorithm.  That algorithm is:
// Floyd-Warshall all pairs shortest path
func compute():
for each node i
for each node j
dist[i][j] = direct distance, or ∞
for each node k
for each node i
for each node j
d = dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]
if d < dist[i][j]
dist[i][j] = d
return
The algorithm begins with the distance table dist[i][j] set to
an actual distance if i is connected to j and infinity otherwise.
Then each round updates the table to account for paths
going through the node k: if it's shorter to go from i to k to j,
it saves that shorter distance in the table.  The nodes are
numbered from 0 to n, so the variables i, j, k are simply integers.
Because there are only n nodes, we know we'll be done after
the outer loop finishes.
The program I wrote to find minimum Boolean formula sizes is
an adaptation, substituting formula sizes for distance.
// Algorithm 1
func compute()
for each function f
size[f] = ∞
for each single variable function f = v
size[f] = 0
loop
changed = false
for each function f
for each function g
d = size[f] + 1 + size[g]
if d < size[f OR g]
size[f OR g] = d
changed = true
if d < size[f AND g]
size[f AND g] = d
changed = true
if not changed
return
Algorithm 1 runs the same kind of iterative update loop as the Floyd-Warshall algorithm,
but it isn't as obvious when you can stop, because you don't
know the maximum formula size beforehand.
So it runs until a round doesn't find any new functions to make,
iterating until it finds a fixed point.
The pseudocode above glosses over some details, such as
the fact that the per-function loops can iterate over a
queue of functions known to have finite size, so that each
loop omits the functions that aren't
yet known.  That's only a constant factor improvement,
but it's a useful one.
Another important detail missing above
is the representation of functions.  The most convenient
representation is a binary truth table.
For example,
if we are computing the complexity of two-variable functions,
there are four possible inputs, which we can number as follows.
X
Y
Value
false
false
00
2
= 0
false
true
01
2
= 1
true
false
10

= 2
true
true
11
2
= 3
The functions are then the 4-bit numbers giving the value of the
function for each input.  For example, function 13 = 1101
2
is true for all inputs except X=false Y=true.
Three-variable functions correspond to 3-bit inputs generating 8-bit truth tables,
and so on.
This representation has two key advantages.  The first is that
the numbering is dense, so that you can implement a map keyed
by function using a simple array.  The second is that the operations
“f AND g” and “f OR g” can be implemented using
bitwise operators: the truth table for “f AND g” is the bitwise
AND of the truth tables for f and g.
That program worked well enough in 2001 to compute the
minimum number of operators necessary to write any
1-, 2-, 3-, and 4-variable Boolean function.  Each round

不同观点：
• **对设计和用户体验的赞赏**：
   - weego 赞扬了网站设计的精美，并询问设计工作是由内部完成还是由代理机构完成。
   - techguy06 对登陆页面的构建工具（如是否使用Framer）表示好奇。

• **对技术实现及产品定位的讨论**：
   - b0a04gl 认为 Reducto 可以作为长期记忆层，处理文档版本中的各种变化，而其他工具通常提取后就会忘记。
   - shuss 强调了文档变体和复杂性对数据提取的挑战，认为需要专门的平台如 Unstract 来处理复杂性，而不是简单地依赖 LLM 和简单提示。

• **市场竞争及产品对比**：
   - throwaway7783 询问 Reducto 是否与 unstructured.io 竞争，并关注谷歌等大公司不断改进的模型。
   - skadamat 询问 Reducto 与 Datalab 在准确性方面的比较。

• **用户体验及技术问题反馈**：
   - serjester 提到移动网站似乎有问题。
   - omaerkhan 报告了访问 studio 链接时出现过多重定向的错误。
   - Fraaaank 质疑为何只有企业计划才提供数据处理协议，这在欧洲是法律要求。

• **对市场动态及产品哲学的深度分析**：
   - jhuguet 分享了从欧洲市场观察到的动态，包括传统工具的惯性及市场对价格的敏感性，并讨论了构建反馈循环及自动化的重要性。
   - jhuguet 还提到了一些技术挑战，如提取置信度问题及 OCR 错误，并分享了一些技术方法和实验链接。

补充讨论：
• **对产品发布及市场成熟的看法**：
   - willwjack 表示该产品在他之前处理 RAG 工作流时会非常有帮助。
   - c_moscardi 恭喜产品发布并提到之前与团队的交流。

• **幽默及非正式互动**：
   - rd 开玩笑地提到看到同名人的惊喜。
   - bravesoul2 开玩笑地表示要拿一份棘手的文档来测试产品。

争议焦点：
• **数据处理协议的法律要求**：Fraaaank 质疑为何只有企业计划才提供数据处理协议，这在欧洲是法律要求，暗示了对产品定价策略的不满。

• **技术实现的可行性**：shuss 和 jhuguet 强调了处理无限变体文档的复杂性，认为简单的 LLM 提示无法在生产环境中有效工作，需要更复杂的平台和工具支持。

总结：评论中主要围绕产品的设计美学、技术实现、市场竞争及用户反馈展开讨论，同时涉及一些技术挑战和市场动态的深度分析。争议点主要集中在数据处理协议的法律要求和技术实现的可行性上。

data.title: Interesting Bits of Postgres Grammar
data.author: sbdchd
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了PostgreSQL的**Squawk**语法分析器及其一些有趣的语法特性：

1. **自定义运算符**：PostgreSQL依赖大量自定义运算符，如`<->`、`##`、`@>`等，这些运算符可以是前缀或中缀，但不能是后缀。有趣的是，利用自定义运算符，类似Trino的lambda表达式可以在PostgreSQL中解析，但优先级可能错误。

2. **复合查询的排序**：在复合查询（如`union`）中，`order by`应用于整个查询结果。

3. **百分比类型**：在创建函数时，可以基于表的列类型指定参数类型。

4. **字符串连续**：连续的字符串字面量会自动合并，但中间有注释则会出错，这是SQL标准的行为。

5. **引用标识符**：标识符可以用双引号括起来，双引号内的双引号需要转义。同时，支持使用Unicode转义字符。

6. **运算符函数**：运算符可以作为函数调用，允许指定运算符的模式和 schema。

文章总结认为，自定义运算符是PostgreSQL与其他主流语言差异较大的部分，实现起来可能比较复杂。

I’ve been working on
Squawk
for a while, it’s a linter for PostgreSQL, and it
now
uses a
handmade parser
.
So let’s explore some interesting bits from the
Postgres grammar
.
Custom Operators
Very few operators are defined in the grammar itself
and lots of Postgres features rely on custom operators.
For example, Postgres uses
<->
for comparing geometric types
, along with a whole host of others:
##
,
@-@
,
#
,
@>
,
<@>
,
&<
,
&>
,
|>>
,
|<<
,
<^
,
>^
,
?-
,
?|
,
?||
,
~=
.
Note: custom operators can be prefix or infix, but not postfix.
A neat consequence of custom operators is that the following
lambda expression syntax from Trino
parses natively in Postgres:
select
array_filter
(
array
[
1
,
2
,
2
,
3
],
e
->
(
e
%
2
)
=
0
);
Albiet with the wrong precedence.
Precedence with Compound
select
s
The following:
select
foo
union
select
bar
order
by
baz
;
Parses the same as:
(
select
foo
union
select
bar
)
order
by
baz
;
Meaning the
order by
clause is applied to the overall compound select.
Percent Types
With
create function
, you can
specify types based on a table’s column type
.
For example, using the type of column
c
on table
t
:
create
function
f
(
a
t
.
c
%
type
)
as
'select 1'
language
plpgsql
;
String Continuation
If you have two string literals separated by new lines, then they’ll be merged together:
select
'foo'
'bar'
;
returns
'foobar'
But if there’s a comment in between, it’s a syntax error:
select
'foo'
/* hmm */
'bar'
;
Query 1 ERROR at Line 2: : ERROR:  syntax error at or near "'bar'"
LINE 2: 'bar';
^
This behavior is part of the
SQL standard
.
Quoted Idents
In Postgres you can optionally quote your identifiers, so the following are the same:
select
*
from
t
;
select
*
from
"t"
;
If you want to include a double quote in your identifier name, you can escape it like so:
select
*
from
"foo
""
bar"
which will select from the
foo " bar
table.
Unicode Escapes
You can also prefix quoted identifiers with
U&
and pass unicode escape codes:
-- `74` is the unicode number for `t`
select
*
from
U
&
"
\0
074"
;
And if you want to change the escape character from
\
, you can write:
-- `74` is the unicode number for `t`
select
*
from
U
&
"!0074"
uescape
'!'
;
Operator Function
Instead of using an operator directly:
select
1
+
2
;
You can use the operator function:
select
1
operator
(
+
)
2
;
Which allows specifying the operator’s schema:
select
1
operator
(
pg_catalog
.
+
)
2
;
It also works as a prefix operator:
select
operator
(
-
)
1
;
Conclusion
Overall, I think custom operators diverge the most from other mainstream languages and can be tricky to implement.

data.title: uv: An extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust
data.author: chirau
data.article_summary:
**uv** 是一个用 Rust 编写的高速 Python 包和项目管理工具，能够替代 pip、pipx、poetry、pyenv 等多个工具。它具有以下特点：

1. **速度快**：比 pip 快 10-100 倍。
2. **项目管理**：支持锁文件、工作区等功能，类似于 rye 或 poetry。
3. **依赖管理**：支持内联依赖元数据，可管理单文件脚本的依赖。
4. **Python 版本管理**：安装和管理多个 Python 版本。
5. **工具执行和安装**：类似 pipx，可运行和安装 Python 包提供的命令行工具。
6. **跨平台**：支持 macOS、Linux 和 Windows。
7. **高效磁盘空间使用**：通过全局缓存进行依赖去重。

安装可通过 curl 或 pip 进行，文档可在 [docs.astral.sh/uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv) 查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Python包管理工具 `uv` 的评价与使用体验

不同观点：
• **支持 `uv`，认为其高效且易用**：
  - 用户 [acheong08] 提到在共享服务器上，由于包和驱动问题以及 `pip` 缓存占用大量空间，切换到 `uv` 后问题解决，体验大幅提升。
  - 用户 [samsartor] 从 `conda` 转向 `uv`，并赞赏其处理非PyPI依赖（如GitHub、内部仓库等）的能力。
  - 用户 [polivier] 对 `uv` 的速度印象深刻，比 `pip` 快很多。
  - 用户 [leonheld] 喜欢 `uv` 的脚本执行功能，通过 `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run` 轻松运行Python脚本。
  - 用户 [mh-] 也提到 `uv` 的速度快得让人怀疑是否工作正常。
  - 用户 [eats_indigo] 和 [IceHegel] 表示 `uv` 带来了显著的开发质量提升，尤其是在与 `Ruff` 结合使用时。
  - 用户 [pu_pe] 认为 `uv` 快得没有理由再用 `pip` 或 `conda`。
  - 用户 [6ak74rfy] 强调 `uv` 无需手动管理环境，自动处理Python版本和运行代码。

• **对 `uv` 的某些功能或配置存在疑问或建议**：
  - 用户 [andy_ppp] 提到希望 `uv` 能自动设置 `PYTHONPATH`，以便更容易地从指定目录导入包。
  - 用户 [larkost] 指出在资源受限的系统（如AWS T2.micro 运行Windows）上，`uv` 会尝试打开过多并发下载，导致超时问题，并建议通过环境变量限制并发数。

补充讨论：
• **`uv` 的技术优势与创新**：
  - 用户 [theLiminator] 认为 `uv` 是“重新发明轮子”的成功案例，专注的目标使其比其他工具更高效。
  - 用户 [kissgyorgy] 详细解释了 `uv` 的优化技术，如Range请求和内存解析，使其速度远超其他包管理器。

• **其他用户对 `uv` 的初步尝试与未来展望**：
  - 用户 [nrvn] 分享了一种运行小型可执行脚本的新方法。
  - 用户 [linsomniac] 正在尝试将 `uv` 与NixOS结合使用，并对未来的开发工作充满期待。

争议焦点：
• 目前争议不大，主要是一些功能上的改进建议，如 `PYTHONPATH` 的自动设置和并发下载的优化。总体上，用户对 `uv` 的评价非常积极。

data.title: NASA's Voyager Found a 30k-50k Kelvin "Wall" at the Edge of Solar System
data.author: world2vec
data.article_summary: 1977年，NASA发射了旅行者号探测器，以研究太阳系的边缘和星际介质。旅行者号探测器先后穿越了太阳风的边界——即日球层顶（heliopause），进入了星际空间。在穿越所谓的"火墙"时，它们测量到温度高达30,000-50,000开尔文（54,000-90,000华氏度）。日球层是由太阳风形成的巨大气泡，而日球层顶是太阳风与星际风压力平衡之处。旅行者1号于2012年、旅行者2号于2018年先后穿越日球层顶，发现外部磁场与内部磁场平行。这些探测器提供了太阳系之外的宝贵数据，揭示了诸多意外发现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NASA Voyager探测器在太阳系边缘发现的温度墙及其相关科学讨论

不同观点：
• [mlhpdx] 认为高温但密度极低的环境难以想象，因为这种情况下热量传递会非常少。
• [LeratoAustini] 提到地球上的生命形式温度相对宇宙中的其他物体非常低，并列举了从0开尔文到超过10万亿开尔文的例子，强调了生命温度的狭窄范围。
• [jakeydus] 指出新闻标题与实际文章内容之间的差异，标题中的"wall"在文章中被解释为并非实际的墙。
• [cooper_ganglia] 回忆起2006年在学校学习时被告知太阳系外有一道无法穿越的“火墙”，认为这一发现部分验证了当时的猜测。
• [anigbrowl] 对目前仅依赖Voyager探测器进行深空探索表示不满，认为长期缺乏后续深空探测项目是一种浪费，并批评对太空探索的长期承诺不足。
• [floxy] 讨论了粒子速度与温度测量之间的关系，质疑温度的定义和应用，尤其是在粒子稀疏的环境中。
• [whycome] 对温度范围的含义和测量精度表示困惑，并希望明确Voyager探测器的数量和具体测量情况。
• [stuff4ben] 对近50年历史的技术仍能提供有用的科学数据表示惊叹，并提到新视野号是另一个可能进入星际空间的任务。
• [1970-01-01] 提出一个假设，如果物体进入太阳系内部的这个温度墙，是否可能被加热到适合生命存在的温度。
• [westurner] 提出了一系列关于质量、能量密度、热墙对称性以及与其他物理现象（如引力波）的关系的问题，并提到超流体量子相对论和不同物质相位的可能性。
• [righthand] 认为太阳系拥有类似大气的结构很有趣，尽管这在高中教育中并未被广泛讨论。
• [flippyhead] 以幽默的方式暗示这是外星人用来隐藏自己的设置。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：新闻标题与实际科学发现之间的差异，以及对深空探测项目长期停滞的不满。
• 重要论据和例子：LeratoAustini列举了宇宙中极端温度的范围，anigbrowl批评太空探索的长期承诺不足并提到对年轻一代的影响，floxy对温度和粒子运动之间的关系进行了深入探讨。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：westurner提到了多种物理现象和理论，如超流体量子相对论，以及对太阳系结构的复杂理解。

44357378.article_content:
Voyager, the little (quite big) spacecraft that could.
Image credit:
NASA/JPL-Caltech
DOWNLOAD PDF VERSION
In 1977, NASA launched the Voyager probes to study the Solar System's edge, and the interstellar medium between the stars. One by one, they both hit the "wall of fire" at the boundaries of our home system, measuring temperatures of 30,000-50,000 kelvin (54,000-90,000 degrees Fahrenheit) on their passage through it.
There are a few ways you could define the edge of the Solar System – for instance, where the planets end, or at the Oort cloud, the boundary of the Sun's gravitational influence where objects may still
return closer
to the Sun. One way is to define it as the edge of the Sun's magnetic field, where it pushes up against the interstellar medium, known as the heliopause.
"The Sun sends out a constant flow of charged particles called the solar wind, which ultimately travels past all the planets to some three times the distance to Pluto before being impeded by the interstellar medium,"
NASA explains
. "This forms a giant bubble around the Sun and its planets, known as the heliosphere."
It is beyond that where the heliopause lies.
"The boundary between solar wind and interstellar wind is the heliopause, where the pressure of the two winds are in balance. This balance in pressure causes the solar wind to turn back and flow down the tail of the heliosphere," NASA
continues
.
"As the heliosphere plows through interstellar space, a
bow shock
forms, similar to what forms as a ship plowing through the ocean."
On August 25, 2012, Voyager 1 became the first spacecraft to go beyond the heliosphere and cross the heliopause, followed by Voyager 2 in
2018
. Prior to the Voyager spacecraft crossing the heliopause, scientists didn't really know where the boundary would be, but the fact that the probes hit it at different distances helped support a few predictions about it.
"Scientists expected that the edge of the heliosphere, called the heliopause, can move as the Sun's activity changes, sort of like a lung expanding and contracting with breath," a
NASA statement
explains. "This was consistent with the fact that the two probes encountered the heliopause at different distances from the Sun."
While not a hard edge, or a "wall" as it has sometimes been called, here both spacecraft measured temperatures of 30,000-50,000 kelvin (54,000-90,000 degrees Fahrenheit), which is why it is sometimes also referred to as a "
wall of fire
".  The craft survived the wall as, though the particles they measured were extremely energetic, the chances of collision in this particle-sparse region of space are so low that not enough heat could be transferred to the duo.
The
Voyager
spacecraft continue to send us data from beyond this "wall", the only two probes that have crossed it so far, nearly 50 years after they were launched. Together they have found several surprises on our first glimpse outside the Solar System.
"An observation by Voyager 2's magnetic field instrument confirms a surprising result from Voyager 1: The magnetic field in the region just beyond the heliopause is parallel to the magnetic field inside the heliosphere," NASA explained, shortly after one such surprise.
"With Voyager 1, scientists had only one sample of these magnetic fields and couldn't say for sure whether the apparent alignment was characteristic of the entire exterior region or just a coincidence. Voyager 2's magnetometer observations confirm the Voyager 1 finding and indicate that the two fields align."

data.title: Transparent Ambition
data.author: goranmoomin
data.article_summary: 《Transparent Ambition》一文探讨了用户界面中透明和半透明效果的演变及其问题。文章指出，从Mac OS X的Aqua界面到Windows的Aero，再到苹果的Vibrancy和Windows 10的Acrylic，这些设计趋势起初是为了让界面看起来更酷，并声称能增加内容显示空间。然而，这些效果往往牺牲了界面的清晰度和易读性，使用户更难解析界面元素。文章批评了如Liquid Glass这样的设计过度追求视觉冲击和品牌一致性，而忽视了实际使用的便利性。作者认为，这种设计哲学本末倒置，过于关注外表而忽略了功能性，最终给用户带来困扰，特别是在macOS系统设置等界面设计中体现明显。文章呼吁设计应更注重实用性而非仅视觉效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple的半透明设计及其在用户界面中的作用

不同观点：
• pwg认为，Apple设计师为了保住工作，必须不断进行设计更改，即使这些更改（如半透明设计）并不受用户欢迎。他认为设计改变更多是为了让设计师在公司内部展示其价值，而非真正满足用户需求。
• abraxas反对极端扁平化设计，认为当前许多UI缺乏视觉线索，难以区分不同元素（如按钮、文本等）。虽然液态玻璃效果可能不太理想，但相比纯文本和简陋图标的设计要好。
• joshmarinacci不认同设计需要在不同平台间保持一致的观点。他购买Mac是为了鼠标和键盘体验，而液态玻璃设计削弱了这种体验。
• w10-1认为Apple已经与实际用户脱节，内部力量主导了决策。用户测试信号被这些内部力量控制，市场信号被Apple传递的高品质形象所掩盖。
• tanvach指出，虽然iOS有“减少透明度”选项，但启用后会感觉设计缺乏精致。他还怀疑透明设计可能是为了UI/UX团队在公司内证明其存在价值。
• karaterobot为Apple设计师辩护，认为虽然半透明设计在信息传递上可能不是最优的，但它们为产品增添了吸引力和个性，这种策略对Apple是成功的。
• matznerd提出，半透明设计可能是为未来的AR眼镜或其他小型设备做准备，这些设备需要透明显示以看到现实世界。
• stephenhandley以讽刺的语气指出，讨论UI设计问题的网站图标却无法链接到主页，暗示设计问题普遍存在。
• PaulHoule回顾了20世纪90年代对操作系统定义的狭隘观点，并比较了不同操作系统在GUI设计上的优缺点，认为Windows虽然不一致且丑陋，但至少能完成工作，而Linux在处理界面问题上更为糟糕。

补充讨论：
• 设计改变是否为了设计师保住工作而进行，存在争议（pwg vs. karaterobot）。
• 半透明设计是否提升了用户体验，存在不同看法（abraxas支持，joshmarinacci反对）。
• Apple是否与用户需求脱节，w10-1持肯定态度，而其他人则未明确提及这一点。
• 半透明设计可能的未来应用（如AR眼镜）引发了新的讨论方向（matznerd）。

44341515.article_content:
Transparent Ambition
2025-06-19
Translucent user interfaces is a nightmare from which I am trying to awake.
Aside from movie visual effect trickery, it started out in Mac OS X's Aqua, followed by Windows Vista's Aero, followed by (then) OS X's Vibrancy, followed by Windows 10's Acrylic. Over time, more and more of the user interface has become translucent similar to foggy/privacy-preserving sheets of glass.
The unstated goal has always been to "look cool". The stated goal has always been to "give more pixels to your content".
The sparse, flat esthetic of iOS 7 and its successors held a tenuous alliance with these transparency effects; being one of few real-world physical effects allowed to be imitated. When waiting for the iOS 7 era to end and the crucible of history to turn once more, the
card-like esthetic
of some prominent new UI features looked like a hint.
Instead, we got Liquid Glass, which is an ambitious implementation of a visual material and associated effects. They look impressive. They do add both personality and a trademark look. They also, to a first approximation, make the user interfaces worse.
They are not as easy to parse visually - static, predictable positions are eschewed, or maintained under the condition that they
do not look
static and predictable. They continue the trend of leaving less and less color/ink for definition of the UI itself; text or symbols cast in Liquid Glass have worse legibility and are harder to make out, while user interface elements on top of Liquid Glass are positioned with the primary purpose to make a Liquid Glass UI look like a Liquid Glass UI. Well-known and time tested elements of design are, if not abandoned, then demoted below the desire to have a visually striking, consistent branding user interface.
Apple's designers (and those of many other companies) come back to the idea of translucency giving order and imbuing personality. I cannot for the life of me understand where this idea comes from. When multiple layers of different imagery shine through each other, I am not helped by this. The user interface placed on a semi-transparent panel is not more effective because it is set against a smeared mess of colors, nor am I emotionally fulfilled as a human being for knowing that the mess comes from a treasured personal memory.
The problem with the philosophy birthing these ideas, and
running rampantly through the manifesto motivating Liquid Glass
, is that
it insists upon itself
.
The world is full of breakthroughs that end up moving the state of the art forward, which have flaws, sharp corners that are then weathered by time and experience. The first decade of Aqua is a great example of this, in going from flashy, jarring, gaudy tech demo to something a bit more toned down, but still elegant, effective, playful, beautiful and with a lot of personality.
Aqua had in its roots that it
wanted
to be user interface, with clearer and bigger fonts, more prominent key buttons, allowances for pro features, solving issues that classic Mac OS had long suffered. Vibrancy and now Liquid Glass do not hold the same desires; rather, they seem to increasingly want there to be
less
user interface. Scooting fifty buttons out of your way when someone is trying to read an email, fine - there are many times where that is legitimate. But the pixels previously devoted to assembling a dependable user interface are now automatically made to retreat, to shrink-to-fit.
Even this makes sense in a handful of scenarios. Mixed reality, augmented reality, or the Vision Pro's "spatial computing" does introduce a concern of physically layering UI on top of not just itself, but also physical objects.
What doesn't make sense, no matter how gangbusters these future technologies break through, is painting every problem with this solution. Much has been made recently of the evaporation of usability from macOS's recent System Settings, being made to ape the iOS System Settings. The tools used to fit things in a navigable hierarchy on a screen a handful of inches are cast as the only tools able to solve a similar problem for a platform where a much bigger canvas and two vastly different interactions are always available.
Rather than model Apple's mastery of all their devices, Liquid Glass models the propensity of design at Apple to wag the rest of the dog. Rather than model that design is how it works, translucency-obsessed design in general and Liquid Glass in particular models that job one, two and three are to look impressive and hang the person who ultimately has to get something done.
Liquid Glass is an obsessive focus on visual design, special effects and appearance. Going back roughly a decade, the iPhone X brought a new interaction design breakthough too, with a gestural interface that made it possible to zip through apps, go back and forth with fluid gestures that moved at the speed you drove them, and change your mind midway through. • PaulHoule回顾了20世纪90年代对操作系统定义的狭隘观点，并比较了不同操作系统在GUI设计上的优缺点，认为Windows虽然不一致且丑陋，但至少能完成工作，而Linux在处理界面问题上更为糟糕。

补充讨论：
• 设计改变是否为了设计师保住工作而进行，存在争议（pwg vs. karaterobot）。
• 半透明设计是否提升了用户体验，存在不同看法（abraxas支持，joshmarinacci反对）。
• Apple是否与用户需求脱节，w10-1持肯定态度，而其他人则未明确提及这一点。
• 半透明设计可能的未来应用（如AR眼镜）引发了新的讨论方向（matznerd）。

i got annoyed at VSCode a while back for being laggy, especially when the vim plugin was running, and at having lots of keybind conflicts between the editor, vim plugin, terminal, and window management. i tried zed but at the time it was quite immature (and still had the problem of lots of keybind conflicts).

data.title: WhatsApp banned on House staffers' devices
data.author: fahd777
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：政府设备的安全性以及在政府设备上使用WhatsApp等应用程序的争议

不同观点：
• **严格限制软件安装和设备安全**：duxup和williamscales认为，政府设备应仅安装最低限度的必要软件，并采取强化安全模式。任何其他软件的安装都应被严格禁止，特别是在涉及高度机密的场所，如白宫或政府设施。

• **加密和元数据的风险**：jandrewrogers和rendall指出，虽然WhatsApp提供端到端加密，但元数据和周边信息的泄露风险仍然存在。元数据可以被用于分析和追踪用户行为，存在安全隐患。

• **政治和合规问题**：theodric和alephnerd提到，禁止在政府机构使用WhatsApp可能更多是出于合规性和透明度的考虑，而非单纯的安全问题。这涉及到避免潜在的法律问题和政治敏感性。

• **技术细节和推测**：reillyse和aaroninsf深入探讨了潜在的技术漏洞和政府可能采取的手段，包括通过合法途径获取数据和嵌入技术代理人。reillyse甚至推测了具体的加密漏洞利用方式。

补充讨论：
• **对Meta和WhatsApp的争议**：baxtr和v5v3引用了Meta发言人的声明，并对其进行了讽刺性评论，指出政府一方面要求安全，另一方面又怀疑应用程序的安全性。

• **替代方案的建议**：deadbabe和fennecbutt提出了使用其他通信工具或对当前状况的批评，表现出对现有安全措施的不满和对替代方案的兴趣。

• **对 Zuckerberg 和 Meta 的怀疑**：aaroninsf和josefritzishere等人对Meta公司及其CEO马克·扎克伯格持怀疑态度，认为他们可能通过后门获取并利用政府高层的通信信息，以维护其商业利益。

争议的焦点：  
1. **WhatsApp的安全性是否足够**：一方认为端到端加密足以保证安全，另一方则担心元数据和其他形式的信息泄露。
2. **政府设备上使用非批准软件的管理问题**：讨论中对如何有效管理和限制政府设备上软件安装存在不同看法。
3. **政治和技术因素的交织**：对于是否因政治因素而非技术原因禁止使用某些软件，存在不同解读。

data.title: Rivulet: An esolang inspired by calligraphy && code [video]
data.author: exiguus
data.article_summary: "Rivulet" 是一种受书法启发的编程语言，摒弃了传统编程语言中的关键字，转而借鉴自然语言的书写形式。其代码以流线型线条书写，类似于手写语言的紧密交织，逻辑与常见编程语言大不相同，更注重视觉表现。Rivulet 代码示例展示了七种不同的数字零写法，每个零都是一个“线条”，多个线条构成“字形”。该语言的规则更像自然演变的语言，强调表达力与模糊性，不同于一般编程语言追求的清晰性。演讲中还介绍了其他类似语言如 Valence 和一种未命名的字母表，它们都将自然语言的复杂性带入编程中。

Fahrplan
[Rivulet](https://github.com/rottytooth/Rivulet) eschews keywords entirely. This is not done to move *away* from natural language (as in APL's use of mathematical symbols) but instead to draw from an aspect of natural language usually ignored in prog language design: calligraphic writing. Rivulet code is written in flowing lines inspired by handwritten natural and constructed languages. Its logic is alien to most programming languages but makes perfect sense in support of its visual representation of tightly-packed tangles of lines.
In this short talk, I'll introduce this new language alongside other esolangs that draw from less-considered aspects of natlangs and conlangs, embracing their ambiguity and expressive power.
Here is a piece of code in the [Rivulet](https://github.com/rottytooth/Rivulet) language. It shows seven different ways to write the number zero:
```
1 ╵  ╰──╮ ╭───╯╭──╯
2  ╰─╮ ─┘ │╰─╮ └─ ╭─╮
3    │╰──┐└─╴│╰───╯ │
5    ╰─╮ ╰─╮ └─┐  ╭─╯
7    ╶─┘   │ ╶─┘  ╰─╮
11        ╶─┘        │
13                  ─╯╷
```
Each zero is written as a *strand*, a tangle of which is called a *glyph*. Strands of different types each have their own reading in how they move through the glyph. The language's visual style is inspired by the satisfying compactness of mazes, Anni Albers's Meanders series, and space-filling algorithms. Its rules are more like a natural language that evolved over time than a typical programming language favoring clarity above all else.
I will show how the rules for Rivulet came together and contrast the language with several other others that bring the ambiguity and expressiveness of natural language into code. This includes the polysemantic esolang [Valence](https://github.com/rottytooth/Valence) and an as-yet-unnamed alphabet that functions simultaneously as conlang and esolang.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：食品人工色素的监管及其相关问题

不同观点：
• klik99认为， previous administrations 没有对食品色素进行合理监管，导致像RFK Jr.这样的极端人物上台推动必要的改革。klik99肯定RFK Jr.推动变革的努力，但将问题归咎于之前的政府不作为。

• fabian2k反对将所有人工色素一概而论，认为RFK Jr.提出的监管可能缺乏科学依据，主张对每种化学物质分别进行科学论证，避免不科学的推动带来负面影响。

• neuroelectron关注动物食品中也使用了人工色素，特别提到狗粮中的使用情况，认为没有必要。
• N_A_T_E认为问题不在于科学或安全性，而在于成分标签不清晰，建议用通俗易懂的名称代替编号色素名称，以减少消费者的恐惧和误解。
• someonehere强烈反对人工色素的使用，指出这些色素大多来自石油，质疑人们为何能接受将其用于食品。
• Molitor5901批评食品公司如Kraft为了利润不愿更换人工色素，建议政府应更严格地限制食品中的成分。
• Flatcircle简单表达了对问题拖延如此之久的困惑。
• msgodel分享了个人经历，声称某些红色色素具有精神活性效果，并影响其认知功能，暗示这些色素可能有未被广泛认知的副作用。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于人工色素的科学性和安全性，部分人认为应该根据具体化学物质分别评估，而不是一刀切地禁止。
- 讨论中还涉及政府监管的必要性以及企业为了经济利益可能忽视消费者健康的问题。
- 另一个值得注意的点是成分标签的透明性问题，消费者对不明确或编号名称的色素感到不安和不信任。

data.title: Apple Pulls 'Convince Your Parents to Get You a Mac' Ad from YouTube
data.author: fortran77
data.article_summary: 苹果公司将发布仅一天的广告视频《The Parent Presentation》在YouTube上设为私密，不再公开可见，并将其在学生页面的位置下调。此广告旨在通过可自定义的幻灯片展示，帮助大学生说服父母购买Mac，但因在社交媒体上收到负面评价，可能因此被撤下。苹果尚未对此做出回应。这并非苹果首次因广告反响不佳而下架视频。广告视频由喜剧演员Martin Herlihy主演，现已下线。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对苹果公司广告的评价以及对Mac与Windows电脑的比较

不同观点：
• andiareso认为广告很有趣，并指出广告本身就是为了搞笑和夸张，作为家长和Mac用户，他觉得广告没有问题。他还提供了广告的存档链接以供参考。
• cosmicgadget对广告持批评态度，用讽刺的语气模仿广告中的语气，质疑苹果试图将PowerPoint演示文稿与青少年流行文化联系起来的合理性，并暗示现代年轻人更可能自己赚钱买高科技设备，而不是依赖父母。
• joshstrange认为广告虽然有些尴尬，但比苹果其他一些广告要好，不值得过多的负面反馈。他用个人经验说明Mac在稳定性和维护方面优于Windows电脑，特别是在大学使用场景中，并推荐大多数人购买Mac，除非有特殊软件需求。
• parliament32同意广告让人感到尴尬，没有进一步展开论述。
• fortran77表示因为反感苹果，会故意给孩子买Windows ARM笔记本，带有个人情绪和反叛心理。
• xattt提出疑问，认为现代年轻人可能对“前卫”的营销方式已经不敏感，质疑广告的有效性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是广告的质量和效果，一些人觉得广告搞笑，而另一些人觉得尴尬或不合适。
• 另一个讨论点是Mac与Windows电脑的比较，joshstrange通过个人经历强调Mac的优点，如稳定性、保值和质量，而fortran77则出于个人情感偏好选择Windows。
• 不同代人对科技产品和营销方式的接受度也成为讨论的一部分，xattt对现代年轻人是否受特定营销影响提出质疑。

Apple Pulls 'Convince Your Parents to Get You a Mac' Ad From YouTube
Saturday June 21, 2025 7:54 am PDT
by
Joe Rossignol
Apple has marked as private its day-old
The Parent Presentation video
on YouTube, meaning that it is no longer available to watch.
Apple has also moved The Parent Presentation to the bottom of its
College Students page
, effectively burying it. When we reported on the marketing campaign yesterday, the presentation was prominently featured at the top of the page.
It is unclear why Apple is suddenly hiding the ad, or if it will return. Apple did not immediately respond to our request for comment.
On social media, some people said that the ad was cringe or gross, so perhaps Apple pulled the video due to overly negative reception. To be clear, this is merely speculation, and there were others who found humor in the video.
Teenagers can be a tough crowd to impress.
It would not be the first time that Apple pulled ads from YouTube that
did not go over well
, or
became the subject of a class action lawsuit
.
The Parent Presentation is a customizable slideshow that explains why a Mac is a useful tool in college. The presentation is
available to download
for free in PowerPoint, Keynote, and Google Slides formats. Students can customize the presentation slides, and then show it to their parents to convince them to buy them a Mac.
In an accompanying YouTube video shared by Apple, comedian Martin Herlihy showed a group of high school students how to effectively use The Parent Presentation.
It is that video that is now hidden.

data.title: DHEA-S hormone linked to shorter lifespan in men, but not women
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 一项由纽约市立大学Mary Schooling教授领导的研究发现，脱氢表雄酮硫酸酯（DHEA-s）激素水平较高的男性寿命较短，但对女性寿命无显著影响。该研究采用孟德尔随机化方法，分析了欧洲大型遗传数据，以减少混杂因素的影响。结果显示，遗传上DHEA-s水平较高的男性血压升高且寿命缩短，而女性无此现象。由于DHEA在美国作为非处方补充剂销售，研究人员对DHEA的标签和可获得性提出了质疑，并呼吁更多关于其健康影响的证据。研究发表于《Nutrition, Metabolism and Cardiovascular Diseases》期刊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DHEA-S与男性寿命的关系及其相关研究的可信度

不同观点：
• [A_D_E_P_T] 认为该研究质量极低，存在多处严重问题。他们指出，研究使用的孟德尔随机化（MR）分析存在根本性缺陷，主要问题包括：遗传工具变量太弱（仅3个变异位点，解释力仅1%）、多效性问题（变异影响多个代谢途径）、以及调整暴露GWAS时引入了碰撞偏倚（collider bias）。此外，使用父母寿命作为代理结果引入了测量误差和社会经济混杂因素。他们还指出，研究在多重检验校正后，关键发现可能不成立，且研究结论被用于反对DHEA补充剂的政策建议是不合理的。

• [cj] 对研究发现持相对谨慎的态度，认为DHEA和睾酮可能与血压升高存在联系，并引用了一项FDA警告和一项关于DHEA与IGF-1关系的研究。他们提出，激素水平在“理想范围”内对健康有益，过高或过低都可能带来负面影响。

• [anonnon] 对DHEA补充剂的使用表示怀疑，指出睾酮前激素具有不可预测性，可能会导致睾酮转化为雌激素或二氢睾酮（DHT）等副作用。

补充讨论：
• [A_D_E_P_T] 对研究通过同行评审表示惊讶，并认为这是科学文献质量低下的典型案例，甚至考虑向编辑写信反映问题。

• [cj] 引用的研究（[0]）链接了DHEA与IGF-1的关联，并提到高IGF-1与癌症风险增加的关系，进一步讨论了激素水平的平衡问题。

争议焦点：
• 研究的核心争议在于孟德尔随机化分析的有效性和可信度，包括遗传工具变量的选择、多效性问题的处理、以及偏倚和混杂因素的校正。
• DHEA补充剂的实际效果和安全性也是一个讨论热点，尤其是其对激素水平和健康的影响。

总结：评论主要围绕研究的科学质量和DHEA补充剂的实用性展开，不同评论者对其结论的可靠性和实际应用价值持不同看法。

The GIST
DHEA-S hormone linked to shorter lifespan in men, but not women
by
The City University of New York
edited by
Gaby Clark
, 																								reviewed by
Andrew Zinin
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
trusted source
proofread
Credit: Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain
A new genetic
study
suggests that higher levels of the hormone dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-s) are associated with a shorter lifespan in men, but show no significant effect on the lifespan of women.
The research, led by CUNY SPH Professor Mary Schooling, used a Mendelian randomization approach, leveraging
genetic data
from large European cohorts to minimize confounding factors. The paper is published in the journal
Nutrition, Metabolism and Cardiovascular Diseases
.
"Gold standard" evidence, i.e., from randomized controlled trials, about the effects of DHEA supplements on blood pressure or lifespan is very limited, with most of the evidence for blood pressure concerning
women
, and no evidence available for lifespan. To address this gap, Professor Schooling and Dr. Jie V. Zhao from the University of Hong Kong assessed how having genetically higher DHEA-s affected blood pressure and lifespan.
The researchers found genetically higher DHEA-s increased blood pressure and reduced lifespan in men, but not in women.
"Given that DHEA-s is a precursor of testosterone, our finding is consistent with a recent
warning
from the FDA that testosterone products may increase
blood pressure
in men," says Schooling. "Our findings about DHEA-s also likely reducing
lifespan
in men raises questions about the labeling and availability of DHEA over the counter in the United States."
More information:
C Mary Schooling et al, Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate on lifespan in men and women using Mendelian randomization,
Nutrition, Metabolism and Cardiovascular Diseases
(2025).
DOI: 10.1016/j.numecd.2025.104128

The City University of New York

44356549.article_summary: 一项由纽约市立大学Mary Schooling教授领导的研究发现，脱氢表雄酮硫酸酯（DHEA-s）激素水平较高的男性寿命较短，但对女性寿命无显著影响。该研究采用孟德尔随机化方法，分析了欧洲大型遗传数据，以减少混杂因素的影响。结果显示，遗传上DHEA-s水平较高的男性血压升高且寿命缩短，而女性无此现象。由于DHEA在美国作为非处方补充剂销售，研究人员对DHEA的标签和可获得性提出了质疑，并呼吁更多关于其健康影响的证据。研究发表于《Nutrition, Metabolism and Cardiovascular Diseases》期刊。
44356549.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DHEA-S与男性寿命的关系及其相关研究的可信度

不同观点：
• [A_D_E_P_T] 认为该研究质量极低，存在多处严重问题。他们指出，研究使用的孟德尔随机化（MR）分析存在根本性缺陷，主要问题包括：遗传工具变量太弱（仅3个变异位点，解释力仅1%）、多效性问题（变异影响多个代谢途径）、以及调整暴露GWAS时引入了碰撞偏倚（collider bias）。此外，使用父母寿命作为代理结果引入了测量误差和社会经济混杂因素。他们还指出，研究在多重检验校正后，关键发现可能不成立，且研究结论被用于反对DHEA补充剂的政策建议是不合理的。

• [cj] 对研究发现持相对谨慎的态度，认为DHEA和睾酮可能与血压升高存在联系，并引用了一项FDA警告和一项关于DHEA与IGF-1关系的研究。他们提出，激素水平在“理想范围”内对健康有益，过高或过低都可能带来负面影响。

• [anonnon] 对DHEA补充剂的使用表示怀疑，指出睾酮前激素具有不可预测性，可能会导致睾酮转化为雌激素或二氢睾酮（DHT）等副作用。

补充讨论：
• [A_D_E_P_T] 对研究通过同行评审表示惊讶，并认为这是科学文献质量低下的典型案例，甚至考虑向编辑写信反映问题。

• [cj] 引用的研究（[0]）链接了DHEA与IGF-1的关联，并提到高IGF-1与癌症风险增加的关系，进一步讨论了激素水平的平衡问题。

争议焦点：
• 研究的核心争议在于孟德尔随机化分析的有效性和可信度，包括遗传工具变量的选择、多效性问题的处理、以及偏倚和混杂因素的校正。
• DHEA补充剂的实际效果和安全性也是一个讨论热点，尤其是其对激素水平和健康的影响。

总结：评论主要围绕研究的科学质量和DHEA补充剂的实用性展开，不同评论者对其结论的可靠性和实际应用价值持不同看法。

data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了作者受Bartosz Ciechanowski博客启发，计划制作一个真实的机械表爆炸图模型的过程和挑战。作者解释了机械表运动的复杂性，并提到目前市场上没有这种展示真实组装的模型。作者打算使用早期1900年代的简单怀表机芯，通过分层透明树脂铸造来实现这一想法。然而，制作过程中遇到了一些问题，包括树脂泛黄、固化时间长以及层间缝隙明显等。尽管如此，作者仍决心继续这一项目，探索未知技能并寻找解决方案。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• **对中国制造手表机芯的讨论**：alexjplant 对文中使用 PT5000 机芯表示赞赏，指出其为 ETA 2824-2 的中国克隆版，并讨论了中国制造手表的性价比和质量。
• **对工艺技术的进一步设想**：
   - ziofill 建议通过改变树脂的折射率，可以让鱼线完全消失。
   - modeless 提出使用一种在固化前为凝胶状的透明物质，以便手动调整部件位置。
   - petermcneeley 指出如果支撑物与树脂的折射率相同，支撑物将不可见。

补充讨论：
• **对 vintage 手表的兴趣**：protonbob 询问在 eBay 上容易买到的古董手表，强调希望是瑞士机芯，但不关心品牌。
• **对类似艺术项目的联想**：

   - jameshart 提到 Adam Savage 的一个类似项目，尝试制作一个屏幕可用的爆炸图手机，但结果更像原型而非展示品。
• **对工艺实现的实际建议**：
   - Retr0id 分享了自己处理树脂铸件的经验，描述了如何用砂纸打磨以达到完美的镜面效果。
• **对项目商业潜力的看法**：
   - jasonjmcgehee 认为这些作品可以被博物馆展示，并提到一个灵感来源。
   - kzzzznot 和 kiru_io 都表示了对项目的喜爱，并认为其有销售潜力或可以与手表制造商合作。
• **替代实现方法的建议**：WillAdams 提出使用激光打印在玻璃或亚克力块内实现类似效果，并提供了一些相关资源链接。

争议焦点：
• **项目的神圣性与创意酷炫之间的张力**：thom 表达了一种复杂的情感，一方面认为这些机械的魅力在于其可靠性和修复过程，另一方面也承认项目的酷炫之处，并联想到自己童年时类似的树脂工艺尝试。

44347425.article_content:
Fredrik Flornes Ellertsen
Projects ▾
Kintsugi repair
Snus reduction
EOG + REM sleep
Nixie alarm clock
2048 algorithm
Design notes
Contact
Mechanical Watch: Exploded View
In May 2022, someone posted to Hacker News
Bartosz
Ciechanowski's
blog post
explaining how mechanical watch movements work. Since then, his blog has
been my absolute favorite corner of the Internet. His posts are not just
well written and easy to follow, the accompanying interactive
illustrations are magnificent.
The first illustration in his blog post about mechanical watch movements
allows you to "explode" a ticking mechanical movement and rotate it to
inspect its every component from any angle. I owe my foray into the
hobby of watchmaking to Bartosz, but that's not what this blog post is
about. Instead, I want to scratch an itch I've had for years now: How
cool would it be to hold an exploded view of a
real
mechanical
watch in your hand?
Screenshot of the exploded view render from
Bartosz
Ciechanowski's
blog post.
Apparently, nobody builds such models
I figured that surely, someone has had this idea and built it before. On
eBay you'll find cubes of resin embedding various random components from
mechanical watches, but they are typically sold as "steampunk art" and
bear little resemblance to the proper assembly of a mechanical watch
movement. Sometimes, you'll find resin castings showing every component
of a movement spread out in a plane like a buffet---very cool, but not
what I'm looking for. Despite my best efforts, I haven't found anyone
who makes what I'm after, and I have a sneaking suspicion as to why that
is.
Every component making up the movement of a beautiful 1960's Longines
Flagship wristwatch I worked on recently, laid out "buffet style".
Building an exploded view of a mechanical watch movement is undoubtedly
very fiddly work and requires working knowledge about how a mechanical
watch is assembled. People with that skillset are called watchmakers.
Maker
, not "destroyer for the sake of art". I guess it falls to
me, then, to give this project an honest shot.
...how do you build such a model?
Here comes my favorite part: jumping head-first into a project requiring
a set of skills I don't even know exist, let alone possess, following a
process that develops as the project evolves. So how would one go
about building a real-life exploded view of a mechanical watch movement?
The first thing to consider is what type of mechanical watch movement to
"explode". Although he doesn't explicitly say, I think Bartosz
Ciechanowski's blog post is based on the
ETA caliber
2824-2
mechanical watch movement (or one of its many clones, such as
the Chinese PT5000). This is a very robust and popular automatic
(self-winding) mechanical wristwatch movement found in many watches.
It's considered one of the all-time "workhorse" movements of the
industry. I highly encourage the curious reader to check out
this YouTube video
of a very skilled and equally witty watchmaker servicing a Hamilton
watch featuring this exact movement. The video will also reveal how many
absolutely miniscule components make up the ETA-2824, making it less
than ideal for my initial prototyping. A larger and simpler movement
would be much better.
Luckily, in the late 1800's to early 1900's, many people carried a
pocketwatch about their person. However, as smaller wristwatches gained
popularity among men, beginning around the first world war with trench
watches, pocket watches lost their value as timepieces. Many were melted
down to reclaim the gold used to case the movement. Today, you can find
gorgeous, hand-engraved movements from the turn of the 20th century on
eBay
for next to nothing.
Pocketwatches are the simplest mechanical watch movements out there:
they typically don't have any date complications, aren't self-winding,
and usually don't even have a central seconds hand---that's a
relatively modern feature. There's a reason budding watchmakers start
out practicing on pocketwatch movements.
Now for the hard part: How do you suspend 50-100 tiny components to form
an exploded view of the assembly?
A beautiful early 1900's pocketwatch movement from eBay. $20 for a piece
of horological art.
Layered resin casting
The model I'm planning to build must stand up to being handled, which
means it must be solid. In turn, that probably means that I need to cast
my components in clear epoxy resin. My first idea was to build the
exploded model up, layer by layer, letting the resin cure between each
layer. To save time, I experimented with clear resin that cures when
exposed to UV light. There are several reasons why this did not work:
The resin I purchased ended up with a heavy yellow tint after
curing.
My puny UV flashlight took forever to cure a pour even 1 mm
deep.
The seams between layers are very visible.
The first two problems can probably be solved by throwing money at the
problem, but the last issue seems to be a problem with varying indices
of refraction throughout my casting. The

data.article_summary: **Interactive Playground** 是一个允许用户直接在浏览器中尝试类型推断示例和探索各种算法的小工具。它提供了动手实践的简单环境，适合学习者通过实际操作来理解编程概念和算法逻辑，无需搭建复杂开发环境。这种互动方式有助于更直观地掌握代码运行和类型推断的机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bruno Oliveira研究小组的工作量以及使用Python进行类型系统建模的可行性

不同观点：
• [dmkolobov] 认为Bruno Oliveira的研究小组产出非常多，并对CP语言（具有不相交交集和并集类型的语言）表示赞赏，提供了一个GitHub链接以供参考。

• [b0a04gl] 指出Python虽然本身对类型的强制性不强，但在建模类型系统方面却出人意料地有效。他解释说，使用Python无需与编译器层级斗争或处理繁琐的细节，可以直接构建推理逻辑、决定类型的统一方式及上下文的存储方式。Python的简洁性让开发者可以专注于理论的实现，帮助更好地理解和映射理论。

• [flashgordon] 对此表示赞叹，并提到自己一直想尝试进行类似的项目但多次失败，很高兴看到有人成功实现。

补充讨论：
- [b0a04gl] 强调了Python在处理类型系统建模时的优势，特别是其无编译器干扰和无需类型注解或转换的特点，使得开发者可以更专注于逻辑实现。
- 争议的焦点可能在于Python作为一种动态类型语言，在类型系统建模中的适用性和优势。这与传统上使用静态类型语言进行类型系统建模的观念形成对比。
- 各方对Bruno Oliveira研究小组的工作量和成果表示赞赏，并认可CP语言在类型系统研究中的潜在价值。

data.title: Low-Temperature Additive Manufacturing of Glass
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 林肯实验室开发了一种低温添加制造工艺，可以通过直接墨水书写技术使用多种无机材料墨水制造玻璃结构，而无需传统高温处理（通常>1000°C），仅需250°C的加热。该工艺能在室温下逐层挤出复合玻璃墨水，形成复杂形状，并具有高分辨率、高热稳定性及低收缩率。这种方法扩展了3D打印玻璃器件（如微流控系统、自由形态光学镜头或高温电子元件）的潜力。当前研究正致力于提升玻璃的光学清晰度及开发具有不同化学和电学特性的墨水。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于基于硅酸盐的3D打印材料及其工艺的分析和讨论

不同观点：
• **Kragen的观点**：评论者Kragen详细分析了该工艺的可能化学原理，推测其依赖于硅酸盐溶液和多价阳离子（如Ca⁺⁺, Mg⁺⁺等）的交联反应，且推测二氧化硅填料（如硅灰）的作用是增强材料强度并降低热膨胀系数。Kragen还提到了专利内容，指出加热过程主要是为了使材料中的水分蒸发，而不是引发其他化学反应。此外，Kragen对专利中提到的功能性填料（如碳纤维、银片）表示关注。

• **gsf_emergency_2的观点**：对专利中提到的其他无机材料（如银片）的具体性质和用途表示好奇，并质疑喷嘴尺寸为何不是更常见的400微米。

• **jiehong的观点**：简单表达了对该技术的赞赏，没有深入讨论。

44311141.article_content:
Low-Temperature Additive Manufacturing of Glass
Researchers used the low-temperature additive manufacturing process to build the glass cups above.   The optical behavior of the printed cups can be tailored by altering the chemical components of the inks.
Additive manufacturing (3D printing) holds promise for fabricating complex glass structures that would be unattainable with traditional glass manufacturing techniques. Lincoln Laboratory’s innovative approach allows additive manufacturing of multimaterial glass items without the need for costly high-temperature processing techniques. Our low-temperature technique could facilitate the widespread adoption of 3D printing for glass devices such as microfluidic systems, free-form optical lenses or fiber, and high-temperature electronic components.
KEY FEATURES
Via direct ink writing, Lincoln Laboratory uses custom inks from a variety of inorganic materials combined with a silicate solution to engineer the optical, chemical, and electrical properties of a composite
The ink ingredients are widely available, and direct ink writing affords a broad range of geometric freedom for creating glass structures
The curing process generates a stable glass structure requiring only a 250°C heat treatment instead of typical glass processing at temperatures > 1,000°C
Additive manufacturing has expanded the ability to rapidly and cost-effectively create system components. However, traditional materials — various plastic and metal composites — can produce 3D printed structures with mechanical, chemical, and thermal instabilities. Using inorganic composite glasses solves many of the instability issues and offers a promising approach to create structures with diverse shapes and properties. However, the high temperatures (greater than 1,000°C) typically used to sinter (harden) glass items have hindered the use of glass in 3D printing. High-temperature processing requires specialized equipment and is incompatible with temperature-sensitive materials and components.
Overview of custom ink engineering. Silicate ink reacts with silica particles to produce rigid silicate/silica glass composite at room temperature.
Lincoln Laboratory has demonstrated viable low-temperature 3D printing of glass structures. The process uses the direct ink writing technique to extrude, layer by layer, the Laboratory-developed multimaterial glass ink (composed of a silicate solution and nanoparticles of other inorganics) into the desired form. The process is done at room temperature. To ensure structural stability, the item is cured in a mineral oil bath heated to just 250°C. Following heat treatment, the structure is rinsed in an organic solvent to remove residual mineral, leaving a fully inorganic silica item.
Tests on items built via low-temperature additive manufacturing have shown promising results:
Structures with a high degree of resolution
High thermal stability
Minimal shrinkage
Ongoing research is focused on improving the optical clarity of the glass and creating inks that enable different chemical and electrical properties.
Contact
Bradley Duncan

data.title: Git Notes: Git's coolest, most unloved­ feature (2022)
data.author: Delgan
data.article_summary: Git notes是Git中用于附加元数据到提交的工具，允许在不修改提交本身的情况下添加信息，如审核和测试记录。它们功能强大，可用于跟踪提交时间、进行代码审查等。然而，Git笔记使用不便，界面 obscure，且GitHub在2014年停止显示提交笔记，导致其普及度低。尽管如此，Git笔记提供了离线存储代码审查数据的可能性，并能实现完全分布式的代码审查，如通过git-appraise系统。总体而言，Git笔记潜力巨大，但因使用难度和低采用率而未被广泛使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Git Notes 功能的使用、优缺点及其实际应用场景

不同观点：
• oftenwrong: 介绍 Git trailers 功能及其在一些系统（如 Gerrit）中的应用，用于附加元数据。
• homebrewer: 补充说明 Forgejo 自版本 10 起也开始支持该功能，并提供了相关链接。
• xg15: 对 Git Notes 在历史重写（如 amend、rebase）过程中的行为提出疑问，担心 Notes 会在这些操作中丢失或无法正确转移。同时也对 Notes 附加到 blob 和 tree 上的行为提出质疑，认为其表现可能与预期不符。
• kccqzy: 认为 Git Notes 只在特定情况下有用，比如为已被还原的提交添加注释。对于大多数情况，直接在提交信息中记录详细内容更为合适。
• b0a04gl: 分享了自己在工作中大量使用 Git Notes 的经验，用于记录内部代码评审和相关上下文信息，避免依赖外部工具如 Slack 或 Jira。
• noelwelsh: 指出 Git Notes 未被广泛使用主要是用户界面问题，如果 GitHub 能更好展示 Notes，其使用率会提高。
• lucasoshiro: 提到 Git 有很多被遗忘的强大功能，如 bisect、pickaxe 等，Git Notes 也是其中之一，但常被误解为仅是“高级网盘”。
• ozim: 认为 Git Notes 仅在特定团队中可能有用，对于跨部门沟通和多仓库管理并不实际。外部系统如 JIRA 更适合非开发人员使用。
• cesarb: 分享了 LibreOffice 项目使用 Git Notes 追踪 Apache OpenOffice 仓库提交的案例，尽管该实践已停止。
• EricRiese: 提到 GitLab 中一个长达 9 年的关于 Notes 支持的请求最近被关闭。
• legends2k: 指出 Git Notes 默认不推送或获取，需团队决定是否使用，其团队选择不使用该功能。
• chrishill89: 分享了其使用 Git Notes 的多种场景，包括附在补丁邮件中、记录私有测试笔记、链接到 CI、为客户编写变更日志等。
• lrvick: 介绍了自己开发的基于 Git Notes 的签名扩展工具，用于附加和验证签名。
• olejorgenb: 对含 Notes 的提交在 rebase 操作中的行为提出疑问。
• paffdragon: 分享了使用 Git Notes 实现版本控制的实践，特别是当需要强制指定版本时。

补充讨论：
• Git Notes 的实际应用场景：包括代码评审、版本控制、补丁邮件、跨团队沟通等。
• Git Notes 在操作中的持久性问题：如 rebase、amend 等操作对 Notes 的影响。
• 用户界面问题：Git Notes 未被广泛使用可能与其在常用平台上的可见性不足有关。
• 对 Git Notes 作为元数据载体的行为和预期不符的讨论，尤其是在 blob 和 tree 上的应用。

争议焦点：
• Git Notes 的实用性：一些用户认为其在特定场景下非常有用，而另一些用户则认为其应用场景有限，且可能被其他工具替代。
• Git Notes 在历史重写过程中的行为不确定性：用户担心在 rebase 或 amend 操作中 Notes 会丢失或无法正确转移。

the short of it is: theyâre cool for appending notes from automated
