Git notes are almost a secret.
Theyâre buried by their own distressing usability.
But git notes are continually rediscovered by engineers trying to
stash metadata inside git.
Sun, 30 Oct 2022 11:05
@simonw
Git notes are powerful tools.
And they could solve
so many problemsâif only they were better known and easier to use.
ð§
What are git notes?
A common use of git notes is tacking metadata onto commits.
Once a commit cements itself in gitâs historyâthatâs it. Itâs
impossible to amend a commit message buried deep in a repoâs log
1
.
But git notes enable you to amend new information about old commits
in a special namespace. And theyâre capable of so much more.
Notes stow metadata about anything tracked by
git
âany object: commits, blobs, and trees. All without futzing
with the object itself.
You add notes to the latest commit in a repo like this:
git notes add -m 'Acked-by: <tyler@tylercipriani.com>'
And then it shows up in
git log
:
commit 1ef8b30ab7fc218ccc85c9a6411b1d2dd2925a16
Author: Tyler Cipriani <thcipriani@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Nov 17 16:51:43 2022 -0700
Initial commit
Notes:
Acked-by: <tyler@tylercipriani.com>
ð¥¾
Git notes in the wild
The git project itself offers an example of git notes in the wild.
They link each commit to its discussion on their mailing list.
For example:
commit 00f09d0e4b1826ee0519ea64e919515032966450
Author: <redacted>
Date:   Thu Jan 28 02:05:55 2010 +0100
bash: support 'git notes' and its subcommands
...
Notes (amlog):
Message-Id: <1264640755-22447-1-git-send-email-szeder@ira.uka.de>
This commitâs notes point intrepid users to the
thread
where this patch was discussed
.
Other folks are using notes for things like:
Tracking time spent per commit or branch
Adding review and testing information to git log
And even fully distributed code review
ð¦
Storing code reviews and test results in git
notes
Here is a plea for all forges: make code review metadata available
offline, inside git.
The
reviewnotes
plugin for Gerrit
2
is an example of how to do this
well. It makes it easy to see who reviewed code in git log:
git fetch origin refs/notes/review:refs/notes/review
git log --show-notes=review
The command above shows me all the standard git log info alongside
information about what tests ran and who reviewed the code. All without
forcing me into my browser.
commit d1d17908d2a97f057887a4afbd99f6c40be56849
Author: User <user@example.com>
Date:   Sun Mar 27 18:10:51 2022 +0200
Change the thing
Notes (review):
Verified+1: SonarQube Bot
Verified+2: jenkins-bot
Code-Review+2: Reviewer Human <reviewerhuman@wikimedia.org>
Submitted-by: jenkins-bot
Submitted-at: Tue, 14 Jun 2022 21:59:58 +0000
Reviewed-on: https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/c/mediawiki/core/+/774005
Project: mediawiki/core
Branch: refs/heads/master
ð
Distributed code review
inside
git notes
Motivated hackers can knead and extend git notes. Using them as
distributed storage for any madcap idea.
Someone at Google cobbled together a full-on code review system
teetering atop git notes called
git-appraise
.
Its authors have declared it a âfully distributed code
reviewââindependent of GitHub, GitLab, or any other code forge.
This system lets you:
Request review of a change
Comment on a change
Review and merge a change
And you can do all this from your local computer, even if GitHub is
down.
Plus, itâs equipped with an affectedly unaesthetic web interface, if
thatâs your thing.
The git-appraise web interface, in all
its NaN-line-numbering glory.
ð­
No one uses git notes
Git notes are a pain to use.
And GitHub
opted to stop
displaying commit notes in 2014
without much explanation.
For commits, you can make viewing and adding notes easier using fancy
options in your gitconfig
3
. But for storing notes about blobs
or trees? Forget it. Youâd need to be comfortable rooting around in
gitâs
plumbing
first.
So, for now:
git notes are relegated to obscurity
.
Forever hamstrung by an obscure and clunky interface and limited
adoptionâI often forget theyâre there.
ð½
Forge independence
Git is a distributed code review system. But much of the value of git
repos ends up locked into forges, like GitHub.
Git notes are a path toward an alternative.
Git distributes the history of a piece of code.
Git notes
could make it possible to distribute the history of an entire
project.
Without having to endure the
perils
of a force push
, anyway.
â©ï¸
The code review system used for
a
couple
of
bigish
projects
.
â©ï¸
Noteably by automagically fetching
notes and displaying them in
git log
via:
$ git config --add \
remote.origin.fetch \
'+refs/notes/*:refs/notes/*'
$ git con

data.title: LibRedirect – Redirects popular sites to alternative privacy-friendly frontends
data.author: riffraff
data.article_summary: LibRedirect是一款网页扩展程序，旨在将YouTube、Instagram、Reddit、TikTok等网站的访问重定向到注重隐私的替代前端。例如，YouTube可重定向到Invidious、Piped等，Twitter到Nitter，Reddit到Libreddit等。该工具支持多种平台，包括Twitter、Twitch、IMDb、SoundCloud等，提供更注重用户隐私的替代服务。用户可通过其官网下载、查看源代码、获取文档及捐赠支持项目。该扩展有助于避免原平台的隐私追踪问题，提升网络浏览的隐私保护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：隐私重定向工具及相关技术方案的有效性、安全性及其实际应用中的问题

不同观点：
• [pndy] 认为隐私重定向工具在防止不良网站方面有其价值，但目前面临实例快速失效的问题，尤其是因为大网站和服务开始反击，阻止重定向。同时提到最早的扩展如Privacy Redirect曾起到作用，但被不法分子利用。
• [jamesponddotco] 提供了一个关于隐私保护前端的列表，认为这些前端仍然有效，尽管很久未更新。

• [mikae1] 推荐使用Redirector扩展来设置重定向，认为这是更方便的选择。

• [romaaeterna] 怀疑"隐私友好"的前端可能被用来追踪用户数据，指出实例主机的好意并不可靠。

• [kelvinjps10] 表示喜欢这些扩展工具。
• [johnisgood] 对在Android上运行Proxigram表示怀疑。
• [nightcoders] 感谢提供的有用信息。
• [snvzz] 指出某些工具无法设置任意目标，特别是对于自托管实例的用户来说，这是一个问题。

• 隐私重定向工具的安全性和可靠性，尤其是实例快速失效和被不法分子利用的问题。

44344246.article_summary: LibRedirect是一款网页扩展程序，旨在将YouTube、Instagram、Reddit、TikTok等网站的访问重定向到注重隐私的替代前端。例如，YouTube可重定向到Invidious、Piped等，Twitter到Nitter，Reddit到Libreddit等。该工具支持多种平台，包括Twitter、Twitch、IMDb、SoundCloud等，提供更注重用户隐私的替代服务。用户可通过其官网下载、查看源代码、获取文档及捐赠支持项目。该扩展有助于避免原平台的隐私追踪问题，提升网络浏览的隐私保护。

data.title: Show HN: I'm building an app to replace Overleaf and Notion
data.author: WolfOliver
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一款类似于Notion的应用的各种评价和建议

不同观点：
• diziet认为该应用不支持离线使用是一个主要缺点，并希望开发者解决这一问题。
• roetlich询问该应用与Typst相比如何，关注与其他工具的比较。
• prezjordan对应用的文本编辑器表示赞赏，但建议使用现成的文本编辑器以处理跨段选择和并发编辑问题，避免开发中的困难。
• rishabhdev2700简单表达了对应用界面干净的赞赏。
• blural对应用的名称不满意，并提出了一些替代名称建议。
• GlacierFox担心该应用的购买模式是否是一次性购买，还是存在隐藏的付费升级条款。
• MDWolinski指出许多Notion的替代品忽视了Notion将数据库集成到文档中的独特功能，认为这是这些替代品所缺乏的关键特性，并希望有一个开源替代品。
• johnecheck认为该应用不是他所期待的开源Notion/Obsidian竞争者，并指出在Android Firefox上的显示问题。
• jkhdigital分享了自己作为 PhD学生对类似工具的需求，表示该应用解决了其在研究工作中遇到的多个问题，但自己最终选择了Obsidian，因为只想专注于研究而不被工具问题困扰。

补充讨论：
• 用户对应用的文本编辑功能、名称、购买模式以及与Notion和其他工具的比较都有不同的看法。
• 争议的焦点在于该应用是否能真正替代Notion，特别是在数据库集成和开源方面的功能。
• 一些用户对应用在特定浏览器上的显示问题提出了技术性反馈。
• jkhdigital的长评提供了对学术研究人员需求的深入洞察，强调了工具易用性和功能集成的重要性。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国与伊朗的紧张关系，特别是关于伊朗核问题、战争可能性以及美国政府的责任与行为。

不同观点：
• 一些评论指出特朗普及其政府在处理国际事务中的行为和态度。例如，[ioa8w35l8aw]提到其家人对特朗普处理乌克兰战争和伊朗问题的态度转变，暗示了公众对战争与和平看法的易变性。同时，[croes]将可能的军事行动类比为特朗普的“任务完成”时刻，暗含对特朗普处理国际危机能力的质疑。

• [adfm]关注美国国会在宣战中的角色，并提出行政部门（如CEO）越权的问题，质疑如何确保问责性，特别是当责任像“烫手山芋”一样被推来推去时。

• [cypherpunks01]和[1234letshaveatw]提到伊朗核协议及其现状，暗示对当前局势的困惑，并提供了相关新闻链接以补充信息。

• [bawolff]和[sherburt3]讨论了伊朗核设施的铀浓缩水平及其影响，认为如果浓缩程度在60%以下且设施被摧毁，可能不会造成太大影响。

• [daft_pink]和[andrewmcwatters]提到国际社会对伊朗核活动的监控能力以及可能的物资囤积行为，暗示政府对核材料的严密监控和高价值情报的获取。

• [diego_moita]将当前局势与历史事件对比，提到美国以往因错误情报发动的战争（如伊拉克的“大规模杀伤性武器”），并使用“美帝国主义”来描述美国的国际行为，暗示对美国外交政策的批评。

• [zzzeek]和[siliconc0w]批评了美国在军事行动前缺乏隐秘性，指出提前泄露攻击计划可能导致对方有时间转移关键设备和物资，降低行动效果。

• [jopsen]质疑军事打击的有效性，认为摧毁核设施并不能阻止其重建，并批评特朗普破坏了美国数十年来积累的外交成果。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到核协议的历史和现状，显示出对伊朗核问题的关注和对国际协议有效性的质疑。
• 对美国政府在国际事务中责任和行为的批评与质疑贯穿整个讨论，尤其是在战争与和平问题上的决策过程。
• 部分评论带有讽刺和幽默，如[zzzek]引用《孙子兵法》和[croes]对“任务完成”的类比，增加了讨论的情感色彩。

争议焦点：
• 美国政府在处理伊朗核问题上的透明度与隐秘性之间的平衡。
• 军事打击的有效性和长期影响，特别是对核设施的摧毁是否能达到预期目标。
• 美国在国际事务中的角色和责任，以及如何确保问责性和避免越权行为。

data.title: Fairphone 6 is switching to a new design that's even more sustainable
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: Fairphone 6的泄露渲染图展示了其模块化设计，便于更换组件。新机型预计采用平边设计和霓虹主题的电源键，有黑、白、绿三色可选。预计6月25日发布，起价€549，配置包括6.31英寸pOLED 120Hz显示屏、Snapdragon 7s Gen 3处理器、4415mAh电池等。该设备强调可持续性，易于维修和更换部件，符合欧盟的可修复性和耐用性认证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：智能手机的设计与功能取舍，包括指纹识别、可修复性、模块化设计、硬件升级、尺寸、以及市场供应等问题。

不同观点：
• **指纹识别 vs. 面部识别**：
  - godelski 认为背部指纹识别是最快捷的解锁方式，不理解为什么人们更喜欢 Face ID。
  
• **手机可修复性与模块化设计**：
  - userbinator 批评现代智能手机自2016年以来在可修复性上大幅倒退，如电池不可更换、缺乏 microSD 卡槽和耳机插孔，并怀念以前更易于自定义和 root 的安卓手机。
  - strangecasts 赞赏 Fairphone 的可修复性，但对其未及时提供 Android 14 更新表示不满，同时对取消耳机插孔感到遗憾。
  - rglullis 认为 Fairphone 应像 Framework 笔记本一样，采用标准化部件，实现更强的可升级性和模块化设计，而不是每两年推出一个妥协的设备。
  - TheCraiggers 表示希望 Fairphone 能在美国市场销售，提供更多选择。
  
• **硬件性能与使用寿命**：
  - msgodel 建议采用支持主线 Linux 的 SoC，以延长手机使用寿命，避免几年后被淘汰。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vera C. Rubin 天文台及其科学价值、技术挑战和未来前景

不同观点：
• jcims 认为维基百科上的文章质量很高，并提到文章中的参考文献包含大量细节。他还关注望远镜焦平面的平整性问题，并提到图像处理根据时间尺度分为三种：即时、每日和每年。特别指出，即时预警系统能在60秒内处理大型图像，这是一个重要的软件工程挑战。同时，提到数据处理将在某保密设施进行，以编辑可能泄露秘密资产的事件。
• dekhn 强调Rubin天文台的"广视场"观测能力，认为这种观测能产生大量有用的数据，有助于改进宇宙学模型。他还提到该项目耗时长久，保持长期关注是一个挑战。
• krunck 关注天文台的 asteroid 检测能力，并分享相关新闻链接。
• mjsweet 分享个人经历，提到Google曾参与数据处理，并对天文台项目的长期发展表示关注。
• perihelions 提供SDSS视图以对比Rubin天文台的曝光深度，帮助理解其观测能力。
• WD-42 强调每晚产生的大量数据对科学研究的重要性，并指出社区正在建设基础设施以高效处理这些数据，但仍需努力。
• NitpickLawyer 对天文台能检测移动天体（如小行星和星际物体）表示兴奋，特别提到对Oumuamua和Borisov类物体的早期预警能力。

补充讨论：
• -warren 和 ludsan 分享了具体的星系和天体图像链接，展示了天文台观测的具体实例。
• runako 感叹深场图像中任何光点都可能是恒星、星系或星系团，并提出关于天文台在资金结束后如何维持运作的问题，特别是智利接管项目的可行性。
• mapt 对M61星系中的微弱光 tendril表示好奇，提出了天文现象解释的问题。
• w10-1 提到图像的颗粒感问题，质疑是否进行过暗场减法处理及其在长曝光中的作用。
• kdamica 和 ramijames 简短感叹了图像中丰富的星体和引力透镜现象。
• dang 提供相关纽约时报文章链接，扩展了对Rubin天文台的讨论。

争议焦点：
• 数据处理的即时性和保密性之间的平衡。jcims 提到数据处理在保密设施进行，以保护秘密资产，这引发了对数据公开性和透明度的关注。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：2025年4月28日伊比利亚半岛及周边地区的电网崩溃事件的原因和解决方案

不同观点：
• AnotherGoodName认为，澳大利亚曾经历过类似的电网崩溃事件，通过在关键位置部署锂电池储能系统成功解决。这些系统不仅防止了更多停电事件，还为拥有者带来了可观利润。澳大利亚正在建设更多的电池储能系统，并有文章建议欧洲应效仿以避免类似问题。
• diggan指出事件的根本原因是电压过高导致的“链式反应”，系统缺乏动态电压控制能力，形成了正反馈回路，导致多个发电站相继脱网。他还建议先阅读报告的附录以了解基本概念，有助于理解报告内容。
• fuoqi认为，可再生能源在电网中的比例过高是导致不稳定的主要原因，尽管可以通过昂贵的措施解决，但超过一定比例后电网架构会变得不稳定。他将此与之前被反对的评论联系起来，指出可再生能源对电网的潜在影响。
• tofflos对报告中关于网络安全和数字系统的十三页内容感到不满，认为应更多关注电力系统操作问题。
• rcarmo指出，报告在第130页才开始有可读的总结，之前的内容详细解释了累积的不稳定性。他担心媒体只会关注网络安全部分，而忽略真正的技术问题。
• robocat解释了发电机通过监测电压、频率和无功功率来调整输出，但由于测量不准确和网络操作员的判断失误，导致不稳定性。他质疑是否有国家在电力网络控制系统设计上更优。
• londons_explore认为报告没有明确识别根本原因，希望看到模拟分析和具体预防措施，并建议定期进行模拟以预防未来事件。
• ranguna好奇是否单个发电厂与自然振荡共同作用引发了严重问题，并提到葡萄牙可能因负电价导致过多需求，但不确定其对整个事件的影响。
• rocqua关注电压振荡的起因，以及为何高电压会导致发电机切断，并探讨了可能的反馈源。
• decimalenough对报告的非保密版本感到好奇，想知道保密版本中有什么未公开的内容。
• JanneVee将事件的复杂性与RIP路由协议的振荡问题类比，认为没有单一解决方案。
• gred对报告中大量关于多因素认证和IT安全的建议感到不解，认为这些与事件核心问题无关，质疑是否为了增加页数。

补充讨论：
- 关于电网中可再生能源角色的争议，特别是其对电网稳定性的影响。
- 对报告中网络安全部分的讨论过多，技术细节和根本原因分析不足。
- 对具体振荡起因及发电机脱网机制的技术探讨。
- 不同国家在电网控制和设计上的比较。

data.title: Environmental Impacts of Artificial Intelligence
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 这份报告探讨了人工智能（AI）对环境的广泛影响。尽管AI技术正迅速改变世界，推动诸多领域的进步，但其应用也带来了新的环境挑战。报告共55页，详细分析了AI在能源消耗、碳排放、资源开采和电子废物等方面的影响。AI系统的训练和运行需要大量计算资源，导致能源使用增加，进而加剧碳足迹。此外，AI硬件的生产和处置也会产生环境负担。报告呼吁在发展AI技术的同时，关注其可持续性，以减少对环境的负面影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI与能源消耗及环境影响的关系

不同观点：
• **支持增加核能以应对能源需求**：imnotlost认为应建设更多核电站来解决能源问题，并将此与全球其他昂贵的军事项目对比，表明有能力投资能源项目。

• **对比AI与娱乐设备能耗**：elpocko指出，全球大量GPU用于娱乐目的（如游戏）的能耗远高于AI的能耗，但人们并未对此表示关注，质疑对AI能耗的特别关注是否合理。

• **AI能耗的潜在环境影响**：Zaylan认为，AI的能耗问题尚未得到足够重视，随着模型规模增长，其对环境的影响可能会比预期更快地显现出来。

• **对AI与电动车能耗的双重标准**：platevoltage指出，有些人对电动车和AI在能耗问题上的态度不一致，质疑为何对AI的能耗问题没有同样的担忧。

• **自动化与生态限制**：narrator预测，自动化将加速资源的消耗，并可能导致经济增长达到生态极限。同时，提出需要“自由市场生态学”来解决这些问题。

• **环保组织的作用与影响**：
  ◦ yomismoaqui调侃环保组织如Greenpeace是否仍有影响力。
  ◦ grej批评Greenpeace反对核能的立场，认为这是一种政治选择，可能使环境问题恶化。

• **AI能效与未来发展**：dydghks2033认为AI能耗问题值得关注，特别是如果AI推理的能耗持续增长，未来在AGI部署中，能效可能成为关键问题。

• **能源使用与政策干预**：djoldman引用Greenpeace的建议，指出AI公司应披露能耗信息并承担环境责任，同时质疑是否应通过政策干预人们使用能源的方式。

• **对环保行动的双重标准**：lenerdenator认为，历史上并未重视其他产业的环境影响，现在也不太可能特别关注AI，尽管从道理上应该关注。

• **核能与环保争议**：option质疑Greenpeace反对核能的环境影响，暗示可能导致更严重的生态问题。

• **AI与其他产业的比较**：MoonGhost认为，在讨论AI能耗时应全面比较AI辅助与传统人工方式的能耗，而不仅仅是单方面考虑AI的能耗问题。

• **全球环保责任分配**：sergiotapia认为，在印度和中国等国未解决塑料污染等问题前，美国和欧洲的环保措施显得不公平，并将AI能耗问题视为次要问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是对AI能耗的双重标准及与其他产业能耗的比较。
• 另一个焦点是核能的利用及其在解决能源需求与环境问题中的角色。
• 环保组织如Greenpeace的作用及其政策建议也引发了讨论，尤其是在核能问题上的立场。
• 自动化与经济增长的生态限制问题被提出，但未有详细解决方案。
• 不同地区在全球环保责任分配上的分歧反映了环保问题的复杂性与全球性。

data.title: Resurrecting flip phone typing as a Linux driver
data.author: foxmoss
data.article_summary: **LibT9** 是一个用C语言编写的开源库，用于创建T9输入法系统。该库遵循LGPL-3.0许可证，只需基础的C标准库即可编译，额外功能如CLI工具需要ncurses和cmake。用户可以通过驱动程序在Linux上运行，或作为命令行工具使用，还提供了网页演示。项目鼓励贡献，未来计划包括标点支持和IBus驱动集成。C代码占比99.9%。项目文档和演示可访问：[foxmoss.github.io/libt9/](foxmoss.github.io/libt9/)。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：T9输入法在现代设备中的应用和其优劣对比

不同观点：
• akdev1l认为电视遥控器应该加入T9输入法支持，目前的输入方式繁琐且不方便，例如需要扫描QR码或通过应用输入。
• throw0101c解释了T9输入法是什么，并提供了维基百科的链接以帮助不熟悉T9的用户理解。
• humanfromearth9怀念在诺基亚3310上使用T9输入法快速打字的体验，并指出在现代智能手机上打字时，由于自动纠错的不可靠性，常常需要犹豫是滑动输入还是逐字输入。
• jesprenj指出T9在美国普遍使用，但在斯洛文尼亚并没有广泛应用，部分原因是默认未启用且对斯洛文尼亚语的支持不佳，人们因此学会了快速打字。
• fimdomeio强调了T9键盘的一个优点，即无需看屏幕就能单手盲打，这对很多人来说非常方便。
• wkirby表达了对T9输入法在现代设备中回归的渴望，甚至梦想为Apple Watch设计一个带有T9输入法的蓝牙键盘外壳。
• cortesoft以幽默的方式指出，因为过去无法负担短信费用，所以没有机会练习在老式手机上快速打字。

补充讨论：
• jauntywundrkind对一个T9输入法的网页演示感到困惑，询问如何查看输入数字后转换的单词。

争议焦点：
• 不同地区对T9输入法的接受度和使用情况存在差异，例如在美国普遍使用，而在斯洛文尼亚则不常见。
• 现代设备输入方式的多样性与T9输入法的便捷性之间的对比，用户对不同输入方式的偏好不同。

data.title: Ocarina of Time Randomizer
data.author: nickswalker
data.article_summary: 《Ocarina of Time》随机物品生成器（OoTR）通过打乱游戏内物品的位置，提供更具动态性的游玩体验。每个随机种子都经过逻辑设计，确保无需使用漏洞即可完成，并避免卡关。随机选项包括道具、钥匙、入口、商人价格等众多元素。社区提供了详细的教程和工具帮助新手入门，并不断开发新功能。玩家还可以加入Discord社区参与竞速和比赛，或观看相关赛事。最新开发版本为v8.3.17，项目仍在积极更新中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ocarina of Time（OOT）随机化器及其相关多游戏随机化器的玩法、技术实现和社区资源

不同观点：
• lbourdages认为OOT随机化器每次都是新的谜题，且有很多质量上的改进（如推箱子更快、跳过过场动画），使其对熟悉游戏的玩家来说更具乐趣。
• LelouBil介绍了一个多游戏随机化器平台Archipelago，玩家可以在不同游戏中互相寻找物品，并认为这种玩法非常有趣且令人惊叹。
• pimeys喜欢在Twitch上观看黑暗之魂随机化器的运行，特别是相关的视频内容。
• maxvu提到了一种结合Ocarina of Time和Majora's Mask的随机化器，特别提到“容器外观匹配内容”选项，使得游戏运行更加动态，并提供了相关网站链接。
• minimaxir推荐了Twitch主播Zfg的OOT随机化器直播，并分享了一个无逻辑运行的示例视频。
• proteal关注如何确保每个种子都能无漏洞完成，并对网站声明生成有效种子的效率表示好奇。
• sylens认为Ocarina of Time本身的游戏设计中包含了一些序列破坏元素，这使得随机化器玩法更加有趣和多样化。
• bevr1337询问是否仍然需要获取合法的OOT ROM才能使用随机化器，特别是在手机上操作时。
• GardenLetter27建议直接在Ship of Harkinian上进行随机化器玩法，并指出这样可以在Steam Deck上完美运行。
• squigz提到开始玩Wind Waker HD随机化器运行，认为这种玩法大大增强了游戏体验，特别是在多次玩过原版游戏后。
• 2OEH8eoCRo0推荐了Good Old Days Gaming的随机化器运行视频资源。

补充讨论：
• 玩家对不同游戏的随机化器玩法表现出浓厚兴趣，包括Ocarina of Time、Majora's Mask、黑暗之魂和Wind Waker HD。
• 技术实现和质量改进是玩家讨论的重要方面，特别是如何确保随机化器种子的有效性和游戏体验的提升。
• 社区资源和推荐，如相关网站、直播和视频资源，为玩家提供了丰富的信息和参与途径。
• 玩家对使用随机化器的实际操作问题也有关注，如ROM的获取和平台的选择。

争议焦点：
• 如何确保每个随机化器种子都能无漏洞完成，这是proteal提出的一个技术性问题，涉及到随机化器的生成算法和效率。

data.title: I ported pigz from Unix to Windows
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者将Unix下的多线程压缩工具pigz移植到Windows系统的过程。由于pigz主要使用标准C库，并且依赖于pthreads和dirent等Unix特有API，作者通过使用现有的pthread-win32库解决线程问题，并找到一个Windows下的dirent API移植版来解决目录读取问题。对于其他如文件状态函数名不同（如stat与_stat）以及缺少某些类型定义的问题，作者通过定义兼容头文件wincompat.h来解决。此外，作者使用Premake工具自动生成Visual Studio项目文件，简化了构建系统的配置。最终，借助已有兼容层和工具，这次移植工作相对顺利。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebKit的libpas内存分配器在Windows上的移植及其相关技术讨论

不同观点：

补充讨论：

争议焦点：
• 该移植的实际应用价值，尤其是在现代多线程服务器环境中的优势，存在争议。jqpabc123对其有效性提出质疑，而igrunert则分享了具体的实现细节和代码量信息。

44327204.article_content:
Home
How I ported pigz from Unix to Windows
edit
I just finished
porting
pigz
from Unix to Windows (you can download
pre-compiled binaries
). This article describes how I did it.
Pigz was clearly written with Unix in mind, with no thought given to cross-platform portability.
Thankfully, it’s a relatively simple, command-line program that sticks to using standard C library.
Porting pthreads
Pigz uses pthreads for threading. Porting pthreads code to Windows would be a nightmare. Lucky me: someone already did all the hard work and
implemented pthreads APIs
on top of Windows API, in only 20.000 lines of code. It seems to Just Work.
Porting dirent
Another Unix-only API that pigz uses is
dirent.h
, for reading the content of directories. I was lucky again: someone created a
Windows port of dirent APIs
.
Misc fixes
There are few functions that pigz uses that are present in Visual Studio’s C library, but under a different name (e.g.
stat
is
_stat
,
fstat
is
_fstat
etc.). This is easily fixed with a
#define
.
Visual C doesn’t define
ssize_t
and
PATH_MAX
. A
typedef
here, a
#define
there solves those problems.
I consolidated all such fixes in a single
wincompat.h
file.
Pigz
#include
s some .h files that are only available under Unix. I used
#ifndef _WIN32
around those.
Build system
Pigz uses standard Unix build tools: gcc and make.
While there are ports of GNU make to Windows and gcc-based compilers that can generate windows binaries (mingw), most Windows developers prefer using Visual Studio IDE.
Creating Visual Studio project files from scratch is time consuming and annoying, especially when you want to support multiple versions of Visual Studio.
Premake
makes it easier. It’s a meta-build system: you write a
text file
that defines the project, which files to compile, compilation flags etc. and premake generates Visual Studio files from that description.
Premake supports Visual Studio 2008 and 2010 (and 2012 supports 2010 project files via conversion).
Conclusion
As far as porting goes, this one was easy thanks to existing efforts that created compatibility shims for the hard parts.
Premake is an interesting tool that allows to save time creating and maintaining Visual Studio projects.

data.title: GitHub CEO: manual coding remains key despite AI boom
data.author: andrewstetsenko
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在编程中的应用及其对程序员工作的影响

不同观点：
• **AI生成的代码不可完全替代人工**：[agentultra] 认为自然语言不如编程语言精确，AI生成的代码需要人工审查和编辑。独立研究显示Copilot可能增加软件错误率，这可能与人们对AI的过度依赖有关。
• **AI擅长处理常见模式但缺乏深层理解**：[sysmax] 指出AI能高效处理常见代码模式，但在处理逻辑差异（如if和switch语句）时可能忽略细微差别，导致代码表面看似正确但实际有误。
• **AI目前相当于初级或中级开发者**：[exiguus] 根据经验认为，AI目前在处理复杂任务时效率不高，且在过去两年中没有显著进步。
• **AI不具备真正的思考能力**：[taysix] 通过实例说明AI在处理特定任务时可能出现错误，如忽略具体指令，表明AI并不具备真正的思考能力。
• **形式语言优于自然语言**：[layer8] 强调编程语言提供的精确性和可控性是自然语言无法替代的，人类需要通过理解和操作代码来控制程序行为。
• **对“手动编码”的负面看法**：[CoffeeOnWrite] 对“手动编码”这一术语表示不满，认为贬低了人类编码的重要性，建议使用更中立的词汇。
• **AI工具对产品经理和团队领导的影响**：[bad_haircut72] 认为产品经理和团队领导看待开发者与AI的互动类似于用户与LLM的互动，AI生成的代码需要多次修订才能使用。
• **AI的目标是自动化而非增强**：[boshalfoshal] 认为AI公司的最终目标是实现软件工程的完全自动化，而不仅仅是增强开发者能力，以降低人力成本。
• **AI工具提高生产力但不能取代开发者**：[strict9] 指出，尽管AI工具提高了开发者的生产力，但代码仍需开发者审查和修改，开发者的角色并未被完全取代。
• **对AI工具过度依赖的问题**：[h4kunamata] 提到开发者过度依赖AI工具，复制粘贴AI生成的代码而不理解其原理，可能导致质量问题。
• **对AI工具的积极看法**：[mewc] 认为对AI工具的抱怨和悲观态度反而为AI工具的开发提供了更好的信号，AI的发展空间仍然很大。
• **写作代码是思考的过程**：[mycocola] 认为编写代码是思考和创造的过程，过度依赖AI工具可能导致程序员忽略高质量软件开发的重要部分。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI工具是否能真正替代人类开发者，特别是在处理复杂逻辑和深层次理解方面。
- 对“手动编码”这一术语的不同看法，以及对AI工具在实际应用中局限性的讨论。
- AI工具在提高生产力和自动化方面的潜力与当前实际能力之间的差距。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Discord平台上的BotGhost服务可能被关闭及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **czk** 认为，Discord可能担心像BotGhost这样的服务能够记录大量私人频道数据，并可能出售这些数据用于AI模型训练，从而对平台构成威胁。还提到了过去类似服务"Spy Pet"的例子。
• **nxrabl** 提到了一个具体的安全漏洞，该漏洞涉及BotGhost服务泄露用户bot tokens的问题，尽管漏洞被迅速修补，但开发者试图掩盖并拒绝重置可能受影响的tokens。
• **throwaway7679** 认为，技术细节和许可证协议等都不重要，问题在于Discord作为一个反复无常且不负责任的公司，BotGhost在与Discord的交涉中缺乏筹码。
• **pavel_lishin** 对"no-code"的概念感到困惑，质疑BotGhost如何在没有代码的情况下运作，并担心如果服务关闭，用户数据将永久丢失，且没有备份。
• **RainyDayTmrw** 认为开发者低估了安全问题的影响，特别是在token泄露事件中。同时批评Discord在执行政策时的不一致性和公关驱动的方式。
• **Banditoz** 从另一个角度提出，如果服务托管Discord bot并存储大量tokens，一旦泄露，攻击者可以对多个Discord服务器进行破坏。同时质疑为何类似服务的Mee6没有被处理。
• **mslansn** 建议将代码发布在docker镜像中，以便用户继续使用产品。
• **apt-apt-apt-apt** 将此事件与苹果等垄断平台的做法相比较，认为Discord可能因为竞争或对业务不利而选择关闭BotGhost。
• **merb** 认为Discord没有为用户提供授权这些平台的方法，这是一个非常愚蠢的设计问题。
• **koakuma-chan** 表示因为类似问题已经几乎停止使用Discord，转向Reddit。
• **pnw** 认为Discord正在加速开发者关系策略，类似于苹果和谷歌的做法，但这种反应不会让开发者对在Discord平台上继续开发感到安心。
• **linotype** 认为将竞争对手曝光出来是不合适的。
• **encom** 以讽刺的语气表示对可能的关闭事件感到兴奋。
• **ranger_danger** 描述了自己多年来无法正常使用Discord的经历，每次尝试都会遇到各种问题和自动封禁。
• **immibis** 提供了一个普遍的PSA，指出"服务条款"和" breach notice"通常没有法律效力，更多是商业决策，Discord是否允许某个服务存在取决于其对自身利益的考量。

补充讨论：

data.title: First methane-powered sea spiders found crawling on the ocean floor
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 科学家在美国西海岸深海发现三种新的海蜘蛛物种，属于Sericosura属，它们通过与细菌共生获取甲烷作为食物来源。这些细菌附着在海蜘蛛的外骨骼上，将甲烷和氧气转化为糖和脂肪供海蜘蛛食用。这种独特的营养获取方式首次在海蜘蛛中被观察到。由于深海无光，微生物依靠化学能而非阳光生存，海蜘蛛则通过"耕种"这些细菌获取营养。研究表明，这些海蜘蛛可能还将甲烷燃料细菌传递给后代作为食物。这一发现不仅揭示了深海生物的独特生存策略，还暗示这些生物可能在阻止甲烷释放到大气中、减缓全球变暖方面发挥重要作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：海蜘蛛与细菌的共生关系及其背后的生态和科学意义

不同观点：
• [apollo_mojave] 和 [leptons] 对海蜘蛛通过身体表面"吃"细菌的类比表示调侃，认为将鸡蛋和皮肤上的细菌作比较不太恰当，但同时也觉得这个形象很有趣。
• [whycome] 指出微生物做了所有的工作但却未被重视，并提出是否可以将这种机制应用于天然甲烷生产者如腐烂物质或奶牛上，以探索实际应用的可能性。
• [Caelus9] 强调了这个发现背后的深远意义，即生物可以直接利用地球化学能量而不依赖阳光，这揭示了一个由甲烷而非光合作用驱动的新型生态系统。
• [palmfacehn] 对深海黑烟囱生态系统表达了兴趣，并进一步思考了在地球深部高温高压条件下微生物生态系统的可能性及其对碳氢化合物沉积的影响。
• [dmos62] 和 [VikingCoder] 以幽默的方式描述了这个现象，认为"甲烷驱动的海蜘蛛"这一表述具有蒸汽朋克风格，并将其比作科幻小说中的场景。
• [bookofjoe] 引用了相关研究文章，提供了科学依据，强调了甲烷驱动的海蜘蛛在深海甲烷渗漏中的重要性。
• [WalterBright] 提出了一个更为科幻的观点，询问是否可以在土卫六的甲烷海洋中孕育生命，探讨这一发现对地外生命的启示。
• [pastureofplenty] 对海蜘蛛如何呼吸提出了疑问，关注其生理机制。

• [yieldcrv] 进一步讨论了这种共生关系的细节，强调了即使80%的细菌被吃掉，剩下的20%仍然能够生存和繁殖，这是一种值得的交换。

• 主要在于如何定义和理解这种共生关系，[thaumasiotes]将其称为"养殖"形式，而其他人可能有不同看法。
• 另外，[pstuart]对甲烷开采的担忧反映了科学发现可能带来的环境和社会影响。

44338309.article_content:
Scientists say the newly found Sericosura sea spiders may pass methane-fueled bacteria to their hatchlings as an easy source of food.
Shana Goffredi
Sign up for CNN’s Wonder Theory science newsletter.
Explore the universe with news on fascinating discoveries, scientific advancements and more
.
CNN
—
Heat-trapping methane may be best known for the dangers it poses to humans and Earth’s atmosphere, but in the dark depths of the ocean, the greenhouse gas is a nourishing meal for some of the world’s most mysterious creatures, new research suggests.
Scientists say they have discovered three previously unknown, unnamed species of sea spider off the US West Coast that could be teaming up with bacteria to thrive off gas bubbling from the seafloor in sparsely
studied
marine habitats known as
methane seeps
thousands of feet below the ocean’s surface.
In this symbiotic relationship, bacteria take up real estate on the spider’s exoskeletons, and in return, the microbes convert carbon-rich methane and oxygen into sugars and fats the spiders can eat, according to
a study
published Monday in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
“Just like you would eat eggs for breakfast, the sea spider grazes the surface of its body, and it munches all those bacteria for nutrition,” said Shana Goffredi, a professor and chair of biology at Occidental College in Los Angeles and the study’s principal investigator. This unique nutrition strategy has never been observed in sea spiders before, she said.
BHUBANESHWAR, ODISHA, INDIA  SEPTEMBER 12: As part of India's Deep Ocean Mission, polymetallic nodules rich in Manganese, Copper, Cobalt, Nickle harvested to mine critical minerals seen here in on September 12, 2023 at Bhubaneshwar, India.  (Photo by Pallava Bagla/Getty Images)
Pallava Bagla/Corbis/Getty Images
Related article
Scientists say they found oxygen where it shouldn’t be. Now, the hunt is on for more answers
Other species of sea spider share more in common with their terrestrial cousins, using large tubelike fangs to capture, immobilize and suck the fluids from soft-bodied prey, such as jellyfish, Goffredi explained. But lab observations of the newfound species, part of the Sericosura genus, revealed they lack the necessary appendages to capture prey, making them more akin to farmers harvesting methane-fueled bacteria from their own bodies.
It’s possible the spiders and their hitchhiking microbes play a crucial role in preventing methane — a natural gas thought to exacerbate global warming — from reaching Earth’s atmosphere, according to Goffredi.
“While the deep sea feels really far away, all organisms are interconnected. Even though they’re small, these animals have a big impact in that environment,” Goffredi said. “We can’t ever hope to sustainably (use) the oceans if we don’t really understand the oceans.”
The methane diet may be good for everyone
Light from the sun doesn’t reach the deep-sea ecosystem where the newly described Sericosura spider species make their home.
To survive in this dark environment, microbes evolved to use chemicals — instead of sunlight — for energy, explained marine biologist Nicole Dubilier, a professor and director of the department of symbiosis at the Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology in Germany. Dubilier was not involved in the study.
After marine life dies, it sinks to the seafloor and becomes buried, Dubilier said. In the process of decomposition, methane gas is released, escaping through the cracks of sediment as bubbles. Instead of floating away with the whims of the water column, the microbes that feed on the methane attach themselves to sea animals to remain among the bubbles.
By analyzing isotopes in the spiders’ tissues, the scientists determined the bacteria weren’t just hitching a ride from an eight-legged friend — they were also being eaten.
ROV SuBastian/Schmidt Ocean Institute
video
Related video
Researchers capture elusive squid on camera
“This is really the beauty of the symbiosis between the two: The bacteria get that perfect Goldilocks zone with everything they need,” Dubilier said. “Even if 80% of the population are eaten (by the spiders), it’s worth it for the 20% to keep surviving and reproducing.”
While these Sericosura species are the first sea spiders caught feeding on the methane-fueled microbes, other deep-sea animals such as tube worms and sponges are known to share the rare diet, Dubilier noted.
Since the deep-sea ecosystem likely plays such a key role in keeping methane away from Earth’s atmosphere, Goffredi said one day, the same type of microbes found on the Sericosura spiders could be cultured to reduce water contaminants elsewhere.
The newfound sea spiders were collected from different areas off the coast of Southern California and Alaska.
Shana Goffredi
A meal for the next generation of sea spiders
The newly discovered Sericosura spiders are translucent and only span about 0.4 inch (1 centimeter) in length, so they likely can’t travel

data.title: The Last of Us Part II – Seattle Locations Tour
data.author: lenocinor
data.article_summary: 《最后生还者2》西雅图地点导览文章主要介绍了游戏中几个关键场景的现实取景地。玩家可以跟随文章游览西雅图，亲眼目睹游戏中出现的著名地点，如国会山、太空针塔和华盛顿湖大桥等。文章详细描述了每个地点在游戏中的重要性及其与现实世界的对应关系，为粉丝提供了深入了解游戏世界构建的机会，同时也为到访西雅图的玩家提供了实用的旅游指南。文章结合了游戏情节和现实背景，增加了沉浸感和探索乐趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：玩家和观众对《The Last of Us Part II》（最后生还者2）的体验、剧情以及相关现实地点游览的看法和反馈。

不同观点：
• [sharkweek] 认为游戏在还原西雅图市区场景方面非常出色，虽然有些地理细节不太准确，但整体享受游戏体验，不会过分纠结于这些小问题。
• [shikshake] 对游戏和其粉丝社区的活跃表示赞赏，并表示期待未来亲自体验游戏中的地点。
• [lenocinor] 提供了自己制作的游览指南，并愿意回答其他人的问题或接受修正，表现出积极参与和分享的态度。
• [rangestransform] 指出剧中许多场景实际上是在温哥华拍摄的，并提供了具体例子，如使用SkyTrain Mk1车厢拍摄僵尸战斗场景。
• [n00bskoolbus] 提供了《The Last of Us》第一季拍摄地点的相关链接，将讨论引向剧集拍摄地。
• [SunlightEdge] 表示游戏在玩法和画面上非常出色，但剧情发展方向不符合个人口味，虽然尊重其对女性和LGBTQ+群体的关注。
• [mikestew] 讨论了技术问题，指出文档在加载时遇到问题，并提出可能的解决方案。
• [tomcam] 警告玩家在夜间游览游戏中的一些地点可能不安全，建议结伴而行并小心使用手机。
• [absurdo] 批评游戏的商业化和过度开发，认为这使得游戏变得“无法玩”，并担心《Uncharted》系列会遭遇同样的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是游戏的剧情，部分玩家（如[SunlightEdge]和[absurdo]）对剧情方向不满，而另一些玩家（如[shikshake]和[sharkweek]）则对整体体验表示赞赏。
• 技术问题（如[mikestew]提到的文档加载问题）和现实安全问题（如[tomcam]提到的夜间游览安全）也是讨论的重要部分。
• 游戏和剧集拍摄地点的真实性及地理细节也是讨论的一个重要方面（如[rangestransform]和[n00bskoolbus]提供的拍摄地点信息）。

After a
court ordered OpenAI to "indefinitely" retain all ChatGPT logs
, including deleted chats, of millions of users, two panicked users tried and failed to intervene. The order sought to preserve potential evidence in a copyright infringement lawsuit raised by news organizations.
In May, Judge Ona Wang, who drafted the order, rejected the first user's
request
on behalf of his company simply because the company should have hired a lawyer to draft the filing. But more recently, Wang
rejected
a second claim from another ChatGPT user, and that order went into greater detail, revealing how the judge is considering opposition to the order ahead of oral arguments this week, which were urgently
requested by OpenAI
.
The second
request
to intervene came from a ChatGPT user named Aidan Hunt, who said that he uses ChatGPT "from time to time," occasionally sending OpenAI "highly sensitive personal and commercial information in the course of using the service."
In his filing, Hunt alleged that Wang's preservation order created a "nationwide mass surveillance program" affecting and potentially harming "all ChatGPT users," who received no warning that their deleted and anonymous chats were suddenly being retained. He warned that the order limiting retention to just ChatGPT outputs carried the same risks as including user inputs, since outputs "inherently reveal, and often explicitly restate, the input questions or topics input."
Hunt claimed that he only learned that ChatGPT was retaining this information—despite policies specifying they would not—by stumbling upon the news in an online forum. Feeling that his Fourth Amendment and due process rights were being infringed, Hunt sought to influence the court's decision and proposed a motion to vacate the order that said Wang's "order effectively requires Defendants to implement a mass surveillance program affecting all ChatGPT users."
Hunt's fears are not unfounded, Corynne McSherry, legal director for the digital rights group the Electronic Frontier Foundation, told Ars.
"The discovery order poses genuine risks to user privacy in itself and as a precedent for the many other lawsuits around the country," McSherry said. "And it is emblematic of a broader problem: AI chatbots are opening another vector for corporate surveillance, especially if users don't have meaningful control over what happens to their chat histories and records."
According to Hunt, Wang failed to "consider exempting 'Anonymous Chats,' which are reasonably expected to contain the most sensitive and potentially damaging information of users, from retention and disclosure in this case," claiming that it "constitutes an overly broad and unreasonable action."
He urged the judge to revise the order to include this exemption, as well as exemptions for any chats "discussing medical, financial, legal, and personal topics that contain deeply private information of users and bear no relevance whatsoever" to the plaintiff news organizations' claimed interests.
For Hunt and many other users blindsided by the order, the stakes appear high. He suggested that Wang should have allowed him to intervene "because this case involves important, novel constitutional questions about the privacy rights incident to artificial intelligence usage—a rapidly developing area of law—and the ability of a magistrate to institute a nationwide mass surveillance program by means of a discovery order in a civil case."
But Wang
disagreed
with Hunt that she exceeded her authority in enforcing the order, emphasizing in a footnote that her order cannot be construed as enabling mass surveillance.
"Proposed Intervenor does not explain how a court’s document retention order that directs the preservation, segregation, and retention of certain privately held data by a private company for the limited purposes of litigation is, or could be, a 'nationwide mass surveillance program,'" Wang wrote. "It is not. The judiciary is not a law enforcement agency."
However, McSherry warned that "it's only a matter of time before law enforcement and private litigants start going to OpenAI to try to get chat histories/records about users for all sorts of purposes, just as they do already for search histories, social media posts, etc." Wang's order could become a gateway to that future, she said.
Wang rejected Hunt's motion primarily because "whether the temporary preservation of certain chat output log data that was routinely being deleted by OpenAI throughout the course of this litigation may infringe on purported constitutional and contractual privacy rights of individual consumers that use ChatGPT" was deemed a "collateral issue" that does not directly pertain to the central question of copyright infringement.

data.title: A deep critique of AI 2027's bad timeline models
data.author: paulpauper
data.article_summary: 本文是对"AI 2027"预测模型的深度批判，作者titotal认为该模型的 timeline 预测存在严重问题。尽管该模型声称通过严谨的数据分析和模拟支持其预测，并得到了包括Yoshua Bengio在内的多名专家的审阅，但作者认为其基本结构存疑，缺乏实证验证，且代码与模型描述不符。作者详细分析了模型的假设和结构，指出了多个问题，并制作了十多张图表来解释其观点。尽管作者与模型创建者进行了友好的交流，并获得了一些反馈，但仍认为该模型的质量不佳。文章最后提醒读者对所有博客内容保持怀疑态度，并给予模型团队适当的回应时间。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI未来发展的预测及其风险

不同观点：
• [mlsu] 提出一个讽刺性观点，认为人类体重按其模型会无限增长，并以此讽刺对AI未来预测的荒谬性。他认为当前对AI的讨论远不如人类体重增长成月亮大小的前景重要。
• [yodon] 指出不同作者对超级智能AI出现时间的预测差异不大，但作者们似乎对自己的预测过于自信，导致不必要的争论。
• [serjester] 批评这些预测缺乏对混沌系统的理解，认为聪明人也难以预测复杂系统，对AI预测过于自信是狂妄的表现。
• [boznz] 通过对比核聚变历史，指出AGI到ASI的科学基础尚不牢固，目前尚未达到"AI点火"阶段。
• [ed] 引用EPIC 2014视频，暗示当前对AI的预测可能会像过去的一些未来预测一样过时。
• [stephc_int13] 强调许多看似指数增长的曲线实际上是逻辑曲线，依赖指数增长的模型很可能是错误的。
• [lubujackson] 认为简单地将AI任务时间缩短视为进步是过于简化的，不同任务复杂度不同，模型未考虑这些因素。
• [sensanaty] 指出AI的危险不在于未来可能的超智能，而是当前因商业利益导致的实际问题，如就业和法律决策中的AI应用。

补充讨论：
• [TimPC] 认为 critique 提供了深刻的见解，并验证了部分数学模型。
• [Animats] 质疑 bugs 数量是否会指数增长及如何消除。
• [staunton] 认为整个讨论只是将"预测是荒谬的"包装成复杂细节，原作者可能会利用这些细节更新其预测。
• [kypro] 认为精确的AI风险预测易受攻击，不如更一般的风险讨论有说服力，并指出预测错误不会带来社会或经济回报。
• [brcmthrowaway] 批评讨论中存在大量无谓的争论和业余专家的意见。

争议焦点：
• 对AI未来发展时间的预测是否可靠及有意义。
• 当前AI讨论是否过于关注未来超智能而忽略了实际问题。
• 对指数增长模型的依赖是否合理。

Thank you to Arepo and Eli Lifland for looking over this article for errors.
I am sorry that this article is so long. Every time I thought I was done with it I ran into more issues with the model, and I wanted to be as thorough as I could. I’m not going to blame anyone for skimming parts of this article.
Note that the majority of this article was written before
Eli’s updated model
was released (the site was updated june 8th). His new model improves on some of my objections, but the majority still stand.
Introduction:
AI 2027
is an article written by the “AI futures team”. The primary piece is a short story penned by Scott Alexander, depicting a month by month scenario of a near-future where AI becomes superintelligent in 2027,proceeding to automate the entire economy in only a year or two and then either kills us all or does not kill us all, depending on government policies.
What makes AI 2027 different from other similar short stories is that it is presented as a forecast based on rigorous modelling and data analysis from forecasting experts. It is accompanied by
five appendices
of “detailed research supporting these predictions” and a codebase for simulations. They state that
“hundreds” of people reviewed
the text, including AI expert Yoshua Bengio, although some of these reviewers
only saw bits of it
.
The scenario in the short story is not the median forecast for any AI futures author, and none of the AI2027 authors actually believe that 2027 is the median year for a singularity to happen. But the argument they make is that 2027 is a
plausible
year, and they back it up with images of sophisticated looking modelling like the following:
This combination of compelling short story and seemingly-rigorous research may have been the secret sauce that let the article to go viral and be treated as a serious project:To
quote the authors themselves
:
It’s been a crazy few weeks here at the AI Futures Project. Almost a million people visited
our webpage
; 166,000 watched
our Dwarkesh interview
. We were invited on something like a million podcasts. Team members gave talks at Harvard, the Federation of American Scientists, and OpenAI.
Now, I was originally happy to dismiss this work and just wait for their predictions to fail, but this thing just keeps spreading, including a youtube video with
millions of views
. So I decided to actually dig into the model and the code, and try to understand what the authors were saying and what evidence they were using to back it up.
The article is huge, so I focussed on one section alone: their “timelines forecast” code and accompanying methodology section. Not to mince words,
I think it’s pretty bad
. It’s not just that I disagree with their parameter estimates, it’s that I think the fundamental structure of their model is highly questionable and at times barely justified, there is very little empirical validation of the model, and there are parts of the code that the write-up of the model straight up misrepresents.
Unfortunately, in my effort to catalogue all the problems I found, this article has ended up being extremely long: it is now almost as long as the actual write-up I’m critiquing, with like a dozen fully original graphs to explain my issues. I have done my best to ensure there are no obvious errors, but I did this all in my spare time so I can’t guarantee perfection.
I have some familiarity with AI but I am certainly no expert. I am a computational physicist, so I do have familarity with computational modelling, and
the actual model used in this forecast is fairly simple at only 300 lines of code or so (which is not necessarily a bad thing)
. In this article I will do my best to stay in my lane, and simply explain to you the assumptions and structure of their model, and then explain the various problems I have with what they did.
The authors of AI2027, to their credit, have been quite open to critique of their work, and have been generally helpful and kind when I corresponded with them about a few errors and critiques of their model.
Eli Lifland, one of the authors of the model I’m critiquing, has kindly looked over this critique for factual errors
. Although he disagrees with me on methodological and philosophical matters, he does agree with some of my critiques and has told me he will make several changes to the model write-up in response.
Even if at the end of this you think that I’m too harsh on the authors, I think this article still does a better job at explaining the AI 2027 timelines model than they do, so you can judge for yourself on it’s merit.
Remember that blogposts are error-ridden by default, and be appropriately skeptical of all of them, this one included. Please give the AI futures team an appropriate amount of time to respond as well. I will be crossposting this to the EA f

data.article_summary: Muntz金属是一种由约60%铜、40%锌和少量铁组成的黄铜合金，由英国人George Fredrick Muntz在1832年专利并商业化。它最初用于替代船底的铜包层，因具有防污能力和较低成本而广受欢迎，还被用于码头桩和机车管道等。Muntz的金属公司在1837年开始生产，后来与Grenfell家族合作扩大生产，1846年专利到期后，其他公司也开始生产类似产品。Muntz于1857年去世，其公司几经转手，最终在1928年并入ICI集团。

44359131.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Type of brass
Bow of the
Cutty Sark
The restored stern of the
Cutty Sark
(with
stern draft
and
rudder
) sheathed in Muntz metal.
Muntz metal
(also known as
yellow metal
[
1
]
) is an
alpha-beta brass
alloy
composed of approximately 60%
copper
, 40%
zinc
and a trace of iron. It is named after
George Fredrick Muntz
, a metal-roller of
Birmingham
,
England
, who commercialised the alloy following his patent of 1832.
[
2
]
[
3
]
The alloy must be worked hot and is used today for corrosion-resistant machine parts. Alpha-beta (also called duplex) metals contain both the α and β phases. The α phase refers to a
crystal structure
that is
face-centered cubic
, while the β phase is
body-centered cubic
.
Its original application was as a replacement for
copper sheathing
on the bottom of boats, as it maintained the
anti-fouling
abilities of the pure copper at around two thirds of the price. It became the material of choice for this application and Muntz made his fortune. It was found that copper prevented any organism that attempted to attach itself to a hull sheathed in the metal.  Thus, it was also used to sheathe the piles of piers in tropical seas, as a protection against teredo
shipworms
, and in locomotive tubes. After successful experimentation with the sheathing Muntz also took out a patent for bolts of the same composition.  These too proved a success as they not only were cheaper but also very strong and lasted longer.  A notable use of Muntz metal was in the hull of the
Cutty Sark
.
[
4
]
Company history
[
edit
]
Muntz's new metal contained more copper, less zinc, and a bit of iron not present in a similar 56:44 alloy patented by William Collins  in 1800. Production began on Water Street, Birmingham, but moved to Swansea in 1837.  In 1842 he bought the French Walls Works in
Smethwick
, formerly the site of
James Watt Jr.
's ironworks. The 4.5-acre (18,000 m
2
) site soon proved inadequate, and in 1850 a further 6.5 acres (26,000 m
2
) were bought, on the other side of the
Birmingham, Wolverhampton & Stour Valley Railway
. Eventually, as the business outgrew Muntz's own rolling mill in Birmingham, he joined in partnership with Pascoe Grenfell and sons who produced it at their Swansea mill as Muntz's Patent Metal Company. They and other partners then fixed the prices of the alloy at £18 per ton lower than the market price for the equivalent copper product, serving to establish Muntz Metal as the sheathing of choice where transport costs still kept it as an efficient competitor. As an example of their success in entering the market, 50 ships were metalled with Muntz metal in 1837, over 100 in 1838, doubling in 1840 and doubling again by 1844.
[
citation needed
]
With Muntz successfully supervising the manufacturing operations, by 1840 Muntz's Patent Metal Company employed 30 men to smelt and roll the alloy and was producing 2,000 tons yearly. Three years later the Company had over 200 men producing 3,000–4,000 tons yearly at £8 per ton profit. By then the Grenfells had left the partnership, for the agreement with Pascoe Grenfell & Sons had been terminated with some acrimony in 1842. When Muntz's patent expired in 1846, they and others began making fastenings and sheathing to the Muntz patent at will.
[
citation needed
]
Muntz died in 1857, to be succeeded by his eldest son, also called George Fredrick, who sold the business in 1864 to a joint stock company, Muntz's Metal Co. Ltd. In 1921 the company was bought by Elliott's Metal Company, which became part of ICI's Imperial Metals division (now
IMI plc
) in 1928.
[
5
]

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国削减汽车行业税收优惠政策的潜在影响

不同观点：
• **反对削减税收优惠**：[duxup]认为削减税收优惠是适得其反的。他指出，在全球其他国家朝电动汽车方向发展的同时，美国和汽车制造商可能会加大内燃机（ICE）汽车的投入，这将损害美国汽车制造商的竞争力。

• **伤害创新**：[throwaway48476]补充说，削减税收优惠不仅影响电动汽车发展，还会损害对更高效汽油发动机的创新研究，尤其是在混合动力车领域。他认为，如果没有对内燃机的需求限制，新的发动机类型可能会变得可行。

• **支持削减税收优惠**：[GenerWork]对削减税收优惠持支持态度，认为如果电动汽车是未来个人交通工具的发展方向，那么即使有短期痛苦，也值得为了长期收益而进行这种转变。

• **政策不确定性**：[laidoffamazon]对政策制定者的意图表示怀疑，指出当前政府领导人可能会通过法律手段攻击任何反对他的实体，因此很难准确预测政策制定者的真正意图和未来行动。

• **提供外部链接**：[LorenDB]提供了一个链接，可能包含与讨论相关的进一步信息或背景资料，但未直接表达立场。

补充讨论：
• **全球趋势与美国政策的对比**：[duxup]提到了全球其他国家向电动汽车转型的趋势，暗示美国如果不跟随这一趋势可能会落后。

• **短期痛苦与长期收益的权衡**：[GenerWork]强调了为了实现长期利益，接受短期挑战的必要性，这一观点与其他反对削减税收优惠的观点形成对比。

• **政策制定者的可信度问题**：[laidoffamazon]提出了对当前政府领导人使用法律手段（“lawfare”）攻击反对实体的担忧，这增加了对政策稳定性和可预测性的不确定性。

data.title: Show HN: Pickaxe – A TypeScript library for building AI agents
data.author: abelanger
data.article_summary: Pickaxe是一个用于构建可扩展AI代理的Typescript库，专注于处理持久执行、队列和调度等复杂性，让开发者专注于核心业务逻辑。它不是框架，所有功能都是开发者自定义的函数，易于与现有代码集成。Pickaxe支持容错和分布式执行，通过Hatchet任务队列实现持久化，确保代理能在失败后恢复或长时间等待外部事件。它具有可配置性、可运行于多种平台，并支持大规模并行任务处理。Pickaxe强调基础设施层的优化，而不限制代理的具体实现细节，如LLM调用或代理内存管理。使用Pickaxe，开发者可以通过简单命令快速创建和部署代理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pickaxe库的用途、功能及其与其他类似工具的比较

不同观点：
• j_rosenthal认为Pickaxe的名字容易与已有的低代码平台（pickaxe.co）混淆，尽管两者没有直接联系。
• movedx01对Pickaxe在异步代理和实时消息流的应用表示关注，尤其是如何在页面重载或用户长时间未操作后恢复消息流。
• jskalc92将Pickaxe的工具和代理的run()方法类比为React Hooks，并询问如何在多工具的聊天助手中传递消息历史。
• blixt指出API文档中对消息结构和模型选择的描述不够清晰，并询问如何在代理流中访问上下文，表达了对实验不同策略的支持需求。
• awaseem对Pickaxe与Mastra的比较表示关注，并询问两者的异同。

补充讨论：
• muratsu将Pickaxe与agent-kit（由Inngest提供）进行比较，询问具体区别。
• randomcatuser对Pickaxe表示赞赏，并表示会尝试使用。
• almosthere认为Pickaxe这样的项目有助于人们理解代理的概念。
• golergka对Pickaxe的发布表示欢迎，认为它解决了一直以来在类似功能开发中的痛点。
• zegl作为Hatchet的长期用户，对Pickaxe的发布感到些许失望，认为应该投入更多工程时间提升Hatchet的核心平台稳定性与性能。

争议焦点：
• Pickaxe的名字容易与其他已有的工具混淆。
• 如何有效实现异步代理和实时消息流的恢复。
• API文档中对消息结构和模型选择的描述不够详细。
• 工程资源是否应该优先投入在提升现有平台的稳定性和性能上。

Pickaxe: A Typescript library for building AI agents that scale
Pickaxe is a simple Typescript library for building AI agents that are fault-tolerant and scalable. It handles the complexities of durable execution, queueing and scheduling, allowing you to focus on writing core business logic.
It is not a framework
.
Everything in Pickaxe is just a function that
you have written
, which makes it easy to integrate with your existing codebase and business logic. You can build agents that call tools, other agents, or any other functions you define:
pickaxe.1.mp4

Get started
Getting started is as easy as two commands:
pnpm i -g @hatchet-dev/pickaxe-cli
pickaxe create first-agent
This will prompt you to create a new Pickaxe project from a template to see an end to end example of Pickaxe in action.
For a full quickstart, check out our
documentation
.
Benefits
Pickaxe is centered around the benefit of
durable execution
, which creates automatic checkpoints for agents so that they can easily recover from failure or wait for external events for a very long time without consuming resources. This is achieved by using a durable task queue called
Hatchet
.
Additionally, Pickaxe agents are:
💻 Code-first
- agents are defined as code and are designed to integrate with your business logic.
🌐 Distributed
- all agents and tools run across a fleet of machines, where scheduling is handled gracefully by Pickaxe. When your underlying machine fails, Pickaxe takes care of rescheduling and resuming the agent on a different machine.
⚙️ Configurable
- simple configuration for retries, rate limiting, concurrency control, and much more
☁️ Runnable anywhere
- Pickaxe agents can run on any container-based platform (Hatchet, Railway, Fly.io, Porter, Kubernetes, AWS ECS, GCP Cloud Run)
Scalability
Pickaxe is designed for scale: specifically, massive throughput and parallelism. Hatchet has run agentic workloads which spawn hundreds of thousands of tasks for a single execution, and runs billions of tasks per month.
Philosophy
Pickaxe is not a framework. Agents and tools are simply functions that you have written. This means you can choose or build the best memory, knowledge, reasoning, or integrations. It does not impose any constraints on how you design your tools, call LLMs, or implement features like agent memory. Pickaxe is opinionated about the infrastructure layer of your agents, but not about the implementation details of your agents.

- agents are functions which call other tools and agents.
Tools
- tools are functions that perform specific tasks and can be called by agents.
Toolbox

44359634.article_content:
June 23, 2025
Sweden acquires IRIS-T SLM air defence system under European Sky Shield Initiative
By Defence Industry Europe
Photo: Bundeswehr/Thorsten Weber.
Sweden’s Defence Materiel Administration (FMV) has signed a major defence contract with German defence company Diehl Defence to procure seven fire units of the IRIS-T SLM medium-range air defence system. The acquisition is part of Sweden’s participation in the European Sky Shield Initiative (ESSI), a multinational effort to strengthen Europe’s air and missile defence capabilities.
According to FMV, initial components of the IRIS-T SLM systems are scheduled to be delivered to the Swedish Armed Forces by mid-2028, with full operational deployment expected by 2030. The contract is valued at approximately USD 925 million, as confirmed by Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson. Diehl Defence has not yet publicly commented on the deal.
The European Sky Shield Initiative, led by Germany, aims to establish a layered air defence system across the continent. Alongside the IRIS-T SLM as the preferred medium-range solution, the ESSI also includes the U.S.-made Patriot system and the Israeli-developed Arrow 3 as complementary long-range missile defence systems.
In a statement, FMV highlighted that the procurement strengthens Sweden’s role in ESSI and contributes to the collective security of Europe. The IRIS-T SLM system has been widely praised for its combat effectiveness, particularly in Ukraine, where it has demonstrated high performance against a range of aerial threats.
Since 2022, the system has been adopted by several European nations including Germany, Latvia, and Estonia, reinforcing its growing reputation as a reliable and advanced air defence solution.

data.title: First celestial image unveiled from revolutionary telescope
data.author: wood_spirit
data.article_summary: 位于智利的薇拉·鲁宾天文台发布了其首张图像，展示了距地球9000光年的三裂星云和泻湖星云的绚丽细节。该天文台配备了全球最强力的数码相机，具备前所未有的宇宙观测能力，预计将极大拓展我们对宇宙的理解。它有望在十年内发现大量太阳系天体，探测近地杀手小行星，绘制银河系地图，并研究暗物质。在发布会上，天文台透露该望远镜10小时内发现了2104颗新小行星和7个近地天体。其十年巡天项目将持续拍摄南半球夜空，帮助科学家探索宇宙历史和超新星爆炸等现象。望远镜的32亿像素相机每40秒拍摄一张照片，每三天覆盖整个天空，数据将由全球科学家分析。这一项目代表了天文界一代人的努力。

44359029.article_content:
First celestial image unveiled from revolutionary telescope
5 hours ago
Share
Save
Ione Wells
South America correspondent
Georgina Rannard
Science correspondent
Share
Save
NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory
The first image revealed by the Vera Rubin telescope shows the Trifid and Lagoon nebulae in stunning detail
A powerful new telescope in Chile has released its first images, showing off its unprecedented ability to peer into the dark depths of the universe.
In one picture, vast colourful gas and dust clouds swirl in a star-forming region 9,000 light years from Earth.
The Vera C Rubin observatory, home to the world's most powerful digital camera, promises to transform our understanding of the universe.
If a ninth planet exists in our solar system, scientists say this telescope would find it in its first year.
RubinObs
Rubin Observatory and the Rubin Auxiliary Telescope in Cerro Pachón in Chile
It should detect killer asteroids in striking distance of Earth and map the Milky Way. It will also answer crucial questions about dark matter, the mysterious substance that makes up most of our universe.
In a press conference on Monday, the observatory revealed that in 10 hours, the telescope detected 2,104 new asteroids and seven space objects close to Earth.
All other space and ground surveys combined usually find about 20,000 asteroids in a year.
This once-in-a-generation moment for astronomy is the start of a continuous 10-year filming of the southern night sky.
"I personally have been working towards this point for about 25 years. For decades we wanted to build this phenomenal facility and to do this type of survey," says Professor Catherine Heymans, Astronomer Royal for Scotland.
The UK is a key partner in the survey and will host data centres to process the extremely detailed snapshots as the telescope sweeps the skies capturing everything in its path.
Vera Rubin could increase the number of known objects in our solar system tenfold.
NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory
A huge cluster of galaxies including spiral galaxies in the vast Virgo cluster, which is about 100 billion times the size of the Milky Way.
BBC News visited the Vera Rubin observatory before the release of the images.
It sits on Cerro Pachón, a mountain in the Chilean Andes that hosts several observatories on private land dedicated to space research.
Very high, very dry, and very dark. It is a perfect location to watch the stars.
Maintaining this darkness is sacrosanct. The bus ride up and down the windy road at night must be done cautiously, because full-beam headlights must not be used.
The inside of the observatory is no different.
There is a whole engineering unit dedicated to making sure the dome surrounding the telescope, which opens to the night sky, is dark – turning off rogue LEDs or other stray lights that could interfere with the astronomical light they are capturing from the night sky.
The starlight is "enough" to navigate, commissioning scientist Elana Urbach explains.
One of the observatory's big goals, she adds, is to "understand the history of the Universe" which means being able to see faint galaxies or supernova explosions that happened "billions of years ago".
"So, we really need very sharp images," Elana says.
Each detail of the observatory's design exhibits similar precision.
SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
Vera Rubin's is 3,200-megapixel camera was built by the US Department of Energy's SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
It achieves this through its unique three-mirror design. Light enters the telescope from the night sky, hits the primary mirror (8.4m diameter), is reflected onto the secondary mirror (3.4m) back onto a third mirror (4.8m) before entering its camera.
The mirrors must be kept in impeccable condition. Even a speck of dust could alter the image quality.
The high reflectivity and speed of this allow the telescope to capture a lot of light which Guillem Megias, an active optics expert at the observatory, says is "really important" to observe things from "really far away which, in astronomy, means they come from earlier times".
The camera inside the telescope will repeatedly capture the night sky for ten years, every three days, for a Legacy Survey of Space and Time.
At 1.65m x 3m, it weighs 2,800kg and provides a wide field of view.
It will capture an image roughly every 40 seconds, for about 8-12 hours a night thanks to rapid repositioning of the moving dome and telescope mount.
It has 3,200 megapixels (67 times more than an iPhone 16 Pro camera) and would require 400 Ultra HD TV screens to show a single image.
"When we got the first photo up here, it was a special moment," Mr Megias said.
"When I first started working with this project, I met someone who had been working on it since 1996. I was born in 1997. It makes you realise this is an endeavour of a generation of astronomers."

主要讨论点：对不同话题的看法和反应，包括文化历史背景下的称谓问题、商业道德问题以及具体链接的内容。

不同观点：
• [profsummergig] 认为使用来自非统治性君主制国家的头衔（如"骑士"）在文化上不合适，尤其在美国这样的共和国。他指出美国历史上反对使用贵族头衔，并表达希望头衔和世袭制度能变得 irrelevant。他特别提到，这些头衔只是形式上的，并不具有法律效力，且与实际统治无关。

• [diasf] 则将焦点转向商业道德问题，批评某些公司在与IYO进行会议并了解其产品后，选择创建名称相似的公司。他认为这种行为不道德，尤其是在这些公司拥有大量资源的情况下。他进一步指出，过去十年中，越来越多的创业公司采取"不惜一切代价取胜"的策略，这种策略以前只在大型科技公司（如微软）中常见。

• [aanet] 并没有直接参与上述讨论，而是提供了一个链接 (https://www.iyo.audio/)，可能是为了回应或澄清[diasf]提到的公司或事件的具体内容。

补充讨论：
- [profsummergig] 强调的是文化与历史背景下的称谓问题，尤其是对世袭头衔的反感，反映出他对共和制度的偏好。
- [diasf] 关注的是商业竞争中的道德问题，特别是大公司利用其资源优势模仿或复制小公司创意的行为，反映出对商业环境中不公平竞争的担忧。
- [aanet] 提供的链接可能与讨论中的具体事件或公司有关，但未做进一步解释。

争议焦点：
- 争议的焦点主要集中在[diasf]提出的商业道德问题上，即大公司在了解小公司的产品后是否应该以相似的名称成立新公司，以获取竞争优势。这涉及商业竞争中的公平性与道德标准。

data.title: Ask HN: How to get rid of Gemini?
data.author: jacquesm
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Google产品中AI功能（如Gemini）的看法和应对方法

不同观点：
• **接受并使用AI功能**：用户quintes表示，虽然Gemini被引入Google Workspace，但在实际使用中并没有造成太大困扰，甚至发现其在某些情况下有用。

• **寻找替代产品**：
  - danieldk建议使用其他付费产品，如Kagi作为搜索引擎、Fastmail或Proton作为邮件服务，以避免Google的AI功能。
  - gburn也提到了寻找Google Workspace替代品的困难，尽管测试了Proton和Microsoft Teams，但都不尽如人意，最终还是因为Google的整体生态系统和便利性而选择留下。

• **使用非Google搜索引擎**：
  - qoez和quaintdev都提到了使用DuckDuckGo和Ecosia等其他搜索引擎来避免Google的AI功能，并表示这些替代搜索引擎的结果已经足够好。
  - candiddevmike提到，如果使用Google Workspace，可能需要通过提交工单来禁用AI功能。

• **技术手段屏蔽AI功能**：
  - notpushkin建议使用uBlock Origin来屏蔽不想要的元素。
  - _wli提到通过VPN或将流量路由到不支持Gemini的国家来避免该功能。
  - deivid提供了一种通过在搜索查询中添加'-ai'来禁用AI摘要的方法。
  - 1vuio0pswjnm7提到使用无JavaScript的命令行搜索来避免AI功能。

补充讨论：
• **对Google商业模式的批评**：jasonpeacock认为用户是Google的产品，Google会继续通过AI功能来吸引用户注意力并从中获利，因此唯一的对策是完全放弃使用Google。

• **具体功能争议**：josefritzishere提到Google Drive中的"Catch Me Up"功能，认为该功能无用且无法禁用，成为用户体验的一大问题。

争议焦点：用户对Google引入AI功能的接受程度以及是否有有效的替代方案或技术手段来屏蔽这些功能。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：当代文学小说为何不再像经典文学作品那样受欢迎，以及影响文学创作和消费的经济与文化因素。

不同观点：
• jl6：认为经典文学作品如《傲慢与偏见》等依然畅销，新书面临与已有书籍的竞争，而人的时间和注意力有限。媒体内容的消费有上限，新作品很难替代经典。
• lapcat：赞同文章的前半部分，特别是关于作家经济机会下降的分析。但认为文章后半部分关于作家为了评论家的赞誉而牺牲销量的论点缺乏解释和证据，并提出企业合并和利润最大化策略是文学问题的主因。
• libraryofbabel：赞同文章对文学小说衰落的供需分析，但希望文章能更多讨论像Sally Rooney这样成功例子的原因，并质疑文学与类型小说之间的严格界限。
• narrator：认为过去娱乐方式有限，人们不得不读书，而现在有无限的娱乐选择。同时，文学小说被政治化，难以找到具有争议性且值得一读的当代小说。
• pclmulqdq：指出许多现在被视为“文学”的作品在当年其实是商业成功的大众读物，认为不应轻易 dismiss当代的流行作品。
• tolerance：认为文学小说要求读者深入体验角色的生活，而现代人不再具备这种“文学头脑”，电子媒体的参与性和表演性更强。
• mcnamaratw：对实验性作家如John Barth或George Saunders的作品感到不适，更喜欢如David Foster Wallace这样介于实验与传统之间的作家。
• unignorant：反驳文章中关于当代文学小说未能进入畅销榜的论点，指出如《所有我们看不见的光》等作品确实进入了榜单。
• alexitorg：认为科幻等其他类型文学也面临类似趋势，更多作品为了迎合评论家而出版，且社会正义主题增多，导致一些老读者不满。
• southernplaces7：认为经典文学作品继续畅销，新小说数量庞大且不断增加，未来哪些作品会被视为文学经典尚不可知。
• fullshark：认为对文化作品发表意见不再赋予个人地位，因为有太多人有深思熟虑的意见，但却对社会无贡献。
• TulliusCicero：读书是为了娱乐，文学小说对他来说不够有趣，更喜欢能立即带来乐趣的作品，如 progression fantasy。
• ang_cire：赞同评论家与消费者脱钩的观点，认为这是经济困境导致的，并指出许多行业正试图重新货币化以摆脱大公司的控制。
• Zaylan：自己的阅读习惯发生了变化，过去喜欢文学小说，现在更倾向于非虚构或短篇作品，认为这可能与时间、注意力和意义的深层转变有关。
• cafard：质疑用过去的一些畅销书作者来批评2023年的文学现状，认为每个时代的畅销书都有大量平庸之作。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点包括当代文学小说是否真的衰落，衰落的原因是供需问题、企业策略还是文化变迁。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是经典与当代作品的比较，以及文学与类型小说之间的界限。
• 个人阅读习惯的变化和对文学作品的不同期待也被多次提及，反映出读者群体的多样性。

data.title: Leak reveals Grok might soon edit your spreadsheets
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: xAI正在开发一款支持电子表格的先进文件编辑器Grok，旨在与OpenAI、Google和微软竞争，将AI助手整合到生产力工具中。据泄露的信息，用户可以在编辑文件的同时与Grok对话并获得协助。此前，xAI推出了Grok Studio和Workspaces功能，使用户可以协作生成文档、代码等。虽然Google的Gemini Workspace有类似功能，但仅限于谷歌生态系统。若泄露属实，xAI的编辑器将助力埃隆·马斯克将X打造成包含文档、聊天、支付和社交媒体的“全能应用”。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44358701.article_content:
Leaked code suggests xAI is developing an advanced file editor for Grok with spreadsheet support, signaling the company’s push to compete with OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft by embedding AI copilots into productivity tools.
“You can talk to Grok and ask it to assist you at the same time you’re editing the files!”
writes
reverse engineer Nima Owji, who leaked the finding.
BREAKING: xAI is working on an advanced FILE EDITOR for GROK!
It even supports SPREADSHEETS!
You can talk to Grok and ask it to assist you at the same time you're editing the files!
pic.twitter.com/9vIKRZj6Wn
— Nima Owji (@nima_owji)
June 22, 2025
TechCrunch has reached out to xAI to confirm the findings and learn more.
xAI hasn’t explicitly detailed its strategy for pursuing interactive, multimodal AI workspaces, but it has dropped a series of announcements that point to how the company is thinking about these tools. In April 2025, xAI launched
Grok Studio
, a split-screen workspace that lets users collaborate with Grok on generating documents, code, reports, and browser games. It also launched the ability to
create Workspaces
that let you organize files and conversations in a single place.
While OpenAI and Microsoft have similar tools, Google’s Gemini
Workspace
for Sheets, Docs, and Gmail appears to be the most similar to what xAI is reportedly building. Google’s tools can edit Docs and Sheets and allow you to chat with Gemini while looking at or editing documents. The difference is that Gemini Workspace only works within Google’s own ecosystem.
It’s not clear what types of files xAI’s editor might support aside from spreadsheets, or whether xAI plans to build a full productivity suite that could compete with Google Workspace or Microsoft 365.
If Owji’s findings are true, the advanced editor would be a step towards Elon Musk’s ambitions to turn X into an “everything app” that includes docs, chat, payments, and social media.

data.title: Show HN: Report idling vehicles in NYC (and get a cut of the fines) with AI
data.author: rafram
data.article_summary: Idle Reporter是一款帮助纽约市民举报商业车辆怠速行为的应用。它通过以下功能简化举报流程：时间戳相机录制视频，显示时间、日期和地点；AI辅助填表（需订阅）；手动编辑器可自行填写报告；自动截图生成器从视频中截取车牌和车主信息；状态跟踪器管理并提交报告给DEP。需注意，该应用非官方工具，用户需自行确保报告的准确性。应用不收集数据，免费下载但提供订阅服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纽约市推出的基于罚款的市民举报应用及其社会影响

不同观点：
• 支持与赞赏观点：
  ◦ [hiAndrewQuinn] 认为该应用是迅速提升法律遵守率的杰出案例，个人会推荐给纽约市的朋友使用。
  ◦ [screye] 称赞去中心化的交通执法是双赢，认为此应用将执法转变为“高效的自由市场”，并表示会尝试使用。
  ◦ [BoxFour] 表示作为纽约市民，很高兴这个应用存在，认为大多数市民也会有同感。

• 对技术透明度的质疑：
  ◦ [a5c11] 对应用中AI机制的透明度提出质疑，认为不应将所有功能隐藏在“神圣的AI”背后，希望了解AI具体在应用中的作用。
  ◦ [MathMonkeyMan] 提到法律界对类似应用的阻碍，并提供相关链接，暗示法律复杂性可能影响应用实施。

• 对社会影响的担忧：
  ◦ [Zaylan] 支持使用AI提升执法效率，但担心举报变成赚钱手段会损害日常信任，呼吁在效率与社区氛围间找到平衡。
  ◦ [waffletower] 认为此方案可能导致公民对立，虽然内燃机（ICE）问题需要关注，但这种方式可能带来负面社会反馈。

• 恶意使用的潜在风险：
  ◦ [wingspar] 担心恶意生成的AI视频报告如何防御，提出了对AI生成证据可靠性的质疑。
  ◦ [nandomrumber] 讽刺地建议增加AI步骤，使任何停放的商用车辆看起来和听起来像是在怠速，暗示此应用可能被恶意操纵。

• 经济与技术可行性讨论：
  ◦ [theptip] 认为定价对偶尔使用的用户偏高，询问iOS是否方便通过Apple Pay进行小额交易，并对开发者通过应用谋生表示理解。
  ◦ [vineyardmike] 分享了自己使用城市311应用的体验，并指出政府在数字化服务和数据开放方面的不足，呼吁更多API和数字格式服务。

补充讨论：
• [crusty] 提到曾看过关于纽约有人通过收集罚款发展成全职工作的视频，认为此应用可能对这些人的生计造成影响。
• [rurcliped] 提出功能请求，希望加入基于AI的风险分析模型，以识别哪些商用车辆可能涉及有组织犯罪。

争议焦点：
• 举报应用带来的社会信任问题与恶意使用风险。
• 应用定价与经济可行性对不同用户的影响。
• 技术透明度与AI在应用中的具体作用。

data.title: Apple Research unearthed forgotten AI technique and using it to generate images
data.author: celias
data.article_summary: Apple正在通过重新探索一种被遗忘的AI技术——归一化流（Normalizing Flows）——来生成图像。与当前流行的扩散模型和自回归模型不同，Apple发布的两个新模型TarFlow和STARFlow，结合了Transformer架构，提升了归一化流在图像生成中的能力。TarFlow通过将图像分割成小块并自回归生成，避免了图像token化的质量损失。STARFlow则在压缩的潜在空间中工作，通过解码器恢复高分辨率图像，并能处理文本提示。与OpenAI的GPT-4o模型相比，Apple的方法更注重在设备上的高效运行，而非依赖云计算。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于苹果公司发表的有关归一化流（Normalizing Flows）的论文的讨论

不同观点：
• 一些读者（如[celias]）对论文的技术内容感兴趣，并提供了论文的链接供其他人查看和讨论。这表明他们对论文的发表持积极态度，并希望引发更多技术层面的探讨。

• 部分讨论者对论文的创新性提出质疑。他们认为论文中的方法或理论在之前的研究中已有涉及，特别是与其他已发表的归一化流模型相比，苹果的这篇论文并没有展现出足够的突破性或独特贡献。

• 另一部分讨论者则关注论文的实际应用价值。他们讨论了论文中提出的方法在实际机器学习任务中的潜在应用，比如图像生成、数据增强等。这部分读者认为，即便论文在理论上没有显著突破，但其应用前景仍然值得关注。

• 还有一部分讨论者对论文的写作和表述提出了意见。他们认为论文在某些部分的表述不够清晰，特别是在数学推导和模型细节上，可能对没有相关背景知识的读者不太友好。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是论文中实验部分的充分性。一些讨论者认为论文中的实验数据不够充分，无法完全证明所提方法的优势，特别是在与其他先进归一化流模型对比时，实验结果的说服力不足。

• 一些读者提到论文的潜在影响，尤其是苹果公司在这个领域的参与是否会带来更多资源和关注，从而推动归一化流技术的发展。这部分讨论涉及对行业趋势和公司科研战略的更广泛思考。

• 最后，有讨论者指出，该论文的发表可能会引发更多关于归一化流模型在隐私保护和数据安全方面的讨论，特别是在苹果这样注重用户隐私的公司背景下，这一技术如何平衡性能和隐私保护是一个值得关注的方向。

44358535.article_content:
Apple Research
Apple Research just unearthed a forgotten AI technique and is using it to generate images
Marcus Mendes
| Jun 23 2025 - 8:59 am PT
2 Comments
Today, most generative image models basically fall into two main categories: diffusion models, like Stable Diffusion, or autoregressive models, like OpenAI’s GPT-4o. But Apple just released two papers that show how there might be room for a third, forgotten technique: Normalizing Flows. And with a dash of Transformers on top, they might be more capable than previously thought.
First things first: What are Normalizing Flows?
Normalizing Flows (NFs) are a type of AI model that works by learning how to mathematically transform real-world data (like images) into structured noise, and then reverse that process to generate new samples.
The big advantage is that they can calculate the exact likelihood of each image they generate, a property that diffusion models can’t do. This makes flows especially appealing for tasks where understanding the probability of an outcome really matters.
But there’s a reason most people haven’t heard much about them lately: Early flow-based models produced images that looked blurry or lacked the detail and diversity offered by diffusion and transformer-based systems.
Study #1: TarFlow
In the paper “
Normalizing Flows are Capable Generative Models
”, Apple introduces a new model called TarFlow, short for Transformer AutoRegressive Flow.
At its core, TarFlow replaces the old, handcrafted layers used in previous flow models with Transformer blocks. Basically, it splits images into small patches, and generates them in blocks, with each block predicted based on all the ones that came before. That’s what’s called autoregressive, which is the same underlying method that OpenAI currently uses for image generation.
Images of various resolutions generated by TarFlow models. From left to right, top to bottom: 256×256 images on AFHQ, 128×128 and 64×64 images on ImageNet. Source:
Normalizing Flows are Capable Generative Models
The key difference is that while OpenAI generates discrete tokens, treating images like long sequences of text-like symbols, Apple’s TarFlow generates pixel values directly, without tokenizing the image first. It’s a small, but significant difference because it lets Apple avoid the quality loss and rigidity that often come with compressing images into a fixed vocabulary of tokens.
Still, there were limitations, especially when it came to scaling up to larger, high-res images. And that’s where the second study comes in.
Study #2: STARFlow
In the paper “
STARFlow: Scaling Latent Normalizing Flows for High-resolution Image Synthesis
”, Apple builds directly on TarFlow and presents STARFlow (Scalable Transformer AutoRegressive Flow), with key upgrades.
The biggest change: STARFlow no longer generates images directly in pixel space. Instead, it basically works on a compressed version of the image, and then hands things off to a decoder that upsamples everything back to full resolution at the final step.
Random samples of STARFlow on ImageNet 256 ×256 and 512 ×512. Source:
STARFlow: Scaling Latent Normalizing Flows for High-resolution Image Synthesis
This shift to what is called latent space means STARFlow doesn’t need to predict millions of pixels directly. It can focus on the broader image structure first, leaving fine texture detail to the decoder.
Apple also reworked how the model handles text prompts. Instead of building a separate text encoder, STARFlow can plug in existing language models (like Google’s small language model Gemma, which in theory could run on-device) to handle language understanding when the user prompts the model to create the image. This keeps the image generation side of the model focused on refining visual details.
How STARFlow compares with OpenAI’s 4o image generator
While Apple is rethinking flows, OpenAI has also recently moved beyond diffusion with its GPT-4o model. But their approach is fundamentally different.
GPT-4o treats images as sequences of discrete tokens, much like words in a sentence. When you ask ChatGPT to generate an image, the model predicts one image token at a time, building the picture piece by piece. This gives OpenAI enormous flexibility: the same model can generate text, images, and audio within a single, unified token stream.
The tradeoff? Token-by-token generation can be slow, especially for large or high-resolution images. And it’s extremely computationally expensive. But since GPT-4o runs entirely in the cloud, OpenAI isn’t as constrained by latency or power use.
In short: both Apple and OpenAI are moving beyond diffusion, but while OpenAI is building for its data centers, Apple is clearly building for our pockets.

data.title: The AI lifestyle subsidy is going to end
data.author: bobbiechen
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论AI生活方式补贴即将结束，以及这将如何影响用户的数字体验。作者引用Derek Thompson的“千禧一代生活方式补贴的终结”一文，说明过去风险资本和零利率政策通过补贴让消费者受益，即使公司亏损。然而，随着利率变化和投资者害怕错过下一个风口，资金继续涌入基于大型语言模型的产品，但这些产品的用户体验可能恶化。文章指出，搜索引擎和社交媒体的结果已经因广告和 affiliate 营销而失真，而AI发现工具如ChatGPT等未来可能更偏向营销内容。同时，生成式引擎优化（GEO）正在成为新的营销策略，AI巨头也可能会引入更多广告，进一步影响用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生活方式补贴及其相关经济模式、技术发展趋势和未来影响

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如some_random）对所谓的"AI生活方式补贴"表示困惑，认为便宜的GPU时间等资源虽然目前价格低廉，但与传统商品（如外卖牛排）的价格上涨趋势不同，AI工具的成本可能通过技术进步进一步降低，或者模型改进后对高端硬件的需求减少。
• throwanem认为使用本地模型更为可靠，愿意牺牲一些功能以换取对模型偏见 static 和可预测的信任。
• pier25通过数据指出OpenAI在亏损巨大的情况下运营，质疑其经济可持续性。
• AstroBen提出AI已经在潜移默化地推销产品，类似于新的SEO。
• barrenko对互联网的现状持悲观态度，但认为互联网本身会存活下来。
• ChrisMarshallNY认为由于AI生成内容的泛滥，导致苹果应用审批时间变长，希望"补贴"尽快结束。
• Quarrelsome对LLM的盈利模式感到困惑，认为即使通过产品植入也难以可靠地实现盈利，更可能通过传统广告形式获利。
• jasonthorsness认为通过硬件或软件进步，AI成本会下降，目前的资金投入像是昂贵的市场营销。
• seydor指出零利率时代的资金进入了科技股，这些股票的估值能够支撑免费产品几十年，科技公司有很大的裁员空间。
• beej71进行了一项实验，取消了ChatGPT订阅，尝试用更困难的方式完成任务，并询问其他人的类似实验结果。
• jfoster认为目前各公司仍在竞争，消费者还能享受模型改进的好处，但未来可能会在某个点被切断。
• h1fra简单表示未来的冲击对某些人/公司将是痛苦的。
• skybrian认为投资者对AI的热情减退后，可能出现不同的商业模式，如订阅费或广告支持模式，具体趋势难以判断。
• daft_pink表示目前支付多个AI订阅费用，但未来可能只支付一到两个，不确定是否真正受益。
• waffletower认为作者未考虑到广告拦截算法的改进潜力，希望订阅模式胜过广告收入模式。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及AI工具价格趋势、广告植入、本地模型的信任与使用、科技公司经济可持续性、订阅模式与广告模式的未来竞争等多个方面。
• 争议焦点包括AI工具成本的未来趋势、当前补贴模式的可持续性以及不同商业模式（如广告与订阅）的优劣。

44356625.article_content:
The AI lifestyle subsidy is going to end
Jun 15
Written By
Bobbie Chen
Or, why your digital experiences are about to get worse.
Whether you’re enthusiastically generating or reluctantly dismissing another pop-up for a useless chatbot, right now is the best it’s ever going to be. Oh, the
technology
is going to get better. But what about your experience as a user?
We lose money on every sale, but we make it up in volume
If you were alive in the bygone era of 2022, you might remember Derek Thompson writing about
The End of the Millennial Lifestyle Subsidy
:
…if you woke up on a Casper mattress, worked out with a Peloton, Ubered to a WeWork, ordered on DoorDash for lunch, took a Lyft home, and ordered dinner through Postmates only to realize your partner had already started on a Blue Apron meal, your household had, in one day, interacted with eight unprofitable companies that collectively lost about $15 billion in one year.
Derek Thompson via The Atlantic:
The End of the Millennial Lifestyle Subsidy
The lifestyle subsidy was a great deal for consumers. Venture capital and zero interest-rate policy supplied a ton of money for any startup that could demonstrate strong growth - even if they were growing by selling customers $20 of services for $10. “We lose money on every sale, but we make it up on volume” was not just a
surprisingly-old joke (first recorded in 1833!)
, but the real pitch to investors.
Is it any different this time around? Interest rates aren’t what they used to be, but investors are still scared of missing out on the next big thing. That investor money is going straight into subsidizing the costs of LLM-based products. Today, dedicated groups are actively farming free trial accounts from AI startups and using them to resell access to Anthropic and OpenAI APIs. (Hopefully those startups realize, instead of happily watching their signup number go up).
But besides unit economics, consumer AI applications present a new opportunity to control the way that people discover things.
Search engines and social media aren’t as good as they used to be
In the original Google research paper (1998), Sergey Brin and Larry Page wrote:
The goals of the advertising business model do not always correspond to providing quality search to users… we expect that advertising funded search engines will be inherently biased towards the advertisers and away from the needs of the consumers.
Sergey Brin and Lawrence Page:
The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine (quote from Appendix A)
Within two years, Google had launched AdWords, and some years later they acquired DoubleClick, setting the stage for Google to be one of the world’s largest and most profitable advertisers today. Now if you search for any company name, you’ll probably see:
An ad for a competitor
An ad from the company itself, desperately fighting for space above the fold
An ad for a phishing site that steals your password and even relays your one-time passcode
And if you scroll down a bit, the actual link to the actual company website
I remember a time when you didn’t need to install an adblocker to get decent Google results without scrolling. But we don’t live in that time anymore.
As people got better at search engine optimization, it became harder to find product reviews that weren’t actually affiliate marketing. Top 5 printers in 2025: best value, best quality, best for photos, best for feng shui, best at some other arbitrary qualification so I could include one more paid link. Sure, go get your money, but I kinda wanted to hear less-biased reviews.
There was also a moment in time when you could search for “printer recommendations reddit” and hear from mostly-real people. But now there’s dozens of tools to monitor relevant social media posts, so FengShuiPrinterCo can swoop in at the right moment (and if you’re lucky, they’ll disclose their affiliation). In more proactive moves, some companies actively moderate relevant Reddit communities to secure their brand dominance.
AI discovery is only going to get worse from here
(June 2025) ChatGPT and friends today are powerful token-generating machines that can use their existing body of trained material, search the internet, and synthesize a reasonable summary to start. It’s a great tool for discovery and learning, especially in new areas. You can follow citations back to the original source (which you want to do, a lot, for when it’s wrong) and ask follow-up questions. I put a date on this claim because I think it could really change a lot in the next six months.
On the marketing side, venture capital firm Andreesen Horowitz is already pushing
Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)
as the successor to social media and search engine optimization. They’ve got a logo wall with dozens of companies to make sure that when you ask ChatGPT about what printer to buy, it will make sure you’ll get a ranking based on feng shui.

data.title: Phoenix.new – Remote AI Runtime for Phoenix
data.author: wut42
data.article_summary: Chris McCord，Elixir 的 Phoenix 框架创建者，推出了新项目 **Phoenix.new**，这是一个专为 Elixir 和 Phoenix 打造的在线编码代理工具。它运行在一个临时的虚拟机（Fly Machine）中，提供完整的根访问权限，让代理可以自由安装软件包和运行程序，而不会影响本地环境。Phoenix.new 集成了全功能的浏览器和 VSCode 界面，代理可以实时查看和测试前端更改，自动进行实时交互和错误检测。该工具旨在简化应用开发和部署流程，生成的应用程序从一开始就运行在云端，拥有可分享的 URL，并与 GitHub 集成，享受 Fly.io 的基础设施保护。通过 Phoenix.new，开发者可以轻松构建协作式实时应用，减少重复性工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Elixir/Phoenix 与 AI 工具（如 Fly.io 和 Phoenix.new）的结合及其对开发者的影响

不同观点：
• **支持与兴奋态度**（colecut、arrowsmith）：colecut 表示自己在短时间内成功部署了一个应用，并对该技术带来的潜力感到兴奋。arrowsmith 则认为这种创新让 Elixir 社区保持了竞争力，避免被 Python、JS 等主流语言甩在后面。
  
• **质疑与反思**（travisgriggs、krainboltgreene）：travisgriggs 对这种“代理式编码”表示担忧，认为它暴露了编程领域的深层次问题，即现代网页技术过于复杂且容易隐藏错误。krainboltgreene 则批评该工具可能反工人阶级，认为社区领袖不应专注于这种工具的开发。
  
• **实用体验与问题**（itsautomatisch、zombiwoof）：itsautomatisch 提到使用过程中遇到 UI 和文档问题，且无法很好地控制代码库，感觉性价比不高。zombiwoof 则抱怨在 Mac 上安装 Phoenix 时遇到 Postgres 配置问题，认为基本功能未正常工作，削弱了对 AI 工具的信心。

• **价格与透明性争议**（rustc、jsmo）：rustc 和 jsmo 都提到 Fly.io 的定价不清晰，尤其是 $20/月的服务具体包含哪些功能和限制没有明确说明，令新用户犹豫。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节探讨**（ativzzz、losvedir）：ativzzz 认为该工具的两大创新点是远程代理和与 Fly 的深度集成，并预测未来 AI 将深度嵌入产品中。losvedir 则关心 AI 工具如何管理上下文、模型选择以及如何避免项目规模扩大导致的管理复杂性。

• **LLM 与 Elixir 的兼容性**（CollinEMac、gavmor）：CollinEMac 对社区中关于 LLM 不擅长处理 Elixir 的说法表示怀疑，而 gavmor 则关注是否存在能最大化利用 BEAM 的代理框架，并提到 jido 可能是一个解决方案。

争议焦点：
• **AI 工具是否让编程变得过于简单**：一部分人（如 travisgriggs）认为这种工具掩盖了编程的本质问题，而另一部分人（如 colecut、arrowsmith）则认为它降低了门槛，让更多人能参与开发。
• **价格与服务透明性**：用户对 Fly.io 服务的定价和具体功能不透明表示不满，影响用户的使用意愿。

总结：讨论围绕 Elixir/Phoenix 与 AI 工具的结合展开，支持者认为它降低了开发门槛，带来了新的机会，而批评者则担心这种工具让编程变得更加浮躁，并质疑其性价比和透明性。

Iâm Chris McCord, the creator of Elixirâs Phoenix framework. For the past several months, Iâve been working on a skunkworks project at Fly.io, and itâs time to show it off.
I wanted LLM agents to work just as well with Elixir as they do with Python and JavaScript. Last December, in order to figure out what that was going to take, I started a little weekend project to find out how difficult it would be to build a coding agent in Elixir.
A few weeks later, I had it spitting out working Phoenix applications and driving a full in-browser IDE. I knew this wasn’t going to stay a weekend project.
If you follow me on Twitter, you’ve probably seen me teasing this work as it picked up steam. We’re at a point where we’re pretty serious about this thing, and so it’s time to make a formal introduction.
World, meet
Phoenix.new
, a batteries-included fully-online coding agent tailored to Elixir and Phoenix. I think it’s going to be the fastest way to build collaborative, real-time applications.
Let’s see it in action:
What’s Interesting About Phoenix.new
First, even though it runs entirely in your browser, Phoenix.new gives both you and your agent a root shell, in an ephemeral virtual machine (a
Fly Machine
) that gives our agent loop free rein to install things and run programs  â without any risk of messing up your local machine. You don’t think about any of this; you just open up the VSCode interface, push the shell button, and there you are, on the isolated machine you share with the Phoenix.new agent.
Second, it’s an agent system I built specifically for Phoenix. Phoenix is about real-time collaborative applications, and Phoenix.new knows what that means. To that end, Phoenix.new includes, in both its UI and its agent tools, a full browser. The Phoenix.new agent uses that browser “headlessly” to check its own front-end changes and interact with the app. Because it’s a full browser, instead of trying to iterate on screenshots, the agent sees real page content and JavaScript state â with or without a human present.
What Root Access Gets Us
Agents build software the way you did when you first got started, the way you still do today when you prototype things. They don’t carefully design Docker container layers and they don’t really do release cycles. An agent wants to pop a shell and get its fingernails dirty.
A fully isolated virtual machine means Phoenix.new’s fingernails can get
arbitrarily dirty.
If it wants to add a package to
mix.exs
, it can do that and then run
mix phx.server
or
mix test
and check the output. Sure. Every agent can do that. But if it wants to add an APT package to the base operating system, it can do that too, and make sure it worked. It owns the whole environment.
This offloads a huge amount of tedious, repetitive work.
At his
AI Startup School talk last week
, Andrej Karpathy related his experience of building a restaurant menu visualizer, which takes camera pictures of text menus and transforms all the menu items into pictures. The code, which he vibe-coded with an LLM agent, was the easy part; he had it working in an afternoon. But getting the app online took him a whole week.
With Phoenix.new, I’m taking dead aim at this problem. The apps we produce live in the cloud from the minute they launch. They have private, shareable URLs (we detect anything the agent generates with a bound port and give it a preview URL underneath
phx.run
, with integrated port-forwarding), they integrate with Github, and they inherit all the infrastructure guardrails of Fly.io: hardware virtualization, WireGuard, and isolated networks.
Githubâs
gh
CLI is installed by default. So the agent knows how to clone any repo, or browse issues, and you can even authorize it for internal repositories to get it working with your teamâs existing projects and dependencies.
Full control of the environment also closes the loop between the agent and deployment. When Phoenix.new boots an app, it watches the logs, and tests the application. When an action triggers an error, Phoenix.new notices and gets to work.
Watch It Build In Real Time
Phoenix.new
can interact with web applications the way users do: with a real browser.
The Phoenix.new environment includes a headless Chrome browser that our agent knows how to drive. Prompt it to add a front-end feature to your application, and it won’t just sketch the code out and make sure it compiles and lints. It’ll pull the app up itself and poke at the UI, simultaneously looking at the page content, JavaScript state, and server-side logs.
Phoenix is all about
“live” real-time
interactivity, and gives us seamless live reload. The user interface for Phoenix.new itself includes a live preview of the app being worked on, so you can kick back and watch it build front-end features incrementally. Any other
.phx.run

44328326.article_summary: Chris McCord，Elixir 的 Phoenix 框架创建者，推出了新项目 **Phoenix.new**，这是一个专为 Elixir 和 Phoenix 打造的在线编码代理工具。它运行在一个临时的虚拟机（Fly Machine）中，提供完整的根访问权限，让代理可以自由安装软件包和运行程序，而不会影响本地环境。Phoenix.new 集成了全功能的浏览器和 VSCode 界面，代理可以实时查看和测试前端更改，自动进行实时交互和错误检测。该工具旨在简化应用开发和部署流程，生成的应用程序从一开始就运行在云端，拥有可分享的 URL，并与 GitHub 集成，享受 Fly.io 的基础设施保护。通过 Phoenix.new，开发者可以轻松构建协作式实时应用，减少重复性工作。
